The City should do the following: designate an area on Lantern House property for a 60-day encampment, increase the number of trash receptacles and the frequency with which they are emptied, locate five portable toilets and one hand washing station per 100 people living at the encampment. She noted she has found a local company that would donate the portable toilets and handwashing stations for 60-days. She noted that fires, crimes, and assaults are occurring due to the lack of visible authority and that can be solved by increasing the presence of Ogden Police Department officers through the c01mnunity policing unit. This unit has been assigned in the past to sweep the Municipal Building grounds every 30 minutes to prevent camping and there is no reason they could not be assigned to the encampment as well during the daytime hours. Overnight, the Police Department could schedule one officer to sit in a patrol car at Lantern House. That would cost $12,600 for a 60-day period and she is happy to connect the City to community partners who will aid in funding that in the name of moral decency, public safety, and health. She stated the solutions she has offered will allow the City and its unsheltered residents to get through the next 60 days. She concluded by emphasizing that this is all about housing affordability in the community. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, December 15, 2020 Page 384 C1ystal Yazzie expressed her concern and frustration about what happened at the Lantern House encampment. She is new to the Ogden area, but has been involved in many community programs in the other cities she has lived in, including Salt Lake City. She tried to help many unsheltered people in that community find housing and other resources when law enforcement was utilized to break up encampments. She is upset to see Ogden follow Salt Lake's example even after Operation Rio Grande was proven to be a failure. The residents were given no resources or help. She loves the Ogden community and has been pleased with her interactions with law enforcement and other community members to this point; however, the most recent actions of the City worry her. She asked how much time those living in the encampment were given to leave the area before their homes were broken down and their belongings hauled away. She stated she has personally experienced homelessness and is a recovering addict and she has tried to put herself in the shoes of those who are now in that situation. She would be horrified to be separated from her children or partner and to have her belongings destroyed or taken away. There are many first-time homeless individuals at this time due to the COVID-19 pandemic and she hopes the City will consider taking a different approach and supp01ting those who find themselves in this situation.

column3: stated she is the President of the Ogden branch of the NAACP and the Director of the Project Success Coalition, a non-pr
column4: Betty Sawyer stated she is the President of the Ogden branch of the NAACP and the Director of the Project Success Coalition, a non-profit organization that works with residents of Ogden City who have specific needs. On behalf of the NAACP, she is present to express her disappointment regarding the fashion that the City addressed the encampment of unsheltered residents. That was done in a very inhumane fashion and the timing was terrible. The City has had all year to work with local organizations to collectively develop solutions for these individuals, but it chose to wait until the winter months. She has heard some say that there is an abundance of affordable housing in Ogden, but she is here to say that is definitely not the case. Prices have increased astronomically over the past year, and more so in the midst ofCOVID-19 and racial unjust. The non-profit she serves has been working to provide food and housing support to people who have been impacted by COVID-19 and she can attest that just one out of 18 housing cases she worked on had a rent of less than $1,000 per month. All other rents are upwards of $1,200 to $1,600 for a two-bedroom unit. She stated that is not affordable to most of the working-class residents of Ogden. She wants Ogden City to lead the way in solving these issues in a humane manner. She advised the City to observe the CDC guidelines. She noted that people make choices to live in different ways and that should be respected by the govermnent. She spent the afternoon in Salt Lake City with the Governor to discuss equity, diversity, and inclusion issues. These things should be priorities for Ogden as it works to find a better way to address issues in the community. She noted "what is done to the least ofus, is done to the greater" and Ogden can do better.

column3: stated he is the founder and chairman of two Salt Lake City based organizations: Peaceful Advocates for Native Dialogue
column4: Carl Moore stated he is the founder and chairman of two Salt Lake City based organizations: Peaceful Advocates for Native Dialogue and Organizing Support (PANDOS) and SLC Air Protectors. Both organizations are Native-led entities, and they have the goal of treating everyone equally as human beings and relatives. He is concerned about the treatment of those relatives that have been pushed around in the City. He completely disagrees with the way that Ogden's Police Department was utilized as a Gestapo force that participated in terrorist actions against unsheltered individuals. These people have a right to exist and be free of oppression and the City is acting as if it knows best for people in different situations. Every single fire that burns in the Last Hope Camp has been blessed and consecrated by himself and Vonda Eaglehorse. That means the people have been blessed as well and when the sacred rights afforded to the people there are violated, there will be legal recourse available to them. He said he hopes the City can do things in the right way in the future.

column3: stated that last night she froze for 3 .5 hours straight with several layers of clothing, a coat, gloves, and her hood p
column4: Cassandra Nelson stated that last night she froze for 3 .5 hours straight with several layers of clothing, a coat, gloves, and her hood pulled over her head. Alongside her she had her four-year-old daughter wrapped up and insulated under a makeshift shelter in a warm sleeping bag. She stated her daughter was fine and they may have been seen on the cover of the Standard Examiner this morning as they were photographed participating in a demonstration opposing the displacement of the homeless encampment in the City. One thing she learned during the protest was that within the first two hours, she could not feel some of her toes and she needed more insulation and warmth. Also, every time she needed to use the restroom, she had to cross the street to use facilities at Christmas Village. Everyone hates going outside in the cold, yet the City found it acceptable to destroy the shelter that people had built to keep themselves warm. If crime was the issue leading to the removal of the encampment, she wondered how the City was comfortable dispersing so-called criminals into the community. She has seen a surge ofunsheltered people in downtown Ogden and as a healthcare employee she has witnessed the difficult choices that people are making in the middle of a pandemic. People have been forced to choose between living outside of a shelter or moving into a shelter with COVID-19 positive residents. If the City is worried about hospitals filling up as the virus spreads, she wonders why Administration would not follow the CDC guidelines. Everyone deserves access to a bathroom and sanitary conditions, as well as other resources they may need. Affordable housing does not exist in Ogden as neighborhoods have become more gentrified. So- called affordable housing is not truly affordable as rents continue to increase while wages stay low. It breaks her heait that she is forced to give her daughter experiences like this to teach her empathy when the City leaders should be taking steps to show her. The people that she has helped to feed have now had their shelters destroyed before her eyes. Her daughter has asked her why it is happening and why the people cannot live in an apartment like her. She agreed with Ms. Castillo's suggestion to assign police officers to patrol the area. Policing resources should be available given that other venues have been closed or locked down due to COVID-19. She would argue that they can provide services that are more effective for the community and protective of those who need it the most rather than destroying the only things these individuals have left.

column3: said he had the opportunity to tour the Lantern Houser prior to the pandemic and he was very shocked to learn there is a
column4: Daniel Matthews said he had the opportunity to tour the Lantern Houser prior to the pandemic and he was very shocked to learn there is a lack of actual shelters for those suffering from the housing crisis. Outside of Salt Lake City and Ogden there are few shelters like the Lantern House. This is a ve1y complex issue that many are very passionate about and he would like leaders to lead with empathy and compassion. He stated most of the points he wished to stress have ah'eady been made, but he would truly like to see an increase in transparency at the City Administration level. There appears to be a lack of communication between Administration and the City Council. He feels that the community continues to witness the City Council being caught off guard by decisions that are made by Administration relative to things like recycling and homelessness. Ms. Castillo made several excellent points that he agrees with and he hopes the City will consider making changes as many in the community likely find themselves closer to homelessness than being stable as a result of this pandemic and economic downturn. Those that are most vulnerable should be thought of at time like this. He urged the City to be 'tender with the young, compassionate with the aged, sympathetic with the striving, and tolerant with the weak and wronged'. At some point in each person's life, they will have fulfilled each of their roles. Chair Choberka invited Mayor Caldwell to address the questions that were raised during the public comment period, specifically about the notice that was given to those living at the encampment, what resources were offered to them, and the City's observance of CDC guidelines. Mayor Caldwell stated that those staying at the encampment were given a 24-hour notice of the need to relocate. He noted he has a brother who is an emergency room physician and he recently contracted COVID-19 and is dealing with it on his own at his home; to say that he has no empathy for those who are at risk of contracting COVID-19 is exceedingly unfair. The actions taken by City Administration were for the health and well-being of the community; many people will disagree with that, but he stands behind that belief. Council member Lopez stated he sympathizes with those who spoke, and he understands why they are upset. This is a very difficult issue, and he does not pretend to understand the complexities surrounding it. This is an issue that is present in many other cities across the State, not just Ogden. The City has hired a homelessness advocate and he has had many conversations with her about efforts to provide support and resources to these people. He knows she was involved in this operation and he trusts her judgement, though he wishes that the circumstances were different. He stated he could talk at length about all the conversations he has had with people in the City and at the Police Department as an individual Council member, but he will refrain from doing so as he feels it is important for the Council and Administration to work collectively to do better by the community. He is very proud of the working relationship this City Council has with City Administration. They ask tough questions of one another though the public may not always hear those questions. They work well together, treat each other with respect, and hold each other accountable. While he agrees with many of the sentiments shared tonight by those who spoke during the public cmmnent period, it is important to remember there is always another side to the stmy. He apologized to those who feels he has failed them but reiterated this is a very difficult issue and he will continue to ask questions and work diligently to try to solve these and other problems in the City. Council member Nadolski stated he has had many experiences in this job that have made it clear to him that politics is not for him. The trend in politics and in society is to assume the worse about and demonize one another and he cautioned the community to refrain from that behavior. There are many good people on the City Council and in City Administration. They have good heaits and only want to do good things for the cmmnunity. That does not mean there is no room for disagreement, but he does not believe anyone acted out of a lack of love or empathy. He respects the opinions that have been shared, but he asked that the community try not to jump to conclusions about one another's character as that type of behavior will result in the City being worse off. Council member Stephens referenced the cmmnents made regarding the decision to hold the Ogden Marathon viltually in 2021. He hopes that the GOAL Foundation will continue to evaluate the circumstances surrounding the pandemic to determine if it may be possible to hold the marathon in person as in the past. He then mentioned the topic of homelessness and the efforts to break down the encampment on the Lantern House prope1ty. The processes in place in the City allow for dialogue between the Council and Administration as well as for public input. He agrees with some of the comments that were made and indicated that now is a tune to reflect upon the suggestions that were provided and determine if something different could be done in the future. Chair Choberka stated that duril1g the work session held prior to this meeting, the Council heard from the Police Chief, Deputy Police Chief, Mayor Caldwell, and Chief Adminish·ative Officer Johnson regardil1g the operation to break down the encampment at the Lantern House. She directed the public to listen to the audio recording of that meeting as she feels that answers were provided to some of the questions that were asked tonight. She stated that in her private employment she has worked on this ilnportant community issue for many years and homelessness has only increased as a result of COVID-19 and economic factors. She stated that this is not a new issue for the cmmnunity; it has been happening for a long tune and she has always h·ied to lead from a place of compassion. She does wish that communication were better so that the cmmnunity is not caught by surprise when Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, December 15, 2020 Page 386 something like this happens. She is of the mindset that it is appropriate to try something new if the practices that have been employed and relied upon for years are no longer working. She is concerned that actions taken may not have been in accordance with CDC guiqance and she would be comfmtable considering a budget amendment to reallocate funds that could be used to support homeless individuals as they try to survive the winter months. She noted that last winter,just around the comer from her home, someone died in church doorway on a freezing cold night and she would be willing to engage in conversations aimed at doing things differently relative to supporting and advocating for homeless individuals. She then addressed the comment made during the public comment period regarding a proposal to create a police refmm committee saying that is something that was also suggested in the past and she is aware Administration has assembled a group of individuals from the community to talk about law enforcement issues. Mayor Caldwell said that is correct. That group continues to meet and is willing to continue their efforts to evaluate operations in the Police Department. He reiterated that he takes these issues very serious and he wishes that people understood that he and City Administration were not being insensitive. He has taken advice from professionals in several different areas of expertise and used that information to make decisions. Council Comments Council member Hyer stated that the comments made tonight and, in the days, leading up to this meeting have caused him to be introspective and consider what could have been done differently. In a perfect world, there would be no homeless individuals, but it is very clear, particularly this year, that this is not a perfect world. He understands that the Mayor and Police Department hear complaints about different issues that are occurring throughout the community and they work diligently to try to solve those problems in the most compassionate way. Someone will always believe that the actions taken were wrong, while others believe they were right, but he can attest that the City views homeless individuals as people. While he cannot fully empathize with the situation homeless individuals fmd themselves in because he has never been homeless or been in a situation where he has been outdoors and cold for several days at a time, he does hope that people recognize that the efforts taken were in good faith. He noted that tonight's meeting is the last in 2020 and he looks forward to 2021 with hopes that it maybe a better year. Vice Chair Blair stated he is also looking forward to 2021. He wished those present a happy holiday season and noted that he appreciates the working relationship he has with his fellow Council members and City Administration. He respects each of them and is grateful for the job they perform for the City. He also thanked everyone who has attended Council meetings in an effort to hold City leaders accountable. The comments that have been made tonight and during previous meetings often cause him to look at issues from a different point of view and he appreciates that. He stated he does believe everyone that is working for the City truly cares about the City and doing what is best for the citizens. He is grateful for the Police Chief for his leadership and for his efforts that have resulted in increased safety of the community. He said that when the City Council asks questions of City Administration, they are very responsive, and he believes they are honest in their responses. He agreed there are always issues that need to be addressed and he is willing to continue to work to address those issues. There are many people doing good things in the City, and he respects and is grateful for them. Council member White stated that the issue of homelessness is very complex and there is not one single solution for it, but she appreciates all the input that has been provided and feels the suggestions made tonight may help to improve decision making in the future. She echoed the comments made by other Council members about the fact that the Council does lead with empathy and is constantly thinking of and working on solutions to problems that arise. Hearing from residents is helpful in those efforts. She understands the frustration in the community and asked that the public keep in mind that the Council and City Administration may also be frustrated, but she hopes that eve1yone can continue to work together. She thanked City Administration for everything they do. She concluded by wishing all a happy holiday season. Chair Choberka said that during tonight's work session there was a focus on the support the City receives from the network oflocal social support agencies. Those agencies are serving a great number of people in the community and they could use donations from the public and other businesses interested in improving the situation of the homeless community. She asked that everyone see homeless individuals as humans and as their neighbors and treat them humanely. She concluded by wishing everyone a happy holiday season and noted she is hopeful about the COVID-19 vaccine and the potential it has to improve conditions in 2021. She is relieved that healthcare workers have access to the vaccine at this time and she looks forward to it being available to the public. She is hopeful that the Council may be able to meet in person again in 2021. Council member Lopez stated that he wants the public to know that this City Council truly listens and cares about the public.

column3: stated he would also echo much of the feedback that has been provided tonight. Additionally, he would like to see the Ci
column4: David Timmerman stated he would also echo much of the feedback that has been provided tonight. Additionally, he would like to see the City create a police reform committee. Committees have been created to tackle many other important issues in the community and he would like to see a committee created to address issues that impact many in the City on a daily basis. This committee could try to improvise and fix inadequacies in the Police Department. He has lived in Ogden for six years and while he believes the City works very hard, many leaders and residents have become accustomed to the way that things are and are afraid to speak up on many important issues that need to be addressed. He would love to see the Council take a more active role in these matters, especially relating to policing. He believes the current Police Chief is out of touch and is living in the past. So much has happened in the past year that needs to be actively addressed and the homelessness issue is just one of many. He believes leadership starts at the top and the Chief has taken the City down the wrong path and is not working on issues that impact people every day. He concluded by thanking the Council and urging them to be more open and transparent as every City policy should be publicly available for scrutiny.

column3: stated he appreciates the response to his past comments about the broken link on the City's website regarding the recycl
column4: Heath Satow stated he appreciates the response to his past comments about the broken link on the City's website regarding the recycling program; however, the information found through the link is already not current. He was glad to read in the Standard-Examiner that the recycling program will resume, but this could have taken place eight months ago. Now there are 200 tons of recycling material permanently buried in landfills, but the reinstatement is an improvement. He noted that he has communicated his feelings in the past regarding the way the City manages residents' tax dollars, but tonight he is 'mad as hell'. A community should be judged by how it treats its most vulnerable members and the City utterly failed its most vulnerable members last week. Instead of dealing with the homeless encampment on 33 rd Street humanely, the City chose to do the opposite of what Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidelines and basic human kindness dictate by dispersing the encampment across the City. These human beings were given two options: move into the Lantern House -where there have been over 50 cases of COVID-19 and multiple deaths-'-- or pickup whatever they could carry their arms and hope to survive the coldest night of the year. He asked the Council to think what they would do if faced with that impossible situation. He asked how business owners who now have people camped in front of their businesses should feel. The Mayor has been warned repeatedly that housing has become unaffordable for many in Ogden and that the homeless population would only keep growing. It is necessary to deal with these issues from multiple angles, but the Mayor's response has been that Ogden has too much affordable housing. Mr. Satow stated this is pa1t of a pattern and cited examples relating to the building code, the Swift building, and recycling. All issues that were left unattended until they were emergencies and then presented to the Council for a hasty decision. Now homeless people have been pushed into :freezing weather to die alone or pushed into a potentially deadly facility while the City ignores housing issues. He said he holds the City Council responsible for not holding the Mayor more accountable. That job should not be left to regular citizens and questions asked about this issue by the Council have been entirely without teeth or depth. These issues are more important than Council members' personal relationships with the Mayor. Lives are on the line and the community's morality is in question. He stated that maybe this is really the best the Mayor can do. If that is the case, that is a problem, and the City Council needs to do more to hold him accountable.

column3: stated he learned last week that the GOAL Foundation had decided to do the Ogden Marathon in a virtual fashion. He is co
column4: Jace Langeveld stated he learned last week that the GOAL Foundation had decided to do the Ogden Marathon in a virtual fashion. He is concerned about that decision being made six months in advance of the actual event. He said he understands the number of COVID-19 cases has spiked recently, but he feels this decision is an unoptimistic outlook at this moment. He has heard there are permitting and transportation issues but feels those can be solved if all parties worked together. To make the decision now is very impactful to small business owners in the community as well as race participants. He feels that if the decision were made to hold the marathon in a traditional fashion, this would give the community something to look forward to. It would also send the message - especially to the youth of the community-that Ogden is an optimistic community that will get through the pandemic together.

column3: stated that sweeping camps and destroying people's essential property that they need for survival in the middle of winte
column4: Katherine Crabtree stated that sweeping camps and destroying people's essential property that they need for survival in the middle of winter is not a solution. Now there are more destitute people that are even worse off than before, and she asked how this helps the community. There are a number of legitimate reasons someone may not want to go to a shelter, including not wanting to be separated from their family, COVID-19 concerns, paranoia, distrust of the system, and not wanting to be found with an outstanding warrant. These sweeps do not meet the community where they are at, which is what harm reduction and community should be about. She would rather see money spent investing in facilities, like public bathrooms at the encampments or community workers reaching out to see if needs are being met and offering alternative resources when people are ready to accept them. Unsheltered neighbors should not be seen as a problem, but instead as part of the community. She truly believes the City could provide a very decent basic standard ofli ving if energy were not being expended toward dividing and controlling. She asked how much notice these individuals received about the plans to destroy their homes.

column3: stated he would like to echo many of the thoughts that have been expressed regarding the destruction of the encampment a
column4: Kevin Lundell stated he would like to echo many of the thoughts that have been expressed regarding the destruction of the encampment at the Lantern House property. He understands these are complicated issues, but those are the types of issues the City must approach with compassion and leadership. What he witnessed was the opposite of compassion. These people are members of the community, but they were offered limited options, including moving into a facility where residents have died of COVID-19 or move from the property. This is not a real option and he asked the Council to step into those shoes and decide what they would have done. The City should have followed the CDC guidelines, which indicate the City should not destroy encampments. There are agencies and individuals in the c01mnunity who have worked to build trust with the homeless community and that was broken by the actions of the City. He is disappointed in City Administration and the Police Department, but he is also concerned that the City Council seems to continuously be caught flat-footed by the Administration's actions. The City Council was not made aware that this option was going to take place just as they were not aware that the recycling program was going to be halted. It is ve1y clear there is a lack of communication from the Administration to the Council and he would like for that to be remedied. He would also like for the City Council to speak out on this issue and the fact that it was not humane or handled with compassion.

column3: stated he is a community activist, and he hosted an event last night on Washington Boulevard to bring awareness to the e
column4: Malik Dayo stated he is a community activist, and he hosted an event last night on Washington Boulevard to bring awareness to the embarrassing actions that Ogden City took against the homeless community. He said he wants to understand why the City blatantly violated CDC guidelines, which would have supported keeping the encampment in place. Now there are unsheltered community members dispersed throughout the community, potentially spreading the virus where they were not at risk of doing so previously. He stated that there is a lot of propaganda suggesting that these individuals were offered help before they were told to disperse, but he personally witnessed several people pushing shopping carts in the coldest night of the year looking Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, December 15, 2020 Page 383 for somewhere else to go. These people had no place to go and he cannot imagine what he would do ifhe were in their situation. He suggested that the Mayor and Council try to put themselves in the position of those homeless people who were forced to leave the encampment. All the stereotyping that has been employed in this situation is improper. The City has indicated that many of the homeless individuals are criminals or drug addicts and that is why they choose not to move into the Lantern House. However, that demographic also exists in the suburbs of the community. Even in the wealthiest neighborhoods in the cmmnunity, there are likely people who abuse drugs, even if those are obtained via a prescription. He said that the questions asked of the Police Chief and Mayor during tonight's work session were disappointing and not serious enough. The Council needs to behave in the fashion of past City Councils that were more vocal and held the Mayor accountable. He wondered what the Council is there for if they are only going to ask 'softball' questions of the City's leadership. He is actively working to determine whether those who were displaced have the legal right to sue the City for the harm that was done by these actions.

column3: stated he feels that the City has other options at its disposal. Different policy approaches could be considered, such a
column4: Phelon Atchison stated he feels that the City has other options at its disposal. Different policy approaches could be considered, such as reallocating funding from the Police Department to homeless shelters.

column3: said she agrees with those who have spoken before her and there ai·e many more people in the community who do not have t
column4: Ruby Mercado said she agrees with those who have spoken before her and there ai·e many more people in the community who do not have the time or ability to participate in this meeting and share their thoughts on the issue. She thanked the Council Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, December 15, 2020 Page 385 and the Police Department for the difficult role they fulfill in the community. She echoed the suggestions made by Ms. Castillo and stated she feels if these suggestions were employed, the City would experience some success relative to homelessness. She added that she would also like for the City to consider opening another shelter and take a deeper look into what is happening at the Lantern House and why people have chosen not to stay there. The City could take more time to look into the conditions at the shelter and also evaluate their policies to understand the choices that homeless individuals are facing.

column3: thanked Chair Choberka for her service as Council Chair over the past year and he wished Chair Blair the best ofluck in
column4: David Timmerman thanked Chair Choberka for her service as Council Chair over the past year and he wished Chair Blair the best ofluck in the coming year. He stated that Chair Blair spoke about the importance of government transparency; the lack of transparency at all levels of government is frustrating and he is hopeful that the Council's leadership will pursue increased transparency. He then noted that the Ogden Police Department is one of the most covert public safety agencies he has seen based upon his experience as a fanner officer. He would love for the Department to try to embrace police reform recommendations, particularly as the Department is on the cusp of a new Chief being sworn in. He questioned the selection of the Deputy Chief as the Mayor's recommended appointee for Police Chief as he is unaware of a wide recruitment or selection process. If there is a desire to enact change, it is often necessary to start from the top down; that cannot be done by choosing someone from the inside who has worked his entire career year. The Department needs reform and transparency, and he encouraged the Council to identify priorities that will make that possible. Angel Castillo congratulated Chair Blair and Vice Chair White on being elected to Council leadership positions; she then addressed the unsheltered population in the community. The Lantern House is experiencing challenges related to increased populations as well as an increase in the number of COVID-19 deaths and cases. The City has been aware of these issues as well as the presence of the homeless encampment near the Lantern House and the actions that were taken are in direct defiance of CDC guidelines. At the last Council meeting she recmmnended a solution to the Council that would be in accordance with CDC guidelines; while this is not a fmal solution, it will help the City and the homeless population on a temporary basis. She asked that the Council consider a temporary resolution allowing camping at the Lantern House location until the facility has no active COVID-19 cases or if there is an alternative quarantine option for positive clients. This will help to prevent further deaths, either from COVID-19 or an unhoused individual freezing to death. She reiterated this is not a pennanent solution, but the Council needs to consider opportunities for keeping people safe in the short tenn. There are community partners standing by to assist and the Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, January 5, 2021 Page 16 City will not bear any fmancial burden for what she has proposed. The Council must simply ask themselves if they care and if the answer is yes, they must take action. She concluded by noting the City does not know better than the CDC. Kelly Wallace echoed Angel Castillo's recommendation of a temporary resolution to allow camping atthe Lantern House property until the facility has no active COVID-19 cases. She stated that the Weber School District CTE program has agreed to provide, at no cost to the City, temporary shelters for the homeless community. This would be in the form of Conestoga huts that can be constructed in a short time by few people. They have locking doors and provide a safe, secure shelter for individuals. It is her understanding the Lantern House is willing to have the shelters placed on their property and they will manage the huts and the people staying in them. If a homeless individual has access to a secure structure where they can lock their belongings, they can spend more time looking for a job or other opportunities to better themselves. Kevin Lundell also discussed the breakdown of the homeless encampment. He heard from the City that the actions were based upon the understanding that the Lantern House had available beds, but homeless individuals were not taking advantage of them. He reiterated that the CDC, along with many other agencies, recommend against the destruction of an encampment and disbursement of individuals. Individuals should not be forced to move into a facility that they feel is unsafe during a pandemic; other facilities and businesses have been operating at half-capacity and that is because they are following CDC guidance to reduce the number of people gathering in one place at a time and that same guideline should be observed for homeless shelters. He then urged the Council to follow a resolution that places a moratorium on the destruction of encampments; forcing people outside of their shelter and into the cold is the wrong thing to do. He urged the City to uphold the commitments they originally made to the Lantern House by creating an off-site location for CO VID-19 patients to be quarantined in order to keep the Lantern House safe for those that choose to stay there. Jenny Gnagy echoed the comments made by those who spoke about the homeless encampment; she feels Ogden City needs to work on a long-term solution to the affordable housing problem in the community. Until that is done, the Council should consider the temporary resolution to allow people to camp outside the Lantern House. Audry Martinez echoed the recommendations made by Angel Castillo and she encouraged her to deliver a formal proposal in writing regarding the solution she has suggested. She asked that the Council have a formal discussion about her proposal in a future meeting to give residents the opportunity to understand the basis for decisions regarding these issues. She thanked Ms. Castillo for coming up with a solution to address the matter she complained about.

column3: thanked the Council for adopting the Utah Compact on Racial Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion earlier in the meeting. He
column4: Heath Satow thanked the Council for adopting the Utah Compact on Racial Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion earlier in the meeting. He then noted that tonight he wished to discuss homelessness in the community and he wished that everyone present tonight were as passionate about this issue as they are about drinking establishments in the community. Last time the Council met residents spoke for nearly an hour about the disbursement of homeless individuals as a result of the encampment being broken down; they addressed the fact that this action was in direct opposition to CDC guidelines. Many had questions about how decisions had been made and how to do things differently in the future. After hearing that hour offeedback from the community, Chair Choberka made thoughtful comments that showed she was interested and concerned about what the community had said. A few additional Council members have since spoken with Angel Castillo about the recommendations she made during the meeting and he hopes more will join them after tonight. This is an issue that results in lives being put on the line. At the end of the meeting, Chair Choberka asked Mayor Caldwell if he wished to provide a response about the resources available to those impacted and whether the CDC guidelines were followed. He stated that his frustration is that the Mayor only responded to this issue for four seconds, then spoke about his own family issues for five minutes. His comments were that "every single encampment, and everything else, got a 24-hour notice that they could do that" and the rest of his comments related to how many of his family members have COVID-19. He stated this is why he has been begging the Mayor for months to do more than is required of him to reduce the spread of the infection in the community; however, the Mayor has done literally the opposite of what is recommended in CDC guidelines by dispersing the Lantern House encampment the way he did. The irony is not lost on him that the Mayor is not present tonight as he 'seems to disappear when things get messy'. He asked that the following message be passed ) on to him: "Mayor Caldwell, listen to your community, let them know they have been heard, and respond to them. Now is not the time to be uncommunicative and stuck in the belief that you cannot do better. Please, human lives matter even when they do not add to the tax base; show us you agree those lives matter. You can do better."

column3: thanked the Council for the time and effort that was put into the decision to amend the ordinance regulating the number
column4: Thaine Fischer thanked the Council for the time and effort that was put into the decision to amend the ordinance regulating the number of drinking establishments on a linear block. He stated that Mr. Satow' s comments were hard to follow and he agreed the situation with the homeless encampment is a very difficult one of the City, but he wished to thank staff and the Council for their consideration of his petition. Harvey Day also addressed the homeless encampment near the Lantern House. He stated that he thinks that every member of the Council, every police officer, and every member of City Administration who signed off on the action should be deeply ashamed of themselves; they agreed to it with the knowledge that there was no back up plan and that the breakup was immoral, responsible, and cruel. He thanked the other members of the community who have commented on this outrageous action.

column3: stated she is very excited about what will happen next and she feels it is always possible to do better. Based on the co
column4: Adrienne Andrews stated she is very excited about what will happen next and she feels it is always possible to do better. Based on the comments that have been made tonight by many community members, the Council and Mayor should have a clear understanding that their constituents want to be involved. She congratulated Chief Young and indicated she knows he will do great things. She also thanked the Council for their service and for accepting the input provided tonight. She is committed to continuing to work on behalf of the cmmnunity alongside many others who also believe that working together will make the entire community stronger.

column3: thanked the Council for being willing to listen to the public tonight. It is not always easy to speak truth to power, bu
column4: Angel Castillo thanked the Council for being willing to listen to the public tonight. It is not always easy to speak truth to power, but the adjustments the Council made to allow for that input and consider opportunities for improving future processes are wonderful and she appreciates their efforts. She wholeheartedly agrees with Council member Choberka's comments about her sadness that it was necessary to have this conversation on the same night that Chief Young was being appointed. Everyone supports him and thinks he is a great man that will do a great job, but as Council member Nadolski said, this is the time to talk about it because the bridge of trust between the community and OPD is very shaky. Everyone is trying to do the work to strengthen the bridge and make the community stronger together. She hopes for more transparency in future processes as it is not appropriate to leave a process intact simply because 'that's the way it has always been done'. It is necessary to constantly evaluate and change processes because there is always room for improvement.

column3: thanked the Council for the time they have taken tonight to listen to the voices of the members of the community. It is
column4: Betty Sawyer thanked the Council for the time they have taken tonight to listen to the voices of the members of the community. It is a small gesture that the Council values the time many have taken to be engaged in this process. She considers herself a public servant and the same is true for others who spoke tonight and each of them applaud the service provided by the City Council. She encouraged them to continue to seek out opportunities for improving Ogden. It is important to listen, value, and affirm each individual's humanity in these types of processes.

column3: stated he was deeply shaken by the events of January 6, 2021 at our nation's capital, as he is sure many were. It made h
column4: Heath Satow stated he was deeply shaken by the events of January 6, 2021 at our nation's capital, as he is sure many were. It made him pause to think about what is important. He was recently selected as the artist of a monumental sculpture for a new city hall building in Florida and he shared a quote he used in his presentation for that project. The Japanese writer and poet,

column3: said "Individually, we are one drop. Together, we are the ocean." As this quote implies, the ocean is only collectively
column4: Ryunosuke Satoro said "Individually, we are one drop. Together, we are the ocean." As this quote implies, the ocean is only collectively powerful, a single drop will not change a coastline, but enough drops together can create great change. This concept of the ocean as a collective force is very much part of what a city hall and community represent to him. He stated that he has a lot to say and much of the time it may feel as if he is 'throwing punches', so this week he chose to spend his three minutes saying thanks. He thanked the City Council and noted each of them has a virtually thankless job. They are not paid enough and must absorb the community feedback they receive with patience and a diplomatic smile. They are responsible for making choices and decisions that will impact a lot of people, sometimes for a generation or more. As individuals, they are not given much power in I the strong mayor form of government under which Ogden City operates. This must be exhausting and, even for those he strongly \ disagrees with, he is thankful they are doing this important work. Like them, he cares about the community that is created together. While he may be angry about things that happen in the community, he does appreciate the role each Council member fulfills in the community.

column3: thanked the Council for their time and thoughtful consideration of public comment tonight. To be civically engaged is ve
column4: Taylor Knuth thanked the Council for their time and thoughtful consideration of public comment tonight. To be civically engaged is very taxing and there are many things he would rather be doing on his Tuesday night. However, he chose to be engaged and it is very difficult to get the feeling- time and time again- that he is 'screaming into the wind' and that his message is being ignored. He stated that he was insulted by Council member Hyer' s comments, which he found to be very rude, because engagement at any level of any kind should be valued regardless of the quantity or quality. The fact that dozens of community members chose to engage in the process tonight and were dismissed is very discouraging. He asked why anyone would make comments to discourage public involvement. He reiterated that his comments earlier in the meeting were never aboutthe product, but the process that was followed to select a new chief of police. This is a process that has been commented on many times and one that creates distrust in the community, especially those communities that the Diversity Commission is tasked to support. He \ stated that elected officials should take a pause to ask themselves why they are doing this job and who they are doing the job for. The community will be discouraged if they are constantly dismissed by those elected to serve them. Malil< Dayo stated he is the president ofEl Comite Social Justice Movement and echoed the comments made about the importance of continuing the dialogue about improving things in the community. He said one issue that has not been discussed Minutes of Special Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, January 12, 2021 Page 29 tonight is the threat of domestic terrorism in all 50 state capitols and local government buildings on Inauguration Day and he asked what steps Ogden City has taken to ensure that its public safety has not been infiltrated by extremist ideologies and to be sure there is a plan in place to combat the threat if it arises. He concluded by congratulating Chief Young and noted he looks forward to working with him in the future.

column3: stated in March of2020 she made a motion as Planning Commissioner intended to get the City Council's attention about the
column4: Angel Castillo stated in March of2020 she made a motion as Planning Commissioner intended to get the City Council's attention about the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) projects aimed at the Marshall White Center; this ultimately ended up costing her her position on the Planning Commission, but it was worth it as the Council ultimately allocated $300,000 for a feasibility study for the Center. She thanked the Council for their attention to that matter over the past year. She stated she has not missed a City Council meeting or work session in over two years, but she has not heard the fmdings of the feasibility study; she asked who is managing the project on the Council's behalf and when their fmdings will be presented to the Council. She then stated that Council staff does a great job at managing virtual meetings and making sure that the Council is accessible to the public, but she looks forward to the opportunity to join City Council meetings in person in the near future. However, she believes many people enjoy the ability to participate electronically and given that so many important matters are discussed during a Council work session, she would like for the City Council to make the effort to broadcast and/or record those meetings and make them publicly available.

column3: thanked the Council for the heartfelt discussion they participated in last week; it was a meaningful experience for the
column4: Heath Satow thanked the Council for the heartfelt discussion they participated in last week; it was a meaningful experience for the residents who were in attendance. He thanked the Mayor for being present tonight as he is not required to attend; he was not present the week before last when there was an intense discussion about actions to break up homeless encampments in direct opposition to Centers for Disease Control (CDC) guidelines. He stated he will repeat his comments from that meeting since he feels the Mayor needs to hear it; members of the community spoke for nearly an hour about their concerns about how the encampment on the Lantern House property was dispersed. After that hour of impassioned speeches, the Mayor responded to these concerns for four seconds- he said only "every single encampment and everything else got a 24-hour notice so they could do that". He stated that is not a cogent response; the Mayor then went on about his personal life for another five minutes. He recommended the Mayor go back and watch himself on the videos of the meetings, especially for the meeting of January 5, 2021 as it was incredibly tone deaf. He stated the Mayor never addressed the concerns raised by the community and he still owes a proper response. He noted Chief Administrative Officer Johnson tried harder the following week, but it was still lacking and, ultimately, it is not his poor decision to defend. Again, just last week many residents spoke about the process to select a new police chief; they were concerned about the secrecy of the process. Many Council members spoke at length and from the heart regarding this issue and the Mayor spoke to these concerns for five seconds this time, saying "if we need to talk about the process and how that works, we can do that". He stated he has tried to say this in many ways, but it is not getting through: Mayor Caldwell should listen to the community, the City Council, and let everyone know they have been heard. Now is not the time to be uncommunicative and seemingly stuck in the belief that one cannot be enlightened. If the Mayor does not feel that way, he is doing a terrible job ofletting the City know he cares; he cannot just say that he appreciates comments and leave it at that. He is not saying the Mayor is a bad person or does not care, but he is providing no evidence to the contrary when his responses are so short. He then concluded by noting he would like an update regarding the status of the City's recycling program. Council member Choberka stated that she does not have an update on the feasibility study for the Marshall White Center, but she is aware that the advisory board has been meeting regarding needs of the facility. Chair Blair then noted that he is not aware of a plan for the timing of resuming in-person meetings and whether virtual participation will still be allowed after that occurs; however, he will discuss the matter with Council staff and report back. Council member Lopez stated that he supports Ms. Castillo's recommendation to stream and record work session meetings as soon as possible. Council Executive Director Eller-Smith reported that a camera was recently installed in the work session room, which now makes it possible to stream meetings. She stated that Council staff has discussed the future format of Council meetings and believes that a hybrid of in-person/virtual meetings would be favored by the public. She stated a formal recommendation will be ) made to the Council soon. She then noted that the audio of all work session meetings has always been recorded and maintained, but Council staff will continue to pursue a video broadcast of the meetings. Council member Choberka stated that will be very helpful to the public as many important discussions take place during work session meetings and it will be nice to refer constituents to a video recording of those discussions. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, January 19, 2021 Page 41

column3: thanked the Council for their service. He then stated that at the previous meeting he spoke about the appointment of a n
column4: David Timmerman thanked the Council for their service. He then stated that at the previous meeting he spoke about the appointment of a new police chief and what the ramifications would be if a majority of the Council chose not to support the Mayor's recommended appointee. He stated he would still like an answer to that question.

column3: addressed comments made by the Mayor at the conclusion of the last Council meeting and noted he fmds it sad that the May
column4: Heath Satow addressed comments made by the Mayor at the conclusion of the last Council meeting and noted he fmds it sad that the Mayor deems actions taken to hold him accountable every four years as 'bullying'; the people of Ogden have recently asked many questions and the Mayor has spent just four seconds speaking to those questions. The Mayor is being asked to answer to a community that he was sworn to serve. Mr. Satow indicated he will not be shamed into being quiet and he will be present every week to ask these questions; when the Mayor refuses to answer those questions, it looks as ifhe is hiding something or just woefully uninformed about those doing the work beneath them. He then stated that he would like to hear answers from those who know the answers on the following topics: recycling and homeless encampments. In terms of recycling, the citizens were lied to ) and much information was hidden. Even the Sustainability Committee did not know what was happening and the Administration's actions make it clear that Committee was created for appearances only, similarly to the Planning Commission and Diversity Commission. The Mayor has made one thing clear, if you step out the bounds ofbeing more than a rubber stamp to him, you will be punished by being kicked off that committee. The recycling issue was hidden from the public until exposed by a newspaper article and recycling was dumped in the landfill for the better part of a year; someone needs to answer for this negligence since the Mayor refuses to. Relative to the removal of an encampment at the Lantern House, he would like to know what City Administration is doing to prevent another similar crisis in the future. Last year, home prices increased a record 9.1 percent and the rate was even higher in Ogden; homelessness will not go away if it is ignored, as the Administration seems to be doing, and it is not an option to sweep human beings under the rug using the police force as a maid service. He concluded he knows that being a Council member is a part time job and that is why it is up to citizens to look into these issues and bring them to the Council. Chair Blair asked that someone address Mr. Timmerman's question. Council Executive Director Eller-Smith indicated she will research that matter and report back.

column3: stated last week the Mayor spent almost as long insulting him as he spent responding to hours of citizens expressing the
column4: Heath Satow stated last week the Mayor spent almost as long insulting him as he spent responding to hours of citizens expressing their unease regarding how homelessness issues and the selection of anew police chief was handled by Ogden City. He is not here to draw the focus of the Mayor; rather, he is asking that the concerns that have been expressed be responded to in a meaningful way. The Mayor referred to these concerns from the public as "recreational outrage", but he assured the Mayor that the outrage in the community is far from "recreational". He noted the Mayor even spent time berating the members of the Council for their own concerns about the police chief selection process; at no point did he ever spend a moment answering any of the public or Council's concerns. The concerns about the selection process are not about the individual selected for the position, but about the selection process that left the public in the dark. Last Thursday he attended a virtual community conversation, in which Chief Young participated, and he was happy to see him speak openly and knowledgably when answering questions from the public. It was refreshing when compared to what he has been getting from the Mayor. He then stated he has emailed the Mayor and Council about unanswered questions regarding the City's recycling program; the City Attorney was tasked with responding to the email and he put 100 percent of the blame. on the recycling company that the City works with. He also communicated that the City's Sustainability Committee was not entitled to receive infonnation about the issue because it was a legal matter. He is left guessing nobody told the City Attorney that the City has claimed a hold-up was due to the City exploring different recycling technology, because he did not raise that in his email. He addressed the Council directly and asked why the City's Sustainability Committee was never informed the City was encountering issues in the recycling program and if anything has been done to make sure the line of communication between the Committee and Administration will be more open in the future. Also, if the City is actually looking into new technology, that is a perfect example of the type of issue that should be referred to the Committee for a recmmnendation. He added it appears the solution the City has arrived at- the extension of a conditional use permit (CUP) for Recycled Earth- could have been implemented several months ago. He asked if the delay was truly due to exploration of new technology or problems with Recycled Earth. He stated that the third matter is the City's failure to tell its citizens that recycling ) materials were being taken to a landfill; this is as good as lying to the public and he asked why that happened. The public trust has been hanned over this issue and he feels the community deserves better answers rather than the attitude that has been displayed by leadership. Even if the answer is a simple one, the public is owed an explanation and/or apology for the failure to address the problem in a timelier marmer. He stated he will continue to follow up with a request for answers if they are not provided tonight. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, February 2, 2021 Page 56 Angel Castillo referenced the honorary street name designation on 2"d Street, which was discussed during tonight's work session meeting; the honorary name would be Bingham Fort Lane. She read excerpts from the Utah Compact on Racial Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion, which the City Council opted to support: "We view racism as more than just an individual character flaw. It is a system of ideas, beliefs, practices, structures, and policies that give some people greater opportunity to be fully human and live a happier and healthier life than others. Umaveling centuries of internalized and systemic racism requires bold anti-racist actions and policies right now. We likewise pledge to foster cultures of inclusion in every aspect of our organizations and society while addressing social injustice and inequality, and condemning all forms of prejudice, bigotry, and discrimination. We further recognize that we must listen and learn from each other, realizing that as we deepen our understanding of differences, we can, in turn, be better understood. Therefore, we commit to, and invite other Utahns to commit to, these anti-racist principles and actions .. .4. Engagement- we engage to effect change. Broader engagement, equitable representation, and deeper connection across social, cultural, and racial lines will uphold the principle- "nothing about us, without us." 5. Movement, not a moment- Utahns unite behind a common goal to create equal opportunity. We affirm our commitment will not just be a passing moment, but a legacy movement of social, racial and economic justice." She stated that the City's Diversity Commission provided direction to the Council as to why the honorary street name designation is not inclusive. She reiterated the City Council signed on to the Compact; just because they do not understand something does not make an action correct and the Council has an opportunity to do better at this point in time. Either the Council fully supports the Diversity Commission's direct experience on a world view that is not the same as theirs, or they believe the Commission is about optics and are in place to allow the City to simply 'check a box'. Either the Council fully supports the Racial Compact or their action was for show and they have no intention oflearning why the proposed street naming is problematic in its current form. When the actual standing Shaman of the Shoshone Nation tells the Council the potential harm that could be done by the historic street name designation, the Council needs to listen. She stated the nation's history is not pretty and our ancestors did the best they could with the tools they had. There are now different tools available, and the Council can do better; she stated they must vote to deny the petition.

column3: stated he has been tuning in to the City Council meetings via podcast and he appreciates the effort of staff to produce
column4: Kevin Lundell stated he has been tuning in to the City Council meetings via podcast and he appreciates the effort of staff to produce a podcast and give residents the ability to tune in at their convenience and understand what is happening in the City. He stated he was a bit frustrated at the end of the last meeting with one of the Mayor's comments; after many constituents spoke about the lack of transparency in the process of fmding a new police chief. He stated he believes ChiefYoung will do well for the City and he is not concerned about his appointment, but there are concerns about the process. In speaking to the comments, the Mayor stated he found it "disheartening that people wanted to make a political platform out of that." He stated he would like to know who was speaking to in that moment and what he was speaking about. He stated that after a summer of civic umest at the intersection of racism and police violence, one of the biggest decisions the City could make is who should be appointed as police chief and the fact that citizens and some members of City Council would have liked for that process to be more transparent is not a matter of political platforming. He stated he personally knows that the concerns expressed were not about political platforming; he has had conversations with activists in the community who care deeply about this issue and they simply wanted a seat at the table at this moment in history. He stated that desire was warranted and for that to be reduced to a claim of political platforming was very unfortunate. He added that the back and forth between Mr. Satow and the Mayor is not something that Mr. Satow would defme as fun; he and many others do not consider their interest in the City to be recreational and he feels that a respectful response is appropriate. Chair Blair invited any member of the Council to respond to public comments. Vice Chair White stated that she truly appreciates the comments made by constituents, but what they need to realize is that the City is a good City, and this is a good Council because of differing views. Each Tuesday the Council is willing to engage in open dialogue and it can be very difficult sometimes to be forthright and display their moral compass in public. She stated that the views of each Council member may be different, but that is what makes them better and stronger as a body. She understands that constituents may have different views as well, but she is pleased that the Council is being open and transparent. She hopes that no member of the Council fears expressing their own opinion just because there may be a different sentiment in the community. She does not want the Council to stop having hard conversations and open dialogue; they are addressing very difficult issues on a weekly basis and it is vital that open channels of communication be maintained. Council member Hyer stated that he is not a member of Ogden City Administration and is not aware of every issue surrounding the recycling program, but as a member of the Weber Area Council of Governments (WACOG), he was aware that the City was investigating new technology aimed at improving the City's recycling program and he has spoken about that in the past. He stated that the answer to Mr. Satow's question about whether the City was investigating new technology or if the problem was solely the responsibility of the service provider is not easy to answer because both things could have been occurring. He stated that the petitioner needed to make the petition they did to trigger Planning Commission review of their operations and ensure compliance with the conditional use permit. He stated that as a Council member he is very excited about the new technology and he hopes the City will move toward it; it has not been ruled out and it is his understanding that Administration is waiting for the opportunity to make site visits and become familiar with it. Until that is done, it is difficult to send anything to the Sustainability Committee for a recommendation. Council member Choberka echoed Council member Hyer' s comments; sometimes there are many different truths in one situation and sometimes Council members are informed at different times about different elements of an issue. Sometimes it is her personal desire for matters to be handled differently or at a quicker pace, but she is not always aware of all factors, especially legal Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, February 2, 2021 Page 57 factors. She stated she understands how this can be frustrating for constituents and could lead them to feel that there is a lack of \ transparency. However, she feels that the Council is very aware of the importance of transparency and they strive to be as J transparent as possible. Council member Nadolski commented on the term 'recreational rage', which has been uttered tonight and in the past meeting. He stated in his experience, most people do not start out being mad. There are many people who reach out wanting to be involved in a constructive way, but when they are ignored, they are left with little choice but to become enraged. He stated that is why he has spoken out so forcefully about the process the City used to select a new police chief; it is not that he does not believe that the right person was selected, but because there are many people who have asked for an opportunity to be involved or provide input and they were totally ignored. That is frustrating to him and he understands that has led them to be very upset. He stated that each Council member does have a voice and opinion and it is his opinion that the City should listen to people in order to truly provide for and service them; if that is done, there will be fewer enraged people. Just because people are mad does not mean they are not important, and he hopes the Council will always do their best to listen to people. Council member Lopez thanked Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper for following up on a request he had about a business owner on Wall A venue who was seeking assistance from the City. He then noted he forwarded an email to the entire Council and Administration from a woman who was looking for assistance from the City relative to drug use and burglaries happening in her home. He would like to hear if Administration has had the opportunity to follow up on that email. Council member Choberka stated she saw an email and advertisement on the City's social media channels about a public survey regarding the Marshall White Center; she encouraged all residents to look at that survey and provide their feedback regarding their desires for a recreation center in the community.

column3: stated he would like to know the plans for the property Ogden City purchased in Ogden Canyon, a 71.29-acre parcel, parce
column4: Edward Mackner stated he would like to know the plans for the property Ogden City purchased in Ogden Canyon, a 71.29-acre parcel, parcel number 13-075-0002. Additionally, the City purchased a rock home above the Lewis Camp, parcel number 13-075-0017. The properties are worth about $1 million and he would like to understand the City's plan for future use of the properties.

column3: stated she will talk to the Council tonight about an issue she has been raising for the past several years: housing affo
column4: Angel Castillo stated she will talk to the Council tonight about an issue she has been raising for the past several years: housing affordability. In October of2020, the Council had a discussion about the issue and acknowledged there was a problem; Council member White indicated she would like to look into housing affordability issues that are specific to Ogden rather than the metropolitan area around Ogden. She noted Council member White has spoken with experts in this field and was told that Ogden has a shortage of2,205 affordable rental units, and 3,160 affordable and available units. She asked what the Council is going to do about the issue. During the October 2020 meeting, Council member Nadolski was adamant that he wanted to begin working on the issue. The City has access to experts in this area and she advised them to utilize those experts; they have current information and can help to implement tangible goals. She noted that this morning Mayor Caldwell participated in a press conference during which Governor Cox indicated the entire State of Utah has a housing affordability problem. She noted Mayor Caldwell has gone on record to indicate that Ogden has a surplus of affordable housing, but that is based on Ogden metropolitan data, which includes cities surrounding Ogden. She asked what the City Council is going to do about the issue; they have talked about it a great deal, but it is time to begin working on a plan that will address opportunities for increasing availability of different types ofhousing in the City. There are some great programs that the City is already employing, butthey will not solve all of the issues in the City, and it is time to take the next step in working to get things done.

column3: stated he would like to know the process to request the creation of a new committee that would work on justice and polic
column4: David Timmerman stated he would like to know the process to request the creation of a new committee that would work on justice and police reform in the City. He is interested in participating on or at least establishing such a committee; he feels the time is right to address these important issues. It is important to evaluate how police are deployed and what responsibilities they have to the community. He noted that the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) convenes in a closed session later tonight and there are a few items that can be discussed in a closed meeting that are important to him: deploying security personnel and using updated crime detention techniques. He noted Ogden has a real time crime center, which can be a boon to the community, but he is concerned there are no 'guard rails' limiting the activity of that group. Any time there is a lack of supervision or specific guidelines, the results can be a serious violation of constitutional rights by the City's men and women in blue. He noted he supports the Police Department strongly but given the current climate it is important to monitor and record activities to avoid violations. Sometimes it is necessary to evaluate the point of certain programs or processes, determine if dollars are being spent wisely, and if there is enough supervision to ensure public safety officials are doing the right thing. He then noted that South Ogden City has an officer who was involved in a fatal shooting; that man was not disciplined, took his fifth amendment rights, and is back in service working for that entity. However, he probably should have been terminated due to his lack of cooperation in the investigation ofthe shooting.

column3: stated that he is looking forward to the day that Ogden City might have its first female Mayor. He then noted that durin
column4: Heath Satow stated that he is looking forward to the day that Ogden City might have its first female Mayor. He then noted that during the last meeting he asked for the appraisal that was used to detennine the sales price of the Brown's Ice Cream Building and Council Executive Director Eller-Smith was helpful in getting that docmnent to him quickly. His concern is about the City's action, not its buyer or broker. The City Council approved the sale, but City Administration may have misled them about some details. What was sent to him was not an appraisal, but instead was a broker's estimate that was broughtto the City by the buyer, according to City Administration. During the December 10,2019, the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) Board heard a presentation from City Administration that indicated "the buyer provided a commercial prope1ty estimate of value similar to a .\ formal appraisal". He stated that any person employed in the real estate field will say that an estimate from a buyer's broker is / nothing close to a fonnal appraisal from an unbiased appraiser. The price the City accepted was based upon an estimated value per square foot multiplied by 5,808 square feet and that size seemed entirely wrong to him, so he spent 10 minutes measuring the building itself; the first floor alone is at least 5,800 square feet and the second floor is 4,500 square feet. He noted buildings down the street from the old Brown's Ice Cream building are selling for $120 to $200 per square foot these days, but even at the low Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, February 23, 2021 Page 74 valuation of $55.50 per square foot, the upper floor is worth over $250,000, but was not included in the price. He noted Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper told the RDA Board that the City enlisted a commercial real estate broker to list the building for sale and that the buyer made an offer within a month. Mr. Satow noted he cannot fmd a listing for the property on the market listing service (MLS), which is the first place a broker typically lists a property, and he wondered if the property was actually ever listed for sale. He stated that he would love to go to a car dealership and tell them he will buy a car based upon what his friends have told him is the value of that car, but that is not how things work in the real world. He stated he simply wants to know if the property that taxpayers owned was sold using any system beyond just trusting what City Administration says. He stated he does not have enough information yet to say exactly what happened in this situation, but none of the explanations he can imagine are acceptable and he asked for the Council to assist him in getting more information. He asked if an actual unbiased appraisal was ever ordered for the property and, if not, why it was not. He also asked who determined the square footage measurements that were used to determine the building's value. He asked who the City's broker was, where they listed the property for sale, and the total number of offers the City received.

column3: stated he listened to the podcast oflast week's work session meeting and he thanked the City employees who make the podc
column4: Kevin Lundell stated he listened to the podcast oflast week's work session meeting and he thanked the City employees who make the podcast happen. He has a few questions about the City's utility study and plans to increase certain utility fees; he polled four of his friends to determine if they have ever paid a late fee on their water bill and all of them told him yes because of the difficulty in signing up for the City's auto pay service. He stated he hopes the new utility billing system will simplify this process and help residents avoid paying late fees. He understands the arguments to change the City's billing system in a manner that will bring it in line with industry standards, but in terms of late fees, if those fees are not expected to result in a noticeable revenue increase, there is no reason to implement them. Those who are most penalized by late fees are those that are on a fixed income; these accelerated late fees could be very detrimental to people in that situation, and he asked that the Council consider all of the unintended consequences of the proposal. He also asked them to consider if the current system is 'broken' and in need of fixing.

column3: stated she has questions about the status of the Marshall White Center; she is aware that the community survey period en
column4: Angel Castillo stated she has questions about the status of the Marshall White Center; she is aware that the community survey period ended last weekend, but she wants to know what type of engineering study has been performed by City Administration. She understood it would take six months to complete engineering studies, but she has not heard an update on that work.
