She also asked if there is a working agreement with the Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA) for their $10 million recreation center; in past discussions, it was communicated that soft-fundraising activities would be underway at this time and she asked what decisions have been made. She asked if the Council has been provided with infonnation about a potential agreement with the YMCA. The pool at the Marshall White Center has been out of commission for three years and the community wants answers about what will be done to improve the facility. Chair Blair invited Council members to address questions that were raised. Council member Choberka addressed Mr. Satow; she noted she received his email and talked to him over the weekend, and she agrees that the process regarding property acquisition by the RDA needs to be more transparent. She then noted she is unsure of public input policies for the Sustainability Committee and indicated she will follow up on that matter. Finally, like Ms. Castillo, she also looks forward to receiving updated infonnation regarding the Marshall White Center. Council member Nadolski addressed Ms. Castillo's comments and asked that Council staff research the issue and provide the Council with an update. He deferred to Administration to respond to Mr. Satow's comments. He noted he will continue to review the details of what Administration provides and he feels that Mr. Cooper has been fmihcoming with facts and details regarding Agency activities. Council member Stephens agreed and stated that he trusts Mr. Cooper will provide the information Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, March 2, 2021 Page 84 needed to make important decisions for the future of Ogden. He added that the Marshall White Center issue is very important and there are still meetings underway regarding any partnering relationship with the YMCA; the City is exploring many options for \. providing community recreation opportunities to the community. Council member Lopez stated he would like to hear the answers to Mr. Satow's questions regarding the Brown's Ice Cream Building. He also looks forward to updated infonnation regarding the Marshall White Center; he has been asking for information regarding future plans for providing a quality community recreation center for the past five years. Chair Blair echoed Council member Stephen's comments about ongoing discussions between the City and the YMCA regarding a potential YMCA project in the community. Progress may not be moving at the pace desired by the community, but it is moving forward. Council member Lopez stated he appreciates what the YMCA is doing, but he desires stronger leadership from the City in terms of improving the Marshall White Center for an underserved area of the community.

column3: stated she is a new community member and is a graduate student in the environmental sociology department at Utah State U
column4: Gina McCracken stated she is a new community member and is a graduate student in the environmental sociology department at Utah State University; she decided to live in Ogden after visiting the community. She reached out to the Council last week to inquire about any climate action plans in the community and she was forwarded an agenda for the Sustainability Committee. She was told they only take public comment every once in a while, with no clear rules as to when it will be accepted. She stated she would like to suggest that the Sustainability Committee take public comment at every meeting and to allow for some form of dialogue; it is critically important for community members to partake in decision making around environmental issues. She then asked what the community is doing in regard to enviromnentaljustice; the climate crisis is impacting people of color and of marginalized identities the most and she wants to be sure that voices of those communities are amplified in discussions about climate action. Without the public comment period in Sustainability Committee meetings, this is not being done. It is her general assumption that those in office at the local or state level are not representative of the identities that she has spoken of. She stressed that it is important to allow for community members to be part of the decision-making process in regard to climate change; she believes if that were the case, the community would have more rigorous climate action goals. She asked if any member of the Council is on the Committee or in contact with those on the Committee; she also asked that her comments be relayed to the leadership of that Committee.

column3: stated it has been over a month and he still has not received answers to the questions he asked about the real estate tr
column4: Heath Satow stated it has been over a month and he still has not received answers to the questions he asked about the real estate transaction regarding the Brown Ice Cream building. This week he would like to ask which Council members have followed up on his questions with City Administration and if they have any answers tonight. The only Council member to contact him about this issue had no answers to share with him. He is only asking for accountability and honest answers should come quickly; the length oftime it has taken to answer these simple questions is only making him more suspicious that something is very wrong. He asked why it would take more than a month to come up with the truth and he indicated he will ask his questions for the third or fourth time now: where are the listings that a broker would have created if he was actually working for the City and not the buyer; why did Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper tell the Council the broker was listing the building in all the usual places; was Mr. Cooper misled or was he misleading the Council; do any of the Council members truly believe the broker, whose professional career is evaluating, appraising, buying, and selling property botched the size of the building by over 50 percent and that Mr. Cooper did not know the real size of the building he was working to redevelop. He stated it is Mr. Cooper's job to understand and evaluate commercial properties so that the Council does not have to. He asked how the professional broker and Mr. Cooper got the valuation of the building so wrong and if there is any accountability for this failure. He stated these questions matter as this action resulted in hundreds of thousands of taxpayer dollars being thrown away on this project, and potentially millions more on other projects where selection processes are just as opaque. He asked why there is a competitive bidding process for smaller projects, but not for a multi-million development; the system is wide open for corruption and he is not getting any answers that make him feel more comfortable about it. There is one question the entire Council should be able to answer right now; based on false data Mr. Cooper gave the Council regarding the value of the building, he asked the Council if their decision to sell the building was influenced by the valuation. He stated that not one member of the Council has answered this question and he asked if that is because they are embarrassed, they were misled; the residents are left with the appearance that no one really cares that they were lied to and he refused to believe that is true. The citizens need the Council to have the courage to seek the truth, even if it makes them uncomfortable. He understands that some property discussions are private, but the Council needs to acknowledge that they have heard his questions and that they share his concerns. At the very least the Council needs to tell him they are working on the issue and when they will have answers for him; the Council needs to demand these answers from City Administration before any more movement is made on developing the property. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, March 16, 2021 Page 99 Administration Comments Chief Administrative Officer Johnson congratulated the Weber State University football team on a successful season; he also congratulated the school's cross-country team on their participation in the national championship in Oklahoma, in which they performed very well.

column3: thanked the Council for taking the time and making the effort to recognize Awesome Autistic Ogden; she referenced the st
column4: Angel Castillo thanked the Council for taking the time and making the effort to recognize Awesome Autistic Ogden; she referenced the story relayed by Council member Nadolski about his experience with the Ogden Police Department and their interaction with neuro atypical child. The officer involved in that situation is a very experienced officer, but one thing that the City's salary survey has uncovered is that the City is losing experienced officers to other cities and jurisdictions. The City's starting wage for an officer is $18.80 while Weber County pays $20.53, and Salt Lake City pay $21.00. Both Weber County and Salt Lake City offer a $5,000 lateral bonus for new hires. During the work session there was mention of an adjustment to employee wages based upon the lower cost ofliving in Ogden and she asked that the Council reach out for hard data about where officers actually live because it is her understanding that only five percent of the City's police officers live in Ogden. It is very important to retain the talent in which the City has invested so heavily and ensure that amazing men and women make up the City's police force. She encouraged the City Council to take a different approach and try to understand all the reasons that officers are leaving for other agencies.

column3: stated he stands in support of preserving and maintaining the Marshall White Center as a beacon and symbol of an ongoing
column4: Dr. Crawford stated he stands in support of preserving and maintaining the Marshall White Center as a beacon and symbol of an ongoing legacy; not only to honor Marshall White, but also to honor the activities that take place at the facility. A number of community-based meetings are held at the facility, which is a centerpiece of youth growth and development in the community. He asked that the Council carefully consider the value the center has brought to the community; it is a place where many can develop important attributes and talents, but more important to him is that the Center is an investment in human capital. This investment underscores the value placed on youth in the community and allowing for the advancement of leadership.

column3: stated that a few weeks ago Council member Nadolski made the comment that most people who reach out to the City "don't s
column4: Heath Satow stated that a few weeks ago Council member Nadolski made the comment that most people who reach out to the City "don't start out mad; lots of people reach out and want to engage but when they are ignored, we leave them with little Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, March 23, 2021 Page 110 choice but to become enraged". He stated that Chief Administrative Officer Johnson, in representation of City Administration during the last City Council meeting, refused to address a single question he asked last week, and he chose, instead, to talk about college football. He stated he is being ignored; when the entire Council comments that they have heard the answers to his questions, yet they have not reached out to him to relay the answers, he is being ignored. He is angry. He stated the Council all agreed that the Brown Ice Cream building should be placed on the historic register, but since he began raising his concerns many have commented that they feel the building should be tom down. Aside from all of the other questions he has asked that have remained unanswered, he would now like to know who put the idea in their heads that one of the few salvageable historic buildings left in downtown Ogden is no longer worth saving. He stated this is an idea that just came forward in the last few weeks and tonight he would like to know the name of the individual who first voiced that idea. He is hoping it is not the broker who does not know how large the building is or the developer who also didn't know the size of the building; he is also hoping it did not come from Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper who, in addition to not knowing the size of the building, falsely told the Council that the building was being publicly marketed, among other contradictions. He asked the Council if they care that they are being misinformed. Someone told him last week that Mr. Cooper had already answered all of his questions, but that is a lie. Mr. Cooper also told the Council he will gladly answer any questions, but that is also false as Mr. Cooper will not respond to him. He has emailed his questions to Mr. Cooper and the entire Council multiple times and has not received a response. He then noted last week Council member Hyer condescendingly indicated that he does not know how Redevelopment Agency's operate and that is false; Council member Hyer suggested that he is asking the wrong questions and that is also incorrect. He stated he has told the Council that an employee of the City responsible for making choices that involve hundreds of millions of dollars is giving the Council false information, that is not a wrong question. He stated that if the Council has the answers to his questions, they should publicly answer them tonight; he would like to hear the answers rather than talk of college football and if no one is hiding anything, providing the answers should be easy. Ifthe building is tom down without multiple developers being given the chance to look at it first, the Council will have failed at their job. He stated he can provide a list of interested developers that are capable of handling the project; he will gladly do the job the broker should have done. Accountability requires transparency, not just blind trust when it comes to government and multi-million-dollar deals. He encouraged the Council to be transparent.

column3: stated she wished to speak about a matter discussed in tonight's work session relating to housing in the community; she
column4: Angel Castillo stated she wished to speak about a matter discussed in tonight's work session relating to housing in the community; she is very disappointed that the person in charge of development in the City is not familiar with Housing and Urban Development (HUD) standards. There is a specific standard that was updated in October of20 19 relating to housing affordability and Community and Economic Development Director Christopulos is unfamiliar with that standard. The answer to housing affordability issues, which other communities are aware of, is to allow condominiums, townhomes, and tiny homes; these types of housing units are typically a smaller footprint and, therefore, the cost is lower. HUD changed their standards to make home ownership easier because this is the fastest way for someone to achieve fmancial independence and security; they expanded their allowances to new or existing condominiums. HUD standard 4,000.1 provides information on how to get HUD approval of existing condos or the construction of new condos. She stated that the City needs to start doing things differently and more creatively to address housing affordability issues, which will only worsen. The City Council, especially Vice Chair White, have repeatedly stressed the need for a housing plan and that still has not come to fruition. The City needs housing of all types: high- end, moderate, and low-income homes and she encouraged them to develop a plan that will provide solutions for developing an inventory of all housing types and something other than the standard single-family home. This will help residents to pursue opportunities for building equity and credit through home ownership.

column3: thanked Council member Lopez for the questions he asked during tonight's work session regarding housing; he hopes that t
column4: Heath Satow thanked Council member Lopez for the questions he asked during tonight's work session regarding housing; he hopes that the Community and Economic Development Director will be able to update his own philosophy regarding housing in the near future. He then noted that he has been asking the Council and Administration questions about the Brown's Ice Cream Building development for the past several weeks; those questions remain unanswered, but it is his guess that the Council is now aware that they have been misled about the details of the project, such as how the developer was chosen and where the property was listed and marketed. The value of the property was underestimated, and he wondered how the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) could, in good conscience, not allow other qualified and interested developers to bid on the project after the original contract expired. Most important is why there is not a formalized bid and selection process for RDA owned properties. He first began asking these questions two months ago and since that time the City Council has learned that the broker undervalued the building by nearly half and it is very hard to believe this was an accident, especially since no one can show how and where the building was marketed for sale publicly. The optics regarding this transaction are not good and they give the appearance of a conflict of interest on the part of the broker and that he worked for the builder, rather than the City, as initially communicated to the Council. He hopes the Council is disturbed by these matters as he is and if he is wrong, he would like someone to provide evidence of such. It is unacceptable for residents to be told to blindly trust their government; the ongoing lack of answers from City Administration does not leave residents with many options. If mistakes were made, he would like to hear an explanation for those mistakes and see processes tightened and improved. A few Council members have spoken with him about these questions, and he appreciates that; however, they have not been able to provide legitimate answers to his questions and that only frustrates him more. He is left with no other conclusion than that City Administration is not being entirely forthcoming with the Council. If the Council cannot get more complete answers to these questions for the public, it is at least their duty as the City Council and RDA Board to formalize the bid and procurement process. The Council makes the laws of the City and provides checks and balances for the City's budget; the Council's own budget statement states: "it has always been a Council priority that fmancial information is transparent and readily available to residents and City employees." All he is asking is that the Council live up to that motto as citizens of Ogden deserve as much. The Administration's development process is not transparent, and they should not be keeping information private because doing so is not in the best interest of the City. He concluded the process is broken and asked that the Council fix it.

column3: stated that last week he asked six very specific questions aboutthe Brown's Ice Cream building and project: how was the
column4: Heath Satow stated that last week he asked six very specific questions aboutthe Brown's Ice Cream building and project: how was the developer chosen; where was the property listed and marketed; where are the links to review these expired listings; how is it that the broker, buyer, and City all underestimated the size and value of the building by over half; how can the Redevelopment Agency (RDA)- in good conscience- not allow other qualified and interested developers to bid on the project after the developer allowed the agreement to expire; and why does the RDA not have a formalized bid process for RDA projects. He stated he understands the Mayor does not want these questions answered or he does not know the answers to the questions, but last week the Mayor crossed a line. After asking the questions during the public comment period, the Mayor chose to say "I think we have given a lot of information to answer a lot of those questions, and so I am not going to spend any more time on that." He stated that the Mayor lied; not one of the questions has been answered. He stated he understands the Mayor does not like him and he does not care, but he that does not give him the right to lie about these issues. Mr. Satow says that these questions have not been answered, that is a fact, and he is telling the truth. None of the questions he asked last week have been answered and the Mayor's response only proves his point that the current system of choosing developers for projects is not transparent at all and lacks accountability. The system is broken. When a citizen asks legitimate questions, instead of getting answers they are bullied and gaslit by being told that the questions have been answered. He stated the Mayor knows there is nothing anyone can do about the matter due to how the current process is set up. When the Mayor is perfectly comfortable lying to people's faces, the City needs a new process that will not give him that option. He stated the residents are relying upon the Council to make needed changes so that they are not forced to trust an Administration that refuses to be transparent or held accountable.

column3: thanked the City Council for their consideration of the budget priority relating to funding of the J Marshall N. White C
column4: Joanne Lawrence thanked the City Council for their consideration of the budget priority relating to funding of the J Marshall N. White Center improvement project. Angel Castillo echoed Ms. Lawrence's gratitude regarding their consideration of the Marshall N. White Center project. She then addressed the Council's action and Mr. Ogden's presentation regarding the Quality Neighborhoods Initiative; she agrees with many Council members that the program is good for the City, but that it is necessary to change the way the City provides housing for the average to median income residents of the City. The City needs to closely monitor market trends that are driving housing prices higher and higher and pursue creative housing programs and types that make it more possible for residents to buy a home and create their own wealth or fmancial independence. The City can allow housing types like condominiums and townhomes mixed in with single-family residential projects that can be independently owned.

column3: thanked Council member Lopez for asking for more information and work to be done regarding a broad housing plan for the
column4: Sebastian Benitez thanked Council member Lopez for asking for more information and work to be done regarding a broad housing plan for the City. He also echoed Ms. Castillo's comments about the need to consider other housing options for this community. He then stated that two years ago the City received a grant award for a sidewalk project to serve Wasatch Elementary. He has spoken with City Administration regarding the project and has not gotten clear information regarding the reason the project has been delayed. He asked that the City pay attention to the issues in his neighborhood because many of them are safety problems that put residents in harm. The residents need the sidewalk to provide for safer transportation to and from school for the youth living in that area.

column3: stated he is an Ogden resident and his comments are regarding the clean renewable energy program that the City signed up
column4: David Timmennan stated he is an Ogden resident and his comments are regarding the clean renewable energy program that the City signed up for over a year ago. He has heard concerns about how this program could challenge poorer citizens of the community, but he does not feel that will be the case because everyone has the opportunity to opt out of the program. He asked that the Council remain engaged in the project with the goal of addressing the climate crisis. He stated that winds have increased and worsened in this area over the last several years and that is a result of climate change across the world due to excessive use of carbon. It would be a 'feather in the cap' of the citizens of Ogden to be able to say that Ogden is a leader in the movement to providing cleaner air and reducing fuel use that is contributing to this crisis. He asked that the Council stay strong in support of the program as it is very important not just for Ogden, but for the entire planet.

column3: stated he was glad to hear the discussion during tonight's work session regarding the importance of transparency when co
column4: Heath Satow stated he was glad to hear the discussion during tonight's work session regarding the importance of transparency when considering appointments to City government positions. For the last few months, he has been hammering the same questions about the Brown's Ice Cream building transaction; his biggest question relates to how the City's broker and the buyer undermeasured the square footage of the building and the value by nearly 50 percent. No one will address that question; either the Council does not know the answer or they have been told not to provide it to him. He stated that last week was very telling because someone else asked a question about a sidewalk repair and Chief Administrative Officer Johnson was more than willing to answer it, while he again ignored the questions about the Brown's Ice Cream building; this is because the answer about the sidewalk repair is not embarrassing to Administration. He stated the reason he keeps asking the questions only to be ignored is that the lack of accountability is wrong; the lies and silent treatment are wrong. It appears the City was fooled by a broker who was working for the buyer while pretending to represent the best interests of the City; he hopes this is concerning to the Council. Or maybe there is an actual reasonable explanation for the failure to value the building properly and to fmd more than one qualified developer; the developer that has been selected seems to be very well connected to City Administration. The public is left with the impression that something 'shady' is going on because no one will answer these questions while the Mayor lies when he says that the questions have been answered. Earlier today the Council discussed the Wonder Block development and he asked if anyone could comment on the process that was used to select the developer for this project; it is a developer that was also selected for the other largest project happening in town on the former Rite Aid block. He inquired as to the process the City uses to fmd the best possible developer for these properties, or if there is even a process at all. He asked if it is only necessary for developers to know the right people in City Administration. He stated the Mayor likes to say that the City is built out and he even heard Council member Hyer use the same phrase last week; yet the land the City has left is being developed by people that are secretly selected in a totally opaque process. He recently asked a Council member how the developer for the Wonder Block project was selected and they had no idea; he feels the Council should know how developers of multi-million-dollar projects are selected. The City needs a selection process that allows for absolutely transparency and accountability. He asked who will be performing the Wonder Block commercial property appraisal mentioned during tonight's work session. Angel Castillo also addressed discussions from tonight's work session; she is in favor oftransparency in the selection process. She noted that Council member Lopez recommended a model similar to that used at Weber State University (WSU) and she also supports that type of model. She stated there are many employment positions in the City that will be held by an appointment for a great deal of time and she feels the public should be involved in the selection process for those positions. She has no problem with individuals who have been selected for certain positions, such as Police Chief, but she has concerns with the process that has been employed to select those appointees. She stated that WSU selected a new president recently and they employed a process that allowed for public involvement; the process also recruited applicants from across the entire Country and she feels the same is appropriate in Ogden City. The Council has the chance to change the process to engage the community and she highly recommend the Council do as much as they can to do so.

column3: stated that he heard a Council member state earlier in the meeting that the needs of the many outweigh the needs of the
column4: Kent Wright stated that he heard a Council member state earlier in the meeting that the needs of the many outweigh the needs of the few. He stated that the rights of the few should still be respected, and the action taken by the Council tonight will infringe on the rights of the few to renew their leases and this comes close to communism. This does not sit well with those who have invested in the Airport over the course of their aviation career. Wayne (no last name given) asked the Council if they are aware that by the permission of the City Attorney, the Airport Manager uses security badges for non-security issues and to enforce disputes; he has deactivated badges so that some have not been able to access their own personal property at the Airport and that is not lawful.

column3: addressed Council member Stephens' cmmnents that the City does not want to take property from hangar owners at the Airpo
column4: Renee Felker addressed Council member Stephens' cmmnents that the City does not want to take property from hangar owners at the Airport; he stated nothing can be further from the truth. Those who have current hangar leases understand that when Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, April 20, 2021 Page 147 their lease ends the City can and will take the hangar. The City wants to capture the residual value of the hangar and lease it to someone else. He stated Mr. Williams can state that lessees do not understand their leases, but that is not the case; he understands his lease, which states that he will be required to move his hangar at the end of his lease if he wishes to retain ownership of it. However, leases have traditionally been extended and that is one ofthe factors that he based his determination to lease upon. Right now his hangar is not in the path of any future development plans, but he can not be assured that he will be able to extend his lease; this means the City can take ownership ofhis hangar and lease it to someone else. However, he is not going to give the City that opportunity as he will move his hangar or sell it to someone else and at least break even. Those at greater risk are those with newer hangars, but those who own older hangars can likely remove and sell their hangars and recoup their money.

column3: addressed the action taken regarding hangar leases at the Airport; he addressed Council member Stephens's comments about
column4: Schnyeder Destine addressed the action taken regarding hangar leases at the Airport; he addressed Council member Stephens's comments about the City's subsidy of the Airport and indicated that when hangars are taken by the City, this will essentially mean that hangar owners will be subsidizing the City and the Airport. He stated he was a renter before he bought his hangar and throughout that time he had been in constant conversation with Airport Management; never did he understand that he was entering into a situation where he understood that the improvements he would complete on the land would be taken away. He concluded that if he had a chance to keep on renting, which he did, he would have chosen to do that rather than buy if he had understood that he was at risk oflosing his property. This situation is very upsetting because it is being rushed and the Council is not entertaining all dialogue; the last person who speaks will be relied upon and their comments will be taken as fact. Leslie Briggs congratulated Mr. Garrett on bringing a new commercial carrier to the Ogden Airport. He then stated that he would like to address the comments about the need to make the Airport profitable; Mr. Garrett is working in that direction but grant assurances for FAA funding do not include requiring the Airport to make a profit; rather, the Airport must be self-sustaining. Any money made at the Airport must stay at the Airport and can not be diverted to other City activities. There is no consideration t of the value that the Airport lends to the cmmnunity; it is worth $105 million to the local cmmnunity, but the cost of maintaining ./ the Airport has been placed on the shoulders of the tenants of the Airport. He stated that many businesses fly private jets into the Airport to refuel, but they are burdening the local economy rather than contributing to it.

column3: stated that it will be impossible for some people to remove their hangars; hers is brick and mortar and is the center un
column4: Sheila Garvey stated that it will be impossible for some people to remove their hangars; hers is brick and mortar and is the center unit of a four-unit building. At the end of her lease she has no option but to let the City take over her building. There are many others who are in the same situation as her and this is a very unfortunate position for them to be in.

column3: thanked the Council for their comments during the work session regarding the idea of seeking pertinent information outsi
column4: Angel Castillo thanked the Council for their comments during the work session regarding the idea of seeking pertinent information outside of their regular meetings; specifically, she is referencing the Sustainability Committee and giving them the opportunity to provide input that would give the Council the ability to make fully informed decisions regarding the CREA. She encouraged the Council to make the decision to stay involved in the CREA b.ecause there is nothing more important than providing a clean environment for future generations of City residents. She then addressed the Council's action regarding the Quality Neighborhoods Initiative; she fully supports the goals of the Initiative, and the work that has been done in the target area. Overall, it is a great package, but if the City does not have a plan for how to provide affordable housing across the entire community, the City is going to struggle to meet the needs of its residents. A concrete plan is needed and such a plan could work hand in hand with the Initiative to meet needs of the target area and the community at large. In regards to the Marshall N. White Center, she appreciates the Council committing to the facility; the MWC is part of the community that serves as a place for children and adults to come together to make a community.

column3: spoke in support of the recommendation that the City Council reach out to the Sustainability Committee to get their inpu
column4: Bonnie Christiansen spoke in support of the recommendation that the City Council reach out to the Sustainability Committee to get their input regarding the CREA; the Committee is made up of many people who have spent a great deal of time researching and considering the subject matter and their input would be valuable.

column3: stated he appreciates all the work the Council does and he feels it is fantastic the City has the opportunity to be invo
column4: David Timmerman stated he appreciates all the work the Council does and he feels it is fantastic the City has the opportunity to be involved with the CREA. He encouraged the Council to continue to work with other partner communities to clean the air. There are few things more important than clean air, water, and food and the City should do whatever it can to mitigate current problems and make improvements in the future. He stated he does not feel the risk of participating is too high, yet the reward is very high. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, April 27, 2021 Page 158 Heath Satow also referenced tonight's work session meeting and he was glad to see the amount of debate regarding many of the matters discussed, no matter how small the potential change. However, there are two City blocks that are being redeveloped and there were no public meetings about how a single developer was chosen to develop both blocks; this will be one of the largest single development projects in the City. As he mentioned before, the City has repeated the sentiment that the City is 'built-out', but if that is the case he wondered why the development of entire City blocks, where the City is giving incentives to developers to participate in the project, were discussed and decided upon by just a few people behind closed doors. He asked if the remaining space available in the City is not worthy of more public debate and discussion than an honorary street name. Everyone knows that sunlight is the best disinfectant, and that power corrupts; the current system allows for absolute power behind closed doors to select developers that will get significant incentives to create $100 million plus developments with no sunlight on the process. There has been no real oversight and as has been seen with the Brown Ice Cream building decision making process, there has been zero accountability. He would have a problem with a system that was ripe for corruption even if he fully trusted everyone involved, but he again reminded the Council about the questions that he has asked and that the Mayor has chosen to lie about by stating they have already been answered. The questions have not been answered and he asked for accountability. He noted that Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper stood in front of the Council and told them to their faces that the building was being marketed on Loop Net and the MLS, but Administration has not and will not provide any evidence of the building ever being listed or marketed by the broker they were working wish. It appears the building was never listed publicly anywhere; MLS listings are available in perpetuity and if the building was in fact listed, the Administration needs to provide the listings or publicly admit they misinformed the RDA Board. As far as he can determine, only one developer was ever infonned about the development opportunity and he is someone the Mayor knows personally, and then the broker underestimated the value of the building by over half. This is an estimate that was presented to the RDA and City Council during every presentation they received regarding the project. Either the broker lied to Mr. Cooper about the marketing of the building or Mr. Cooper knowingly misinformed the RDA and he asked if anyone is concerned about this and ifthere is any accountability for misleading the RDA. He asked if anyone is looking into this issue; if the City Council cannot and will not hold Administration accountable for misleading them, they should at least adopt a new process that will not allow something similar to happen in the future. A public bidding system is needed to shine light on the entire process and deals should not be made behind closed doors.

column3: thanked the Council for its support of the Marshall N. White Center and stated she hopes when the time comes, the Counci
column4: Joanne Lawrence thanked the Council for its support of the Marshall N. White Center and stated she hopes when the time comes, the Council will ensure that the funding that has been set aside will be used not just for day-to-day operations, but to make real improvements at the Center.

column3: stated she was also very pleased to hear that the Council plans to remain involved in the Community Renewal Energy Act (
column4: Linda Zevelov stated she was also very pleased to hear that the Council plans to remain involved in the Community Renewal Energy Act (CREA) to pursue 100 percent sustainable electricity by the year 2030. The fact that only a couple of municipalities have signed on to participate in the Act is a misunderstanding given that many other communities signed on in 2019 at the same time as Ogden City. The update to the legislation simply provides other communities additional time to opt into the program. She asked that Ogden City take the steps necessary to be listed on the Utah 100 website as a participating entity in the process. She added there are many in the community that have the expertise to provide support to the City in its sustainability efforts. Trevor Jones echoed the comments made in support of the City's involvement in the CREA. He also referenced the Council's discussion of the Weber State University (WSU) net-zero energy home program; he performed research to determine how many net-zero homes would need to be constructed to equal the carbon emissions of Ogden's involvement in the CREA. He found that staying in the CREA is equivalent to creating 17,3 3 0 net homes, which is higher than he thought and underscores the importance of being involved in the CREA. The CREA dwarfs other projects that are underway, and he is very happy that the City has decided to stay involved. He understands the difficulty of that decision because of the lack of information, but he is grateful for the Council's foresight in understanding the value of the CREA and choosing to lead by their efforts. Katherine Myer also spoke in support of the CREA; she knows every city is unique and that is why staying involved in the Act is the only way to answer Ogden's unique environmental issues. Renewable energy is being discussed at all levels of government and the CREA will help to prepare Ogden for the demand associated with economic development projects that require renewable energy. She added there are many local residents who can provide support to the City as it explores renewable energy options for the community. Jeremy Shinoda also spoke to the CREA and indicated he is very excited about the goal of achieving an amount equivalent to 100 percent of the annual electric energy supply for participating customers by 2030; this fits the vision he has for Ogden's future, and he is happy he will have the choice to choose renewable energy options for his own household. The CREA will give all residents and businesses that choice and each customer will have the ability to opt-out of the program. He encouraged the Council to continue to attend the open houses and informational sessions hosted by the Utah 100 communities and to add Ogden's name to the Utah100.org/team webpage. Adam Toby also voiced his support for the City's participation in the CREA. He encouraged the Council to utilize the resources available to it, including the Sustainability Committee and many students/professionals from WSU who have a great deal of knowledge about the matter.

column3: stated he listened into the City's work session meeting this evening and was pleased to hear the City Council voice supp
column4: Mark Stephenson stated he listened into the City's work session meeting this evening and was pleased to hear the City Council voice support for continuing to be involved in renewable energy efforts in the State of Utah. He understands there are many questions about these efforts, and he suggested that the Council rely upon the City's Natural Resources and Sustainability Stewardship Committee to help them keep up with the details of Statewide efforts.

column3: thanked the Council for the questions they asked during the work session meeting as then engaged in discussion with Poli
column4: Angel Castillo thanked the Council for the questions they asked during the work session meeting as then engaged in discussion with Police Department Administration regarding operations of their department. She echoed Mr. Satow's comments regarding references to the Ogden-Clearfield metro area for various data points; this includes housing statistics that are not representative of Ogden proper; the median income in the Clearfield area is much higher than the Ogden area and the two should not be grouped together for the purposes of basing very important decisions on the data for the metro area.

column3: stated that Council member Nadolski, a Council member that he respects, made it clear to him his trust and respect of Co
column4: Heath Satow stated that Council member Nadolski, a Council member that he respects, made it clear to him his trust and respect of Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper and how his comments to the Council have come across as personal attacks on Mr. Cooper. He stated that was not his goal, but he recognizes how it could have appeared that way and he apologized. He regrets that his delivery of the questions he has asked have taken away from the focus on the questions themselves. He was and is still frustrated about the lack of transparency in processes the City follows for certain redevelopment projects and he hopes that his feedback will help those processes to evolve and become more transparent. He still has two questions and he has emailed them to the City Council for their review. He then stated that as it becomes possible to hold in- person Council meetings in the Council Chambers, he hopes the City will continue to allow residents to participate via Zoom, particularly for work sessions that begin at4:00 p.m. as it is difficult for some to attend a meeting at that time of day. Zoom also makes it easier for many to attend meetings and provide input. He concluded by discussing the claim of the job market in Ogden being number one in America for 2021; that data is for the Ogden-Clearfield area, which is largely due to the presence of the military operations at Hill Air Force Base.

column3: thanked Mr. Smith for his explanation about the difference between housing projects to be completed utilizing Housing an
column4: Angel Castillo thanked Mr. Smith for his explanation about the difference between housing projects to be completed utilizing Housing and Urban Development (HUD) funds under the Annual Action Plan (AAP). She noted there are many housing programs in the City, and it can be difficult to understand the nuances of each program. She thanked Council member Choberka Minutes of Special Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, May 11, 2021 Page 173 for her statement of intent to continue to explore and pursue a housing plan that will address low to moderate income housing needs in the community.

column3: asked if the City Council members received an email he sent last week; he resent the email today because he did not rece
column4: Heath Satow asked if the City Council members received an email he sent last week; he resent the email today because he did not receive a response from any Council member or representative of City Administration. He would like confirmation as to when he can expect an answer to his questions as he has been asking the same questions for several months. He then referenced a discussion that took place during tonight's work session and asked for clarification of terms discussed; his understanding is that the Council is being removed from the decision-making process for several types of projects in the City and he asked for clarification. He concluded by thanking the Council for concluding to offer virtual participation in public meetings in the future.

column3: stated last week only two people made public comments to the City Council, himself and one other individual. He asked a
column4: Heath Satow stated last week only two people made public comments to the City Council, himself and one other individual. He asked a few questions of the Council and Administration, but at the conclusion of his comments there was no acknowledgement that he had even spoken. He stated he fmds that to be impolite. He knows that Council members Choberka, Lopez, and Nadolski have tried to get answers to his specific questions, but the rest of the Council has failed to acknowledge that his questions have been asked. He is very frustrated, to say the least; he has sent the same email to the entire Council twice and it has been ignored both times. He stated tonight his question is how to go about getting those questions answered and he asked that someone acknowledge that he is asking those questions rather than ignoring him. ·

column3: stated she attended the Weber County Prosperity Center of Excellence meeting yesterday and she commended Council members
column4: Angel Castillo stated she attended the Weber County Prosperity Center of Excellence meeting yesterday and she commended Council members White and Hyer for also attending to hear important information about the housing challenges the entire State of Utah is facing. She referenced an email she sent to the Council on January 23, 2019 that discussed many of the things that were considered during yesterday's meeting, and she encouraged the Council to revisit that email and to listen to the recording of the meeting. Important decisions are being made based upon current conditions, which includes a dramatic spike in home ownership and rental rates. The City will face difficulties in continuing to administer programs aimed at providing homes to low to moderate income individuals given that construction prices continue to increase; the City should not be selling homes in the $400,000 price range and classify those homes as affordable. Certain models need to be reconsidered and the City should consider zoning adjustments and allowing smaller homes to keep prices low. These are things the Council should be considering as they enter the 2021 budget season. J ase Reyneveld stated he attended the Farmers Market over the weekend, and it was great to see so many visitors, small businesses, and the community gathering together. He then noted that he is disappointed that the Ogden Marathon was cancelled this year; he understands that the Get Out And Live (GOAL) Foundation did a great job in hosting a virtual event, but he was saddened that an in-person annual event that has brought so much joy to people was cancelled. He stated that if the matter had ) been approached with optimism rather than pessimism, it would have been possible to hold the event, similar to the manner in which the Farmers Market proceeded in a somewhat normal fashion. He then concluded by asking when the Council will return to in-person meetings; these meetings are a great opportunity for the community to come together and engage with their elected officials and he would like for them to return to a normal, in-person format soon.

column3: stated he is very disappointed that a Council member wants to 'game' the voting process for the honorary street name cha
column4: Heath Satow stated he is very disappointed that a Council member wants to 'game' the voting process for the honorary street name change resolution. He then stated that he appreciated a few Council members addressing questions he has asked over the course of the last few meetings; he was told that Council members have tried to get answers to his questions from City Administration, but they have had no luck. It was confmned by Council member Hyer last week that each member of the Council has received his questions via email and Council member Lopez confmned that the Council has not received answers to the questions from Administration. He was told to reach out to Administration to get answers to his questions, but the fact is that he ) has asked the same questions of the Administration via email, in public comment portions of Council meetings since February, and he has even filled out the online fonn to request a meeting with the Mayor, but the Mayor refused to respond to any of his methods for communicating about his concems. He stated that he is not sure how to get the Mayor to respond in any meaningful way. He is left with the sense that somewhere along the way it was leamed that hard questions are best left ignored and, if ignored, Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, May 25, 2021 Page 193 they will just go away. He is not interested in allowing the Administration to be held unaccountable for their actions and he asked what the secret is; why will Administration not even acknowledge that he has asked questions and why do they refuse to answer ( the questions, even when Council members have inquired. He stated the questions that the Administration refuses to answer are: how did an experienced broker supposedly representing the City undervalue the Brown's Ice Cream building by over half; was the broker secretly working on behalf of the developer that is getting the building at a fraction of the value at a significant loss to future investment by the Redevelopment Agency (RDA); does the Administration care about these issues. The RDA was told that the broker was marketing the building in typical ways, but it appears that if the broker told the City this, they were lying because there is no evidence the building was marketed at all by the broker. Again, this makes it look like the broker was working for the developer rather than the City. By not answering these questions, it appears the City is comfortable with the understanding that the broker 'ripped off' the City of Ogden. He is begging the Council to not allow the transaction move forward until Administration is willing to publicly answer the questions.

column3: discussed safe sidewalk projects in neighborhoods in the community to provide a safe way for children to commute to and
column4: Sebastian Benitez discussed safe sidewalk projects in neighborhoods in the community to provide a safe way for children to commute to and from school; these projects have been discussed for many years and he is happy that they have been completed this year. He knows that many people have been inconvenienced by construction on the projects, but safety of the children is most important to him.

column3: stated he is the Chair of the Ogden Trails Network Committee, and he requested a status update of the Council's consider
column4: Brian Waters stated he is the Chair of the Ogden Trails Network Committee, and he requested a status update of the Council's consideration of possible adjustments to the Board member approval process for various advisory committees; it is his understanding the Council is considering adjusting the ordinance, but he is awaiting the appointment of three new members right now and until those members are appointed, it is difficult for the Committee to conduct business.

column3: stated it is great to see everyone in person after being stuck on Zoom meetings for a year. He addressed Mayor Caldwell
column4: Heath Satow stated it is great to see everyone in person after being stuck on Zoom meetings for a year. He addressed Mayor Caldwell and stated that while he has made choices as the City's Mayor that he clearly disagrees with, he believes Mayor Caldwell's intentions for Ogden are good. He is glad to see Mayor Caldwell in person tonight because he has not been able to swear with certainty that the Mayor wants what is best for Ogden based upon his silence on a number of issues. Most pressing is the concern that the Mayor has not responded to a question he began asking in February of this year; he has expressed this concern weekly in Council meetings, via emails, and in an in-person meeting with the Mayor, but there has been no response at all. Council members have responded to him and said even they cannot get answers to the questions and he is getting a sense that the Mayor does not understand his concerns; he restated them as follows: why did an experienced broker supposedly representing the City undervalue the Brown Ice Cream building by over $1 00,000; was the broker working on behalf of the developer rather than in the best interest of the City; does the City even know the answers to these questions and if not, why not; the RDA told the public that the broker had marketed the building in usual ways, but there is no evidence the building was marketed at all. These matters are of significant concern as it creates the appearance that the broker was working for the developer and not the City. The answers to these questions are of great concern to the citizens and he asked if the Mayor will show that he believes in transparency and accountability by responding in a meaningful way to the concerns. He noted his fmal request tonight is for the Council in their capacity of the Redevelopment Agency; he asked that they not allow the project to move forward at all until the Administration is willing to be transparent about these concerns. If Administration refuses, the process should be restarted with a broker that the public can be assured has the best interest of the City in mind.

column3: discussed high daytime and overnight temperatures and indicated that if people are unable to cool themselves down, they
column4: Bonnie Christiansen discussed high daytime and overnight temperatures and indicated that if people are unable to cool themselves down, they are susceptible to heat stroke. Other communities have worked with their local health departments to establish cooling centers for elderly residents or those without air conditioning in their homes and she wondered of similar efforts are underway in Ogden.

column3: thanked the Council for their consideration of his comments regarding The Comer Plaza arts project; the last thing he wa
column4: Heath Satow thanked the Council for their consideration of his comments regarding The Comer Plaza arts project; the last thing he wants to do is obstruct public art and he loves the murals that are being completed on Grant A venue. He then noted that he wanted to thank Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper for meeting with him for over three hours last week to discuss his concerns and questions that had not been answered up to that date. It took three months to get his answers about the Brown's Ice Cream building and he learned that there is still much to talk about. He is hoping to meet with City Council members, and he would like for the City to prioritize the creation of public policy around the selection of developers for City properties. Angel Castillo referenced the frreworks restrictions in the community and noted she has witnessed frreworks on the east bench since the restrictions were implemented. This is very scary given the dry conditions on the east bench. She noted she understands the Fire Chief is operating within what he believes to be his purview but noted that other cities in Utah have instituted frreworks bans; she has spoken with lawyers who have told her that local municipalities can take health and safety precautions if there is a legitimate public safety concern. This is a loophole the City must use to implement complete bans on frreworks. She does not believe that she is being an alarmist and she encouraged Ogden to follow other communities in the State who have taken actions to dramatically increase their restrictions or implement a complete ban. Some cities are allowing public frreworks in defmed areas where the frre risk is much lower; this is an option for the City, but she would prefer expanded restrictions or an all- out ban. She encouraged Ogden to lead on this issue as it is so important for the entire community. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, June 15, 2021 Page 226 Administration Comments Chief Administrative Officer Johnson referenced Ms. Martinez's comments and stated it is a great idea to utilize stakeholders to help spread the word about the declaration responsive to drought conditions. The City is also working on a communications piece in the event that it is necessary to shut down the water treatment plant. He then addressed Ms. Christiansen's question about the presence of cooling centers; this is a great idea and Ogden City is working with the Red Cross to create local cooling centers in the community. He also referenced Ms. Castillo's comments about a fireworks ban; the City will continue to evaluate its options, but if a fireworks ban is enacted illegally, the City is at risk of being sued, which can be very costly for the residents. He will monitor what is happening in other communities to detennine the City's most viable options. He agreed that those living above Harrison Boulevard are not following fireworks restrictions and that is why he feels that increased enforcement is necessary.

column3: stated she is a candidate for Ogden City Council District Three, and she has questions with regard to the water shortage
column4: Priscilla Martinez stated she is a candidate for Ogden City Council District Three, and she has questions with regard to the water shortage issue. She asked ifthere is already a communication plan in place if it becomes necessary to shut down the water treatment plant. She then advised that the City utilize stakeholders in the community, such as church leaders and non-profit organizations, to disseminate the important information regarding the water shortage declaration.

column3: reported that last week he spent a few hours speaking with Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper abo
column4: Heath Satow reported that last week he spent a few hours speaking with Community and Economic Development Deputy Director Cooper about the acquisition of the Brown's Ice Cream building. This conversation made it clear to him why Administration resisted answering the questions he has been asking for the past three months. What he learned is that the scenario that took place does not break any existing rules and that City Administration can legally hire a broker of their choice- in this case the broker had a business relationship with the developer- and the broker can undervalue the building and only tell that one developer about the project. This is because the City chose not to sign any contract with the broker, which would have legally required him to accurately value the building or risk losing their license. He stated that this seems intentional. The Redevelopment Agency (RDA), supposedly representing the best interests of the City and its people, was given infonnation that they based their decision on; this infonnation came from a broker that was only working in the developer's best interest. In other words, there was no effort to represent the citizens of Ogden. The broker was working to estimate the value of the building as low as possible without raising any red flags. The current rules completely allowed a 'buddy of a buddy' to develop a property and take advantage of a $250,000 gift that would have been prohibited if there were rules in place. He stated he feels everyone should be able to agree that what happened is not right; this type of situation is the very reason bureaucracy exists, though many people hate bureaucracy. It is not reasonable to assume that everyone is naturally working in the best interest of the City. He thanked Mr. Cooper for taking the time to explain what is legally allowed by current processes, but this unintentionally increased his concerns about the Brown's Ice Cream transaction and other development deals in the City. Since the original deal approved by the RDA for the Brown's Ice Cream building has expired, Mr. Satow suggested that the City sign a contract with a different broker to get a true and factual valuation for the building in order for it to be properly marketed to qualified developers. He stated that he believes this will yield more money for the RDA and result in a more inspired vision for the building. He is glad to hear that some members of the Council are working to change the system to ensure increased transparency in the future.

column3: spoke to the need of the City to consider a comprehensive housing plan that focuses on providing affordable housing choi
column4: Angel Castillo spoke to the need of the City to consider a comprehensive housing plan that focuses on providing affordable housing choices to those who currently live in the City as well as future generations that will desire to live in the community. This includes the working class of Ogden that contribute greatly to the community. She referenced her comments regarding parking fee adjustments and noted she is simply asking the City to consider a real and true fmancial hardship and adjust parking citation fees accordingly. There are many people who live in the community who do not enjoy the same privileges as others; this is a working-class town and she is concerned about those on a fixed income that cannot afford things that others may be able to.

column3: stated he loves Ogden and the outdoor recreation scene and easy access to beautiful mountains and trails. He added his s
column4: David Timmerman stated he loves Ogden and the outdoor recreation scene and easy access to beautiful mountains and trails. He added his support for the City to remain involved in the program created by House Bill411, the Community Renewable Energy Act. This should be the most important issue, not just for Ogden and Utah residents, but for everyone worldwide. Increased winds, extreme heat, and other weather occurrences are evidence of climate change. Climate change is not a hoax. He is aware there will be a vote on this issue next week and he encouraged the Council to support continued participate in the program. Everyone needs to work towards creating clean renewable energy sources.

column3: discussed the Community Renewable Energy Program; climate change is getting worse, and she encouraged Ogden to do its pa
column4: Lynn Carrol discussed the Community Renewable Energy Program; climate change is getting worse, and she encouraged Ogden to do its part to help achieve net 100 percent renewable energy by 2030. She discussed Rocky Mountain Power's ability to provide power to the community, but noted their sources are not entirely renewable. It will not cost Ogden residents much extra if the City participates in the State-wide program and she encouraged the Council to remain in the program. Heath Satow also discussed renewable energy and occurrences in California related to their renewable energy programs; they may be producing excess power at this time, but there will come a time in the future when other states may need more energy and California can charge those states to use their excess energy. He added that solar power costs have dropped recently and are now more comparable with other types of energy sources, and as a late comer to the 'solar game' the City can capitalize on the things that have been learned about solar and create systems that are easily cut off of the power grid to avoid problems. He encouraged Ogden to be a leader rather than a follower.lt is impmtant for the City to get facts about energy issues that have arisen in other States, such as Texas, and not base important decisions on false or incomplete information. He noted that California has never had an energy crisis similar to the one that occurred in Texas in the past year. He stated it is not necessary for the City to have all answers before proceeding with certain programs; this type of methodology makes the future worse for future generations. The City Administration seems to be more than willing to lose hundreds of thousands of dollars to benefit a single developer but paying $35,000 for an energy program might be too much. The City can no longer deny the reality of important environmental issues and he asked that leadership put as much effort into our children's futures as into street naming.

column3: stated he has sent an email to all City Council members and the Mayor about his suggestion to consider budget amendments
column4: Sebastian Benitez stated he has sent an email to all City Council members and the Mayor about his suggestion to consider budget amendments to increase pay for police officers in the City; the Police Department is at risk of losing quality officers because of low wages and the City needs to address this issue. column3: voiced his support for the Ogden City Arts Grants and thanked the Council for their consideration of the proposed awards
column4: Trevor Jones voiced his support for the Ogden City Arts Grants and thanked the Council for their consideration of the proposed awards that were communicated to them earlier this evening. He then echoed the comments made by those before him about the importance of the City's participation on the community renewable energy act. The State Legislature has recognized climate change and the important of doing work to overcome it; the question now is what that work looks, how to do it, and when. He stated a lot of work has been done over the last 10 to 15 years to reduce the cost of renewable energy resources so that they are comparable to traditional energy sources. Costs are likely to decline even further. He referenced the work session discussion of the matter and noted he recognizes that there are differing viewpoints; he thanked those who are in favor of considering renewable energy options. He addressed those that are undecided on how to proceed and implored them to consider the science behind the issues and what it means to be a good steward of the earth and its nature resources. It is important to be forward thinking and proactive and he encouraged the City to stay involved in the programs created by the Community Renewable Energy Act. Bonnie Christiansen also spoke about the importance of being involved in the Community Renewable Energy Act; she enjoys living in Ogden because of access to outdoor recreation activities and in order to preserve those opportunities, the City must be proactive in pursuing renewable energy programs. Climate change is accelerating and is very impactful to residents and everyone is responsible to take action to address it. She thanked the City for its efforts thus far to be engaged in the programs created by the Community Renewable Energy Act and she encouraged them to stay involved.

column3: stated she is part of the sustainability team at Weber State University (WSU), and she thanked the Council for voting to
column4: Alice Molder stated she is part of the sustainability team at Weber State University (WSU), and she thanked the Council for voting to reinforce the commitment they made in 2019 to pursue net renewable electricity by 2030. It is critical for Ogden to be a leader in this endeavor, and she believes that other communities will wish they had gotten involved in the program when they had the opportunity. She discussed the 'blue sky' program, which is an optional add-on to the larger program, and provides other options for those who do not opt out. She thanked the Council members for commenting about their concerns, the things they have learned, and their support for exploring something that can truly benefit the community. She is happy that Ogden has received a formal commitment from WSU to help with outreach efforts in the community.

column3: stated that she is pleased with many of the discussions and actions that have taken place tonight; the Council has made
column4: Angel Castillo stated that she is pleased with many of the discussions and actions that have taken place tonight; the Council has made difficult decisions and she is pleased that the Council renewed its commitment to pursuing net renewable energy. column4: Bonnie Christiansen stated she is grateful that the Council made the choice to pursue renewable energy sources as she feels this will benefit the entire community, especially vulnerable citizens in the community. Ogden should be celebrated as northern Utah's clean energy leader.

column3: stated it was disheartening to hear the hesitancy to act on the community renewable energy program and he is disappointe
column4: Heath Satow stated it was disheartening to hear the hesitancy to act on the community renewable energy program and he is disappointed City Administration has chosen not to lead out on this issue. He agreed with Council member Nadolski's assessment that the City needs to have a 'seat at the table' in regard to governance of this program. He referenced Council member Hyer's comments and stated that the experts he has spoken to is a climate change denialist; he has been formally accused of scientific dishonesty by a group of environmental scientists. He is disappointed to have that unqualified voice brought into this conversation. He stated settled science indicates that huge amounts of carbon dioxide are being created by human generated automotive and industrial activities; this is a fact, and the environment is being heated up by this increased in energy consumption. The costs of being involved in the program at this point is a very small fraction of the City's annual budget. The City has been debating the cost of replacing sidewalks in front of 15 homes in the community and he contrasted that with discussion of energy issues that have the potential to literally save the lives of future generations. He will gladly forego replacement of the broken Minutes of Special Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, July 13, 2021 Page 268 sidewalk in front of his home for a few more years in order for the City to remain in the program. He thanked those that supported remaining in the program. Sebastian Benitez also spoke to the importance of being involved in the Community Renewable Energy Program; he understands the concerns that have been expressed, but he is so happy that the decision to remain in the program was made. The funding implications are small when compared to other programs and projects the City spends money on. He thanked the Council for their vote in support of pursuing net renewable energy sources. David Timmennan also thanked the Council for voting to uphold their commitmentto explore change in terms of energy sources; the City now has a seat in the process of designing the program and he is pleased that WSU has committed to support the City in those endeavors. Trevor Jones also thanked the Council for their vote to support the program; he noted that many valid concerns were expressed tonight, but many of those concerns are based upon the assumption that energy rates are increasing for those who participate in the program. However, it is his guess that rates will stay the same or even decrease because it is now cheaper to build a new utility solar farm than to run an existing coal plant. Costs of solar and wind power continue to decrease dramatically and those sources, along with nuclear, are the best power sources for the community in the future. He supports nuclear power if costs can be decreased, but that is yet to be seen. He expects low income individuals to understand and support clean energy because they understand the impacts of climate change as they are not insulated from it. He thanked the Council for their vote tonight for himself and for future generations of this community. Jennifer Bodine also thanked the Council for their careful thought of the program and for ultimately voting to remain in the program. She feels that many of the concerns and questions will be addressed as the process to further develop the program moves forward. She also reiterated that WSU is here to support the City by engaging the community, attend meetings, perform analysis, and develop rate models; they will advocate for the City and its participation in the program.

column4: Jenny Gnagey stated she is also proud ofthe Council and thanked them for the decision they made tonight regarding the Community Renewable Energy Program. column4: Priscilla Martinez stated she is a candidate for office in Council District Three; Ogden is evolving and changing and remaining involved in the Community Renewable Energy Program is a great way for Ogden to look out for its residents and lead in renewable energy efforts. column4: Rick Creager stated that he attended a Rocky Mountain Power (RMP) meeting recently where there was discussion of closing down a coal plant, but that plant could be converted to wind or solar and RMP could secure fossil fuel subsidies to maintain the employees ofthe plan and reeducate power users. column4: Tammy Creager stated there is no denying climate change and she supports the Council in its decision to remain in the program and being a leader for positive change going forward.

column4: Amy Wicks stated there was an incident that happened yesterday morning, August 2 at 11:00 a.m., at approximately 24th Street and Fillmore Avenue. The weather was rainy; this was predicted and should not have been a surprise. Yet, a contractor displayed a disgusting waste of taxpayer dollars by painting bike lanes and a center lane down the road in the middle of the rainstorm. The paint was running off the road and into the gutters, which feed the stonn water system and are discharged into local rivers and streams. Beyond the environmental damage, the work looks terrible and will not last, and this is a tremendous waste of taxpayer dollars. The contractor should be fmed, should not be paid for this shoddy work, and should be banned from receiving future contracts with Ogden City. She has filed a report with the Division of Water Quality of the State of Utah, and they will be reaching out to the City to get information about the contractor. She hopes City Administration will respond to this issue in a timely manner, as this is not acceptable. The City needs to do a better job at making sure contractors follow best practices when they are performing work for the City and to ensure that precious taxpayer dollars are not being wasted.

column4: Gaylene Morley stated she sent a letter to the City Council to summarize some ofher concems. column4: Heath Satow spoke about a group listed on the City website that is charged with advising the Mayor and City Council on policies pertaining to City education programs relating to sustainable environmental practices and responsible stewardship of Ogden's natural resources. This committee, the Ogden Natural Resources and Sustainability Stewardship Committee, could have been very helpful during the City's recycling crisis last year and particularly during the recent discussions surrounding the Community Renewable Energy Act, also known as House :J?ill411. He recently learned the Committee lacks enough members to have a quorum and has had only five members for the last eight months; they basically cannot vote on anything and their hands are tied. He also understands that people have applied to be appointed to the committee, but those applications are just sitting on the Mayor's desk waiting for him to take action. He asked that the Council press the Mayor to take a few moments to review the applications and fill the vacancies so the Committee can do its job and help the City make better, more informed choices. The Committees should be shown the respect they deserve for the time and effort they dedicate to helping the City.
