column3: encouraged the Council to revert to virtual meetings rather than in-person meetings to do their part to reduce the sprea
column4: Heath Satow encouraged the Council to revert to virtual meetings rather than in-person meetings to do their part to reduce the spread of COVID-19. He noted that many people have become vaccinated, but even vaccinated individuals are still contracting the virus. He then echoed Ms. Castillo's reference to the developer selection process discussion, noting that he feels the Council's discussion represents a 'half-effort' rather than a genuine interest in developing a policy that remedies issues that have arisen in past selection processes for development projects. He stated that he hopes the Council will consider any and all opportunities to make the process more equitable and take the measures necessary to ensure that developers and brokers are being truthful and are working in the best interest of the City rather than just those that they represent financially.

column3: stated he is past member of the Ogden Airport Advisory Committee; he referenced the agenda item dealing with the appoint
column4: Ed McKinney stated he is past member of the Ogden Airport Advisory Committee; he referenced the agenda item dealing with the appointments and reappointments of the Ogden Airport Advisory Committee and stated the purpose ofhis comments are to suggest that the Council not approve that list of candidates with the exception of Robert Dandoy. Having sat on several Airport Advisory Boards in many states, he can say the role of Airport Manager requires some of the most in-depth and diverse knowledge of any municipal job; with this in mind, it is equally important that the Advisory Committee have similar in-depth knowledge on topics such as grant assurances, FAA regulations, liability insurance, and airport safety. The candidates that have been recmmnended for appointment have little to no aviation knowledge, skills, or experience and no in-depth relationships or understanding of the businesses or stakeholders at the Ogden Airport and they lack the skills and experience to advise the Airport Manager in Ogden City as is required by Ordinance2021-6, Section 2(c)(1)(a). As a result, he appealed to the Council to fill these critical roles with candidates who can speak with authority on airport and aviation issues and opportunities. Angel Castillo referenced the work session agenda item relating to ordinance text amendments regarding conditional use permits (CUPs). She is most concerned about an exterior favade change not requiring Planning Commission input and approval. She supports the other adjustments as she feels they will help Planning staff process applications more efficiently, but the Planning staff is not as representative of the community as the Planning Commission is and, therefore, the Planning Commission is better equipped to handle request for exterior favade changes. Until the City adopts a very specific list of exterior building materials to govern decisions of Planning staff, she suggests that type of CUP amendment should be referred to the Planning Commission. She referenced another work session item dealing with a zone change that would allow development of a housing project on a cul-de-sac; she does not believe cul-de-sacs are a wise use of public investment in tenns offacilities. Additionally, the Council needs to consider the smallest residential lot size they are comfmtable with and how many single-family homes can be built on a smaller lot; the City needs high density housing, single family homes, and townhomes because there is a demand for all types of housing right now. However, developers in the cmmnunity are stymied by development regulations that are too restrictive for the current market. Priscilla Martinez simply stated she would echo Ms. Castillo's input.

column3: stated she is a homeowner in Ogden, and she is here to address the Council regarding property at 550 East 900 North wher
column4: Alene Evans stated she is a homeowner in Ogden, and she is here to address the Council regarding property at 550 East 900 North where a church building is being demolished and the property is being redeveloped. A developer has submitted a request to change the current single family housing zoning to one that would allow multi-family dwellings and increased density. Ogden City is currently over 50 percent rental properties, and 900 North is the access to a high-density mobile home park; the traffic onto Washington Boulevard at 900 North is extremely congested, hazardous, and deadly. Rental complexes do not increase neighborhood home values, nor do they create pride of ownership; transitional housing does not build stability in a neighborhood. Crime rates are higher at rental prope1ties and the fees for law enforcement and fire personnel are disproportionate and concerning. Absentee landlords are not invested in the maintenance and well-being of rental properties. Ogden City has recently experienced a dramatic increase in apartment complexes and high-density housing, and this is a great concern for single family homeowners. The Plarming Commission and City Council should not feel obligated to change the zoning regulations for developers in order for them to make more money at the expense of current homeowners that have invested in their neighborhoods. The area could use nice, affordable homes but not apartment complexes. Ogden City no longer has long range planning directives for the Planning Commission and City Council to consider when making this type of decision; in the past, the Planning staff and Planning Commission would have had plans to rely upon. Building codes should impose specific standards to ensure aesthetically pleasing and safe high-density developments, different than the type ofproject that was recently built on Wall Minutes of Special Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, September 14, 2021 Page 309 Avenue that is placed right up to the sidewalk in that area. The north end of the City has many existing high-density developments and all of the City's mobile home parks are located north of 12111 Street; changing the zoning of the subject property without a deep consideration of the existing amount of high-density development and the existing homeowners in the area is concerning. Council member Hyer noted that Ms. Evans was an Ogden City employee for many years until her recent retirement.

column3: stated she is happy that people are attending City Council meetings and making their voices heard about issues that are
column4: Angel Castillo stated she is happy that people are attending City Council meetings and making their voices heard about issues that are concerning to them. However, she wished to offer information about the economic and fiscal impact of multi- family housing from the Harvard Center of Housing. She stated those that have spoken before her made claims of negative impacts ofhigh-density housing, but studies have shown that police activity is no higher in a high-density project than in a single- family subdivision and, in many cases, it is lower than in single family areas. The Harvard report also goes on to explain how renters are invested in their communities as a homeowner; they are twice as likely to socialize with their neighbors as homeowners and equally as likely to take part in structured social groups, have an interest in politics, identify closely with their town or city, and are only slightly less likely to attend religious services. In conclusion, the study undermines the notion that apartment residents somehow do not care about or do not involve themselves in the community in which they live. She wants to make sure that the Council is considering all points of view and data. Most important is the type of housing that is built on the subject property; the median home price in Ogden has increased by 33 percent in recent months and the City needs to adjust zoning standards to allow for smaller units for purchase and develop a plan to filter high density housing throughout the entire City. Ogden needs to be reactive rather than proactive in providing different housing options, both for rent and purchase.

column3: stated she is speaking about the same property as Ms. Evans; she has reached out to the entire Council to voice her conc
column4: Judy Lewis stated she is speaking about the same property as Ms. Evans; she has reached out to the entire Council to voice her concerns about the proposed zone change and development of the subject property and she heard back from just two Council members. She stated several of her neighbors are present this evening and they all share the same concerns expressed by Ms. Evans. She has lived in her home for 62 years and when she first moved to the home, the area was unincorporated, and she paid for services in both Ogden and North Ogden cities. It was later incorporated, but she was still paying Bona Vista Water and the North Ogden Cemetery, and it took her some time to rectify those issues. She is now appealing to the City Council to protect her neighborhood from an apartment building at 550 East 900 North. She discussed issues such as limited parking, which leads to on-street parking at the present time. She encouraged the Council to vote to deny the zone change. Russell James also spoke to the development of the property at 550 East 900 North. He is concerned about building another high-density project so close to elementary schools in the area. John Ray also discussed the property at 550 East 900 North; he discussed dangerous traffic issues in the area and noted the proposed project will make conditions more hazardous. Don Hughes also discussed the property at 550 East 900 North; he invited the City Council to personally visit the area to observe present conditions. Those that live in single family homes have tried hard to make the area a nice place to live and allowing this apartment complex will negatively impact those efforts. He acknowledged that the decision the Council is being asked to make is a very hard one and he asked them to seriously consider the proposal and the input provided by the residents.

column3: stated that the views she is expressing are solely hers as a citizen and they are not representative of any board or Sta
column4: Angel Castillo stated that the views she is expressing are solely hers as a citizen and they are not representative of any board or State committee she participates on. She stated the redistricting task before the Council is a very serious one and she is concerned about some of the discussions that have taken place thus far regarding the subject. It is important that this action adequately represent the citizens of Ogden and she is specifically concerned about rezoning east to west and incorporating the east bench into the east central community. She had a conversation with Weber County Election Official Ryan Cowley and he expressed that he is not pleased that he is 'under the gun' to prepare a redistricting proposal for the City to consider. They would have liked sufficient time to accept public input regarding the matter, but their timeline has been impacted by the State Legislature's timing of State-wide redistricting. The Voting Rights Act states that district lines should not be drawn to prevent minorities from having a majority and that the lines respect communities of interest as well as natural geographic or manmade boundaries. Part of the challenge is avoiding the creation of a disparity, specifically when considering the Ogden School District boundaries; mixing the east bench with the East Central Community will result in socioeconomic groups having diluted representation. She advised that Ogden City will be contacted by the Ogden branch of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) regarding this matter.

column3: stated that his comments are minor in comparison to those who have spoken about the construction project at BDO. His com
column4: Heath Satow stated that his comments are minor in comparison to those who have spoken about the construction project at BDO. His comments are regarding comments made about the City's Diversity Commission. During today' s work session he heard a Council member state that the Diversity Commission has a bias. He noted that nearly every committee has some sort of bias if someone chooses to perceive viewpoints as bias; the committees exist to share their views based upon their knowledge base. They have been appointed by the Mayor because of their expertise on specific issues, and this is expertise that the Council does not likely have. Each Committee is charged with a certain subject and the subject that the Diversity Committee has been charged with is meeting the needs of the diverse communities in Ogden. Nobody complaints about the bias of other committees and he suggested that the Council member concerned about the bias of the Diversity Commission consider his own viewpoints. If someone has a specific complaint about something the Diversity Commission shared with the Council, that complaint should be said directly, but just saying that the Commission has a bias comes across as racist. He stated he knows that is not the intent of the Council member who made the comment but complaining about a viewpoint being biased is not helpful or respectful to the Commission. Committees created by the City should be allowed to do the job they have been tasked with doing, and their conclusions should be respected and discussed. If someone feels the Commission is not doing their job properly, that needs to be addressed directly.

column3: stated he lives at 1271 West200 South in Marriott-Slaterville, and he echoed the frustration expressed by his neighbors.
column4: Jake Moss stated he lives at 1271 West200 South in Marriott-Slaterville, and he echoed the frustration expressed by his neighbors. The buildings have been built and he asked if the City has a plan for addressing the concerns and mitigating negative impacts, such as noise, light pollution, construction and huck traffic noise, and internet accessibility. He stated that the citizens of Marriott-Slaterville would like to work together with Ogden City, but it does not appear Ogden City feels the same.

column4: Janet Meyerhoffer stated she has lived on 1200 West for 33 years. She is devasted to lose the views of the mountains and to have the sunrise blocked. She is constantly looking at the mountains now and soaking in their beauty because she knows that view will soon be lost. A few years ago, she visited China and saw the depressing concrete buildings and dreary views and she thought how awful it would be to live in that environment. Now that is her reality. She loves to see the stars, but the light pollution from BDO blocks those views. She will miss seeing the little family of deer across the fence in the Nature Center. The value of her home has been lost. Even if she wanted to move, she would not be able to sell her home or to buy another home elsewhere due to the market. The quality of her life will never be the same and it is depressing and heartbreaking. She is mouming the loss of that quality oflife in the cmmnunity that was settled by her husband's great grandfather. She asked that the Council put themselves in the residents' shoes and try to understand how they would feel if that were what they had to look at every day.

column3: stated he lives on 1200 West in Marriott-Slaterville City, and he addressed the Council four years ago regarding his con
column4: Kerry Wayne stated he lives on 1200 West in Marriott-Slaterville City, and he addressed the Council four years ago regarding his concerns about the impact that commercial development at Business Depot Ogden (BDO) is having on the Ogden Nature Center. Now, he is concerned about the construction of warehouses along 1200 West that are less than four car lengths distance from the homes across the street; the residents living on 1200 West were not notified of these projects. He stated it is hard for his family to not be emotional about the history of the MWC facility and he wondered if the problems that have occurred are a result of a lack of caring from career bureaucrats. His family and the community have been patient for the past 54 years while they have waited for improvements to the facility, and he reminded the elected officials of the City that the citizens are their boss.

column4: Sean Bishop stated that since moving to Ogden he has heard about the MWC and what is and is not happening there; he is a member of the MWC Advisory Committee but speaking on his own behalf. He urged the Council to review the submissions from the Committee regarding so many different subjects and vital issues at the MWC. He grew up in Delta and Riverton Utah and leamed to swim at the West Millard Pool, which is a County funded pool. He took karate, dance, and theater classes at another public facility in Riverton; these programs not only changed his life but saved it. As a young queer person, he struggled to fmd friends and to stay away from dangerous activities and his life was bettered by access to valuable programs. He expressed his willingness to speak to any member of Administration or the Council about the recommendations made by the MWC Advisory Committee; their original repmt was submitted on March 31, 2021, and only now they are hearing that the information provided was not good enough and there has been no specific instruction on different expectations for the Committee.

column3: commented in the disrepair at the MWC and stated that the situation is due to the inaction by the City Council and Mayor
column4: Sebastian Benitez commented in the disrepair at the MWC and stated that the situation is due to the inaction by the City Council and Mayor; this Administration has not cared about the MWC for the past 10 years and so many are saddened that the building has essentially been destroyed because of a lack of funding for needed maintenance and improvements. He will continue to fight for action at the facility and stated he wished there was greater leadership in the City.

column3: stated that the City treats its citizens as bad as they treat residents from other cities; not one person from the City
column4: Shelly Kautzman stated that the City treats its citizens as bad as they treat residents from other cities; not one person from the City Council has contacted any resident from Marriott-Slaterville to discuss their concerns. She discussed the demographic of her neighborhood and expressed the manner in which they have been impacted by the project at BDO; she is ashamed of the entire Council for their behavior responsive to this project, with the exception of Council member Lopez. She stated that nearly every household in her neighborhood has been touched by cancer because of the contamination of the soil in BDO and that contamination being disturbed in recent years. Upon the plumes being opened up, there was a drastic increase in respiratory disease and illness in her neighborhood. She welcomed the Council to come to her house and smell the air for themselves and try to understand how the residents are impacted. Additionally, the people who will be working in the new buildings will face the same impacts of the residents.

column3: stated this meeting reminds her of a similar situation related the Jefferson School; there were public meetings about th
column4: Shirley Miller stated this meeting reminds her of a similar situation related the Jefferson School; there were public meetings about the future of that school, but decisions had already been made before those meetings were held. The kids that attended that school were separated and sent to five different schools, which negatively impacted them because of prejudice of the teachers and administrators against the Black, Hispanic, and poor white children. Children in the community are still treated differently and this is largely due to the Utah culture; the children who were treated poorly in their youth will remember that for the rest of their life and she asked that Ogden City stop this cycle by doing the right thing with the MWC.

column3: stated he is a professor at the University of Utah in the Deparhnent of Parks and Recreation and Tourism and is a Recrea
column4: Steven Bell stated he is a professor at the University of Utah in the Deparhnent of Parks and Recreation and Tourism and is a Recreation Therapist by trade; he is present to address the Marshall White Center (MWC) facility in the City. He has reviewed the Master Plan for the City, which indicates that development of tax exempt and vacant land will likely have the greatest impact on City revenue and work toward reducing the projected 2040 deficit of$10 million. He stated the Jefferson Avenue area of Ogden City needs attention and the MWC is the hub of that area of the City. The Master Plan also states that growth must be balanced to ensure land values increase in the core and not pulled the periphery of downtown. He stated recreation is a conduit for social health and residential improvement. He stated that 1,100 surveys were completed about the project and there is much interest in the subject matter; the City needs someone who knows about building recreation centers. Ogden City needs a state-of- the-art recreation center, and he suggests that project be completed at the site of the existing MWC.

column3: stated she planned to talk about transparency tonight, but it is clear to her that the Mayor has not been transparent re
column4: Suzanne Davis stated she planned to talk about transparency tonight, but it is clear to her that the Mayor has not been transparent regarding the MWC. So, she decided to talk about institutional racism, for which she provided the defmition: policies, practices, and procedures in an institution that have a disproportionately negative effect on racial minorities, access to quality of goods, services and opportunities, while advancing the larger white community. She stated the MWC has been a recreational center for 50 years; it has been a community center and a cultural center and now that it has reached its useful life, she believes the City is saying that the neighborhood is not worthy of a $30 million investment. It is hard for white people to see institutional racism, but she implored City officials to educate themselves on the matter as it appears that is what is happening in the City.

column3: stated that he would also like the Council be aware that Weber State University (WSU) has conducted four focus group mee
column4: Tad Barnett stated that he would also like the Council be aware that Weber State University (WSU) has conducted four focus group meetings on the MWC to address the cmTent interest in the planning of a recreation center project; their meetings are recorded and publicly available. Two focus groups included parents and the other two included teens, all of which live in inner- Minutes of Special Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, November 9, 2021 Page 371 City Ogden. They spoke to the demand for the classes but indicated that teachers were not always available. This is because staffmg is inadequate, and this is an additional matter that should be addressed.

column3: stated that this Council and the Mayor seem to have an obsession with ceremony; he frrstnoticed this when he was appoint
column4: Taylor Knuth stated that this Council and the Mayor seem to have an obsession with ceremony; he frrstnoticed this when he was appointed to the City's Diversity Commission in 2015 or 2016. In the six years he has served as a member of that Commission, there have been nine resignations due to the obsession with ceremony; they felt the Commission was under- resourced and they had no authority. They were essentially set up for failure and that is exactly what the Council has done with the MWC Advisory Committee and any other advisory committee that has been created. The committees are filled by volunteers who perform meaningful work for free only to have their work disgraced and ignored. It is shameful that the City has a facility named for a fallen police officer, but it has been allowed to fall into such disrepair and that many areas have been closed and cannot be reopened. He has spent so much time talking about how special Ogden City is and how it is a place where everyone belongs, but it is all ceremonial as the Mayor and Council have ignored the recommendations that have been made. In fact, may advisory bodies are openly disrespected in Council meetings and a few weeks ago, Council member Hyer indicated that the Diversity Commission was unfair and biased. It is incredibly disheartening to observe how the Council operates and the fact that they cannot listen to the people who have expressed their feelings.

column3: offered suggestions for improving communication between the City and its residents. She has tried to learn more about th
column4: Ava Barnett offered suggestions for improving communication between the City and its residents. She has tried to learn more about things that are happening in the City and relay that infonnation to her neighbors. Specifically, her neighborhood has been impacted by the BRT project, but there has been little communication from the City or UTA about the construction schedule and when they will be experiencing serious impacts, such as no access to water. It is important for the City to pursue other communication channels, especially for those who do not use the internet and social media. Increased opportunities for connecting could be advettised on City publications and on the website; if a phone number were advertised for residents to contact to provide feedback, that would be very helpful. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, December 7, 2021 Page 398

column3: stated he wanted to take a moment to acknowledge that on this date, 76 years ago, Joe McQueen blessed
column4: Daniel Mathews stated he wanted to take a moment to acknowledge that on this date, 76 years ago, Joe McQueen blessed Ogden City with his presence. Sadly, two years ago, also on this date, Ogden lost Joe McQueen. It is ironic that the City honored Farr's Ice Cream tonight as it was one ofMr. McQueen's favorite places and he suggested making spumoni ice cream the official ice cream flavor of Ogden city as it was Mr. McQueen's favorite. He stated one of Mr. McQueen's quotes is to "be selfless instead of selfish; in every moment there is a gift if you are open to it." He encouraged everyone to carry the spirit of Mr. McQueen with them to honor the contribution he made to Ogden. He then thanked the member of the Council that have expended effort to Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, December 7, 2021 Page 397 become part of the conversation about the Marshall White Center (MWC). This is an issue that is very important to the community. He thanked Council member Choberka for speaking at an event last Saturday and thanked Council members Nadolski, Lopez, Stephens, and Vice Chair White for attending. He also thanked Chief Administrative Officer Johnson for attending and fielding questions about the facility. It is obvious that Ogden is spending a lot of money on meaningful projects and residents should pay close attention to that spending and the prioritization of certain projects. He also encouraged members of the community to check out the City's Master Plan that was created in 2016 to learn the City's vision for the MWC facility. Heath Satow referenced tonight's work session discussion about the City's acquisition ofhomes for refurbishment. He inquired as to the realtor the City uses for those transactions and if the same realtor is always used. He then noted that there is a quick movement on restricting silent protesting in the Council Chambers and he wished there had been as much attention given to the MWC when it was first obvious that something needed to happen. He stated that Executive Director Eller-Smith indicated that a couple of Council members had complained about the silent protest signs being used during Council meetings and it would be helpful if those Council members would identify themselves as it is important for that information to be part of the public record. He then cited Mayor Caldwell's attendance this evening after having been absent to important events over the past three weeks, including the very important community meeting regarding the MWC. Mayor Caldwell sent a City employee to many of these events, and in the case of the MWC meeting, that City employee 'took the heat' that the Mayor should be taking from the community. He stated he has literally never seen Mayor Caldwell show up for something where he would be faced with answering questions from the public. Tonight, would be a great night to show leadership on the MWC issue and he asked why the City is paying him $18,000 a month for salary and benefits when he does not show up to events and does not answer or respond to phone calls and emails. It is an open secret that Mayor Caldwell has decided this will be his last term in office and he seems to have a case of'senior-itis'. If any other City employee was absent as much as the Mayor, they would no longer have a job. There are real issues in the City and the Mayor's refusal to lead in response to those issues is very upsetting. He asked that the Mayor lead the City in a meaningful way or stop accepting taxpayer money for his salary. Angel Castillo relayed her own personal story ofFarr's Ice Cream and stated she appreciates that the City recognized the business as a legacy business. She then echoed the gratitude expressed to certain Council members for their engagement with the community and participation in the recent community meeting regarding the MWC. She then referenced Mr. Hutchinson's comments about safety issues in his neighborhood, noting that the size of the City's police force has not kept pace with growth. The City is not getting the type of policing it deserves because the City has not prioritized things that are important to the community. The City could use Business Depot Ogden lease revenue to support the Police Department, renovate the MWC, and use as grant matching funds for vital infrastructure. She stated that the most important thing is giving the community the recreation center that it deserves at the current location of the MWC. Taylor Knuth first echoed the sentiments expressed by Ava Barnett regarding the Capital Square project and safety concerns for residents in the East Central neighborhood. He agrees that the lack oflighting in public areas is problematic and there has been little to no action responsive to other safety concerns. He stated that the City has hired a community engagement liaison to meet with residents of this area of the City specific to Utah Transit Authority's (UTA) Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project, but that individual has not once knocked on his door to engage him. However, Mr. Knuth has contacted the consultant several times to discuss this impacts that he is experiencing due to the BRT construction in the area, with no response. He encouraged Administration to detennine if that consultant should be getting paid as he is not performing the services intended. He then referenced the MWC project and also thanked the Council members who attended the community meeting regarding the project. He left that meeting with a little bit of hope that the City will do right by Marshall White by building a world class facility at the present location of the MWC. A comment made by Council member Lopez hit home with him and that is that there is a void of leadership under Mayor Caldwell and his Administrative team. He does not recall the last time the Mayor showed up to participate in any kind of community conversation. He added that when the Mayor has shown up at events, he has made comments about feeling like he was the chief complaint officer or in front of a firing squad. He encouraged the Mayor and his team to evaluate their commitment to community engagement and engaging the cmmnunity in authentic ways. He closed by expressing gratitude to those representatives of the City as well as community members who participated in the cmmnunity meeting regarding the matter Alicia Washington echoed the thanks expressed by others to Council members and Mr. Johnson for patticipating in the community meeting. The meeting was recorded, and a copy can be sent to any member of City Administration or the City Council. She looks forward to continued conversations about the project and she reminded the Council to lean heavily upon the volunteers that make up the City's Diversity Commission and the MWC Advisory Committee. Now is a good time to do right by Marshall White and his family.

column3: stated he lives on 28th Street east of Harrison Boulevard and he is speaking in representation of many of the people who
column4: James Hutchinson stated he lives on 28th Street east of Harrison Boulevard and he is speaking in representation of many of the people who live in his neighborhood. There is a huge problem with speeding and running stop signs in the area. He identified the locations of existing stop signs and varying speed limits in the area and stated he would like the City to consider a uniform speed limit of25 miles per hour throughout the neighborhood. He stated that he has asked that the area be patrolled, but he has been told that there are not enough patrol officers employed by the City. He stated that the area becomes more dangerous every day and every year, and it is necessary for the City to fmd a way to increase staffmg levels in the Police Department and to address the concerns of residents.

column3: thanked the Council for their continued discussion of the Marshall White Center and the proper project to proceed with i
column4: Angel Castillo thanked the Council for their continued discussion of the Marshall White Center and the proper project to proceed with in terms of creating a community center in Ogden City. The matter has been delayed for some time and the residents of the City have indicated they want action; now is the time to move forward. She then referenced a comment made by Council member Hyer during tonight's work session regarding the need for collaboration between Council leadership and City Administration relative to applying for ARP grants. This is a funding mechanism that could make it possible to move money around throughout the City to make the project happen sooner. All residents have paid taxes towards creating the ARP fund and it is appropriate for some of that money to be sent back to Ogden for such an important project. Heath Satow referenced current drought conditions and suggested the Council begin the work now to develop a water conservation plan for the coming growing season; this is a high priority as the forecast for summer of2022looks grim. He then thanked Council member Choberka for speaking up about the need to better address the growing unhoused population in Ogden; this ties into the lack of communication from Administration about the issue. While campaigning in 2019, Mayor Caldwell chastised Salt Lake City for the way they dealt with their unsheltered population and he played a clip of Mayor Caldwell's statement; however, in 2020, Ogden City was caught off guard by the use of the same heavy-handed tactics that were employed in Salt Lake City. This was in direct conflict with the Mayor's previous statement just a year prior. This is on his mind today because he drove by the Lantern House and saw a police vehicle parked on the street; he is not sure of the resulting interaction between police and unsheltered individuals, but last year the Mayor chose to uproot and scatter those individuals on the coldest night of the year. No one was ever held accountable for the violation of CDC guidelines and human decency, and he is concerned that history may repeat itself. He hopes that this year Ogden is prepared to do better than last year. Blair Mathews echoed the gratitude expressed to the Council for making the Marshall White Center project a priority. He had the opportunity to speak to one of Ogden's representatives in the Legislature to discuss access to ARP funds and he was told Administration needs to be the entity to request that funding. He encouraged the Council to lean on Administration to make the appropriate application for funding. He then thanked Vice Chair White for proposing consideration of a resolution aimed at prioritizing the Center. He then asked if it would be possible to dedicate the Center as a public art project similar to what was done earlier tonight with the BRT project. He concluded by discussing upcoming special events to be held in the City aimed at providing last minute shopping opportunities for residents. He concluded by asking the Council to look into a situation at the Fire Department; someone is being punished for being a medical cannabis patient and he does not think that is appropriate.

column3: stated he is present in representation of Indie Ogden, and he spoke about the December 19, 2021 Bizarre
column4: Daniel Mathews stated he is present in representation of Indie Ogden, and he spoke about the December 19, 2021 Bizarre Art Market. It was an honor to hold the event at the Marshall White Center (MWC) and during that time he had the ability to poll participants about their feelings regarding the MWC. He found the staff of the MWC to be phenomenal and very supportive and noted the energy of the building is palpable. The way the building has been maintained, however, is a slight to the residents of the City. He will continue to hold monthly events at the facility and look for ways to support the renovation project there. Angel Castillo again thanked the Council for expressing a willingness to consider renaming a City facility to honor Mr. Singh. It is very important to honor members of the community who are doing good work. She then thanked Council members Nadolski and Lopez for being willing to serve in leadership roles on the Council. Finally, she spoke to the importance of receiving the COVID-19 vaccine to help to stop the spread of the disease in the community. She asked the Council to help to spread the message of the importance of the vaccine and boosters.

column3: stated that he feels that the way Mr. Singh died does matter and should be taken into consideration when determining whe
column4: Heath Satow stated that he feels that the way Mr. Singh died does matter and should be taken into consideration when determining whether to honor him by renaming a street or facility after him. He looks forward to honoring this man who died while serving the community. He then congratulated Council members Nadolski and Lopez on being elected to serve as Chair and Vice Chair and noted he hopes this new leadership of the City Council will spend more time addressing community concerns, such as those expressed by the residents of Marriott-Slaterville. Also, he expects to see far more attention paid to the MWC and the needed improvements or reconstruction of that facility. Sebastian Benitez also expressed congratulations to newly elected and re-elected Council members and thanked them for the service they provide to the community. He also congratulated Council members Nadolski and Lopez on being selected as Chair and Vice Chair. He then encouraged Mr. Wayne to continue fighting for the residents of Marriott-Slaterville.

column3: addressed a meeting held last month regarding the issues that have been raised by Marriott-Slaterville residents regardi
column4: Kerry Wayne addressed a meeting held last month regarding the issues that have been raised by Marriott-Slaterville residents regarding a project on the western side of Business Depot Ogden. He thanked members of the Council and Administration for participating in the meeting but indicated he would have liked to hear discussion of solutions to problems and the idea of holding another meeting to continue discussing the matter. He cited dangerous road conditions caused by the buildings shading the streets making it difficult for snow and ice to melt from the roadway, inability of residents to access high speed internet, idling vehicles that are working on the construction site, and overnight activities that include bright lights. Hazel Nadolski congratulated the recently elected and re-elected members of the City Council.

column4: Jordan Silver stated he is a career pilot and regular user of the Ogden Airport for the past 18 years; he expressed gratitude for an operational airport in the City of Ogden, but he has been saddened to see the Airport deteriorate rapidly from a user-friendly place to conduct recreation business to an unpleasant, financially ruinous endeavor. He believes the current Airport management and the City Attorney are trying to effect positive change in the name of progress at the Airport, but he feels they are doing so with a secretive underhanded attitude that is accompanied by malice and greed. He has many complaints as follows: first, is the class action lawsuit between ORAA and Ogden City regarding illegal actions of Airport management and Ogden city including confiscation of private property, unequal enforcement of onerous and excessive hangar inspections, continuous failure to comply with grant assurances required for continued receipt of federal funds, unreasonably short land leases to current hangar owners, and unprecedent insurance requirements for aircraft and hangar owners. Second, efforts and massive tax dollar expenditures on attempts to bring large commercial operations to the Ogden Airport are ill planned and implemented and are currently failing. Third, rejection of proposed growth by uses like Foresight and the U.S. Forest Service, and others, would have brought revenue and jobs to the Airport; seeking to evict and render assets worthless for companies like Sky Dive Ogden, is problematic. Fourth, the Airport Advisory Board is consistently ignored by the City, has recently refused public comment at their meeting, and has a member with a conflict of interest as he is a manager of the federally contracted airport control tower. Fifth, air traffic controllers Minutes of Special Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, January 11, 2022 SESS SS SS a SS SS a ae oe eS SS a | eS ee, who are ruining user experiences and discouraging growth through harsh and negative interactions with pilots. Sixth, hoarding of aircraft tie down spots by the Airport and threatening impoundment. Seventh, use of actual Airport badge confiscation or limitation in a punitive matter, which is illegal. All of these issues are being discussed by pilots throughout the nation and the Airport is a joke throughout the industry. He will provide additional details in future meetings.

column3: thanked the Council for their adoption of the joint resolution regarding the Marshall White Center. He then discussed th
column4: Taylor Knuth thanked the Council for their adoption of the joint resolution regarding the Marshall White Center. He then discussed the Human Rights Coalition’s Municipal Equality Index Score; this was determined by conduction of a nationwide survey to determine inclusivity of the LGBTQ+ community. Salt Lake City received a score of 100, the highest score possible, but Ogden only received a score of 58. This is a result of the lack of non-discrimination laws preventing unfair treatment in the areas of housing, employment, and public accommodations as well as the lack of insurance policies that would provide coverage for domestic partners. The City does not have a LGBTQ+ liaison position in City Administration or the Police Department, which also contributed to a low score. He mentioned other factors, such as youth bullying and lack of community support. He encouraged the Council to consider this index score as a solid measure of success in future policy considerations. Council member White inquired as to the individual that completed the survey. Mr. Knuth stated that the Coalition’s website indicates that the survey was sent to the City’s Administrative Offices, so he imagines the City’s Diversity Coordinator completed the survey. Sebastian Benitez echoed the comments made by Mr. Satow about freedom of speech and the rights of individuals to display signs communicating a message. He strongly believes in freedom and does not believe that anyone’s voice should be restricted or silenced. Betty Sawyer also echoed the sentiments expressed regarding the possibility that the Council will enact restrictions that will limit freedom of speech and involvement in public discussions. There must be great care in passing policies, especially when no problem exists. According to the discussion during tonight’s work session, there has only been one or two problems in the last several years and it is problematic to create policy when no problem exists or when a problem is only created through rhetoric. There are ways to address the issue of signage without enacting policies that are unproductive. Angel Castillo praised Council staff for their efforts to increase transparency of Council actions through the creation of a podcast and streaming meetings on Facebook. Ogden City is leading while Weber County is not; she is very disappointed that Weber County does not stream their meetings whatsoever. She then stated that it has been so important to consider options for allowing residents to participate in meetings during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. She indicated Weber State University’s Stewart Stadium holds 17,500 spectators and there are currently 24,147 new active COVID cases in the State of Utah. She asked the Council to encourage their constituents to be vaccinated and receive booster shots; this is the only way of getting back to normal, which includes keeping kids in school and keeping businesses open.

column3: stated that she lives adjacent to the property at the corner of 25" Street and Porter Avenue, which was discussed during
column4: Cindy Toone stated that she lives adjacent to the property at the corner of 25" Street and Porter Avenue, which was discussed during tonight’s work session. She is very concerned about the size of the proposed mixed-use project that would be constructed on the property, and the depiction of the right-of-way on the conceptual plans for the project is not accurate. Porter Avenue is very narrow and cannot accommodate two travel lanes and on-street parking on both sides of the street. She is very concerned about additional traffic in the area and would prefer fewer units in the project. The Arts District Master Plan suggests a small one-story building on the site, which would be used by artists. She is concerned about the proximity of the proposed project to other historic homes in the Jefferson Avenue Historic District. Property owners there have made a substantial investment in their property, as has Ogden City, and she feels this proposed project would diminish the historic district. This is the third development proposal that has been made for the project, but it is the most dense and impactful for surrounding property owners.

column3: stated he is the individual who purchased the Brown Ice Cream Building in the Wonder Block project area. He has complete
column4: Dan McEntee stated he is the individual who purchased the Brown Ice Cream Building in the Wonder Block project area. He has completed approximately 12 projects in Ogden after purchasing buildings that were either abandoned or in other states of disrepair. He has invested his own funds and has never borrowed money from the City to complete these projects and he does not understand the disparaging remarks that have been made about the transaction related to the Brown Ice Cream Building. He purchased the building at fair market value, which was determined based upon the current condition of the building. He has created jobs and increased sales tax for the City without asking for tax rebates or cuts from Ogden City or Weber County. He felt it important to address the Council to dispel completely incorrect statements that have been made by others in the community. He deeply cares about Ogden and that is why he does what he does. Over the last 16 years, Ogden has gone through prosperous and difficult times, but the status of the City is one of prosperity which is largely due to the current Administration, staff, and City Council members.

column3: stated the residents who rely upon the services of the MWC and the Golden Hours Center could really benefit from access
column4: Daniel Mathews stated the residents who rely upon the services of the MWC and the Golden Hours Center could really benefit from access to those facilities. He encouraged the City to reopen the facilities in the safest way possible. He noted that other non-government facilities have remained open to serve their patrons. He asked Administration to explain why they are unwilling to pursue federal funds for the MWC project. He thanked the Council for taking action to communicate their plans regarding the MWC but noted the community does not believe the Administration or City Council has truly prioritized the MWC Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, February 1, 2022 or arecreation center in the heart of Ogden. This belief is based upon other actions regarding other projects that seem to be more important.

column3: stated he is aware of a second meeting between Ogden City Administration and the Marriott-Slaterville administration reg
column4: Kerry Wayne stated he is aware of a second meeting between Ogden City Administration and the Marriott-Slaterville administration regarding the project on the west side of Business Depot Ogden (BDO). He asked the Marriott-Slaterville City Administrator for a report of that meeting, and he indicated that no decisions were made, and nothing will be done. He sent a letter asking that a noise waiver for the project be terminated because work on the project is very noisy and is impacting residents across the City, but he has not received a response from the Mayor’s office. The residents of Marriott-Slaterville have tolerated a lot and they are being disregarded. There is a great deal of standing water and mud along the 1200 West roadway and The Boyer Company is ignoring it, though they have made sure that the buildings within the BDO property are well landscaped and maintained. He stated that claims have been made that the project is in line with longstanding plans for the area, but that is not correct. He then recited quotes about integrity and morality and concluded that Ogden City and The Boyer Company are not being good neighbors and do not have integrity. He asked for another meeting and for decisions to be made that will require The Boyer Company to be proactive in addressing the problems they have created. Heath Satow referenced a recent media article about the City’s efforts to secure financing for the $24 million parking deck in the Wonder Block project. This led him to believe that the City has made extensive plans and invested millions into the project long before having an idea of how to pay for it. Yet, when the Marshall White Center (MWC) project is discussed, the first response from the City is that it is necessary to figure out how to pay for the project before planning it. Administration has been presented with different funding opportunities, yet there has been no movement from Administration. He asked for an explanation of this contradiction. No one has mentioned how the parking deck will benefit all residents, though the MWC project will benefit all residents of the City. He stated it is important to be aware of these inconsistencies. Angel Castillo referenced the discussion in tonight’s work session meeting regarding municipal redistricting. There are many unintended consequences of this action, including rural areas gaining more control than urban areas of the community. She suggested the Council work with Jenny Gnagey of Weber State University, who is very familiar with the census tracts and the ethnic dispersion within those tracts. Her input could be used to determine the equity of the decisions to be made by the Council regarding redistricting. Drawing districts from the east to the west could dilute representation for various areas of the community, which will result in a great deal of conflict.

column3: stated she lives adjacent to the Porter Avenue property discussed in tonight’s work session. She echoed the concerns exp
column4: Lydia Gravis stated she lives adjacent to the Porter Avenue property discussed in tonight’s work session. She echoed the concerns expressed by Ms. Toone. She noted 10 years ago she leveraged her assets to purchase and renovate a home in the Jefferson Historic District. It has been a pleasure to live in the area, but she is now concerned about the project proposed for the corner of 25" Street and Jefferson Avenue. She appreciates the adjustments the developer has made to the project, but she does not feel it is enough as the buildings that will face Jefferson Avenue will still be very tall. She requested that the building heights be reduced. She has spent the last year working with the City on the Dumke Arts Plaza project and she does not believe that the proposed project on Porter Avenue will complement the Plaza and is not in line with the Arts District Master Plan. She encouraged the Council to think about the intentions of that Master Plan and whether developments proposed in the area compliment the desired uses in the area. She added she is also concerned about the increased traffic and the danger that will be presented to pedestrians in the area.

column4: Brown Ice Cream Building was sold three months ago; the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) was not consulted or even told about the sale. As members of the RDA, each Council member is aware that their original approval of the sale was based upon false information; they learned after the original approval that only one developer was contacted about the opportunity and that the City never performed a proper assessment to determine the accurate value of the property, and that they were presented a deflated value by a broker that was working on the developer’s behalf. The developer allowed the agreement to expire, and, in the meantime, property values skyrocketed in Ogden. Despite all of this, Administration proceeded to execute the original lapsed agreement without notifying any member of the Board. He does not know if that action is illegal, but he does know that it is wrong, and the Council should as well. City Administration promised the Council increased transparency, but they are not delivering on that promise. The Council is not even being shown basic respect in their role as members of the RDA.

column4: Kerry Wayne stated he lives in Marriott-Slaterville and in the last two weeks he received communication from The Boyer Company regarding their plans for proceeding with painting the new buildings and installing landscaping on the west side of Business Depot Ogden (BDO). Those activities have resumed, but the water and mud issues along 1200 West have not been remedied. He spoke to the Weber County Commission this morning and they will send their storm water inspector to the area to determine if there is a violation. He stated that if standing water issues continue, the mosquito population in the area will increase dramatically. He then noted that the noise waiver for the construction project was extended in October, and he asked that the waiver be revoked so that residents are not dealing with construction noise until 2:00 a.m. each evening. He stated that his next- door neighbor sold their home at a significant discount and will be moving this weekend; he expects that many other residents will be doing the same. He then referenced lighting of the buildings; lighting is still very invasive, and the lights never shut off during the day. He added that there is no security in the area even though the City and The Boyer Company can afford increased security measures to keep people from crossing the border between BDO and 1200 West to get onto private properties.

Other cities are already doing this to meet demand for housing in the State of Utah. She then addressed Vice Chair Lopez’s repeated request for a ‘dashboard’ tool that can be used to communicate the progress or status of certain projects the Council has asked for; this is important for the Council and the community as it is important that the Council is accountable to their constituency. column3: stated he is a stakeholder at the Ogden Airport; he referenced a meeting of the City Council on June 26, 2018. There is
column4: David Carlson stated he is a stakeholder at the Ogden Airport; he referenced a meeting of the City Council on June 26, 2018. There is a video of the meeting and at the one hour, 26-minute mark, City Attorney Williams addressed the City Council concerning the Airport land lease and fee increases. Mr. Williams indicated that the proposal was a one-time adjustment, which equated to approximately 25 percent, and that additional increases would be in line with the consumer price index (CPI). This would bring the Airport up to date and help cut into the Airport’s deficit. That sounded great at the time, even though the vote cost him a 225 percent increase in his land fees. The increases were first put into effect in 2019, but approximately 26 months later during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Council voted to approve a 100 percent fee increase. Basic owner fees have doubled and there is another 25 percent increase to follow next year. Mr. Williams told the Council a mistruth. He asked if the Airport is still running at a deficit. He asked if Allegiant Airlines is taking a break or leaving the City’s Airport. He asked if now is the right time to deny Airport land leases to people who have money and pay on time. The City is planning to tear down 27 hangars occupied by people who just experienced a rate increase, but are all paying their rent. He asked how much that will cost the residents of Ogden. He asked who will take care of the airline’s ground equipment after his own shop is bulldozed.

column3: spoke to his ongoing concerns regarding the development of the property on the west side of Business Depot Ogden (BDO),
column4: Kerry Wayne spoke to his ongoing concerns regarding the development of the property on the west side of Business Depot Ogden (BDO), which has been very negatively impactful to Marriott-Slaterville residents. The response from The Boyer Company has been inadequate and there continues to be mud and standing water issues, excessive dust that is landing on homes and properties in Marriott-Slaterville. The residents would like a timetable and some communication about things that the City and The Boyer Company plan to do in response to these issues. Alan Walker and Mike Miller discussed their efforts to build a garage in the area of 7" Street and Wall Avenue; they continue to encounter codes that prevent them from making the improvements they desire on their property. Metal siding is disallowed while vinyl siding is. They have applied for a permit, but it has taken a great deal of time to get adequate responses from City staff. Mr. Walker provided the Council with materials illustrating his concerns and the code amendments that he would like to see in order for him to proceed with his project. He concluded that he only wants to help improve the appearance of his neighborhood.

column3: stated she and her husband moved to Ogden 24 years ago from New Orleans; they now live on 25" Street and were surprised
column4: Rena Jordan stated she and her husband moved to Ogden 24 years ago from New Orleans; they now live on 25" Street and were surprised to hear that a builder there is executing plans for a five-story building. She cannot understand how such a tall building will fit into the historic nature of the neighborhood as there is no other building of similar height on or around what is an iconic street. Clearly at some point this project was approved and she is dismayed. The building will obscure her view, but she is more concerned about the integrity of the beautiful neighborhood. She hopes it is possible for the Council to consider some action that would address the matter.

column3: stated he appreciated the discussion during tonight’s work session regarding compensation for elected officials; he than
column4: Heath Satow stated he appreciated the discussion during tonight’s work session regarding compensation for elected officials; he thanked Chair Nadolski and Vice Chair Lopez for their willingness to accept reduced pay. He stated he agreed with the results of the study that concluded the City’s current Mayor and Chief Administrative Officer are significantly overpaid when compared to their counterparts in other comparable cities in Utah and, at the very least, he would recommend maintaining their current salaries rather than offering increases. While the Council has been responsive to concerns expressed by residents, the Chief Administrative Officer and Mayor have not, despite being paid more than all Council members combined. The lack of response to the residents of Marriott-Slaterville is an example of their utter apathy for anything that does not benefit them or their ‘developer buddies’; they can continue to try to blame previous administrations, but the problems at BDO are their responsibility and they cannot continue to ignore it. He stated he can guarantee there will be no meaningful response from the Mayor tonight and he encouraged the Council to maintain pressure on the Mayor and Chief Administrative Officer to meaningfully address the concerns of residents who have been seriously harmed in the name of profit for Ogden City; he referred to the profit as ‘blood money’. Angel Castillo agreed with Mr. Satow’s comments about compensation matters. She then referred to a federal website that provides information about local government interactions. She stated that the website indicates that a single well-spoken public comment may carry more weight than a thousand formal letters. The Ogden City Council has been addressed by children who have made important comments and the Council has commented on their bravery for coming forward. The Council knows how difficult it is to get people to become engaged and she asked that they consider that when hearing from Marriott-Slaterville Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, April 19, 2022 residents. The Council can take control of the issue by utilizing their authority over the City’s annual budget; the Council can refuse to fund something in order to demand that the Administration directly address what is happening in Marriott-Slaterville City. It is now time to mitigate the mess on the west side of BDO; residents are becoming frustrated and angry due to the fact that they are not being heard.

column3: spoke to the ongoing concerns from Marriott-Slaterville residents regarding the continued development on the west side o
column4: Kerry Wayne spoke to the ongoing concerns from Marriott-Slaterville residents regarding the continued development on the west side of Business Depot Ogden (BDO); he referenced infrastructure problems, landscaping issues, and failed communications between Ogden and Marriott-Slaterville elected officials and The Boyer Company. The residents would like written communication of the improvements to be completed and a timeline for the improvements. Chad Jones echoed Mr. Wayne’s comments; he gets the feeling that the Council simply thinks that the Marriott- Slaterville residents are just complaining, but they are frustrated and the main reason for that frustration was the lack of information provided to them regarding the projects to be completed on the west side of BDO. He and others believe they are entitled to some form of compensation from The Boyer Company about the damages they have suffered, and he asked for the help of the Ogden City Council to hold The Boyer Company accountable.

column3: stated he also lives on 1200 West, and he agrees with the comments that have been made; there is not necessarily a lack
column4: Kevin Layton stated he also lives on 1200 West, and he agrees with the comments that have been made; there is not necessarily a lack of accountability, but rather a lack of will to do the right thing on the part of Ogden City and The Boyer Company. He stated his view of the mountains is gone and every morning he wakes up to a 45-foot-tall echo chamber. He referenced the earlier recognition of Mike Slater of the Ogden Fire Department; he stated that Mr. Slater grew up in Marriott- Slaterville and was the best friend of his son in his youth. He stated he knows that Mr. Slater would defend the residents of Marriott-Slaterville in this situation.

column3: stated she listened with interest to the discussions earlier in the meeting regarding the redevelopment of the old Wangs
column4: Lori Slater stated she listened with interest to the discussions earlier in the meeting regarding the redevelopment of the old Wangsgard’s grocery store site. Many are concerned about the quality of the development as there is a great deal of history at that site. The same is true with BDO, which was redeveloped from an old military installation, and she asked if any member of the Council has driven to the western side of the project area to gain a personal understanding of the feeling that the new buildings create across the street from residential properties. The buildings are 45 feet tall and the one in front of her home spans the length of five properties. She asked the Council to imagine if someone came into their neighborhoods and built a similar building. She stated she has been in her home for 21 years and it sits on property that was formerly farmed by her grandfather. The property now houses 18 homes and the value has been destroyed. The buildings block the sun and 1200 West ices over in the winter, which makes the area very hazardous for residents and motorists. She stated that the City of Ogden had an opportunity to do something great on the property, but they chose to allow The Boyer Company to pursue a project that is harmful to the City’s neighbors in Marriott-Slaterville.

column3: stated that he also lives in Marriott-Slaterville, and he thanked the Council members who attended the community meeting
column4: Monty Stokes stated that he also lives in Marriott-Slaterville, and he thanked the Council members who attended the community meeting regarding the BDO project; he also thanked his neighbors who are continuing to address both Ogden City and Marriott-Slaterville to try to pursue appropriate action. He thanked the Marriott-Slaterville mayor for writing a very articulate letter to both governing bodies as well as the State Legislature; it detailed the problems created by the project, but no response has been provided. He then echoed many of the comments made by residents of Marriott-Slaterville; the walls have created an echo chamber for residents, lighting is very intrusive, the buildings are not aesthetically pleasing whatsoever, and the view of the mountains is completely blocked. He asked for neighborly cooperation to help address the situation.

column4: Sebastian Benitez stated he has made his home in Ogden City and the United States because he believes in justice for all. He implored the Council to listen and to act appropriately.

column3: stated she is also a Marriott-Slaterville resident, and she echoed the comments made by Mr. Wayne and Mr. Jones; she spe
column4: Yvonne Long stated she is also a Marriott-Slaterville resident, and she echoed the comments made by Mr. Wayne and Mr. Jones; she specifically focused on the disturbance of toxic dirt in the area upon which the new buildings have been constructed. A huge cement wall has been erected, which she refers to as the ‘great wall of 1200 West’. She and others are frustrated that their questions and concerns have not been answered. She noted she has lost her internet service because of the construction, and she desperately needs it due to medical issues in her home. She is on a fixed income and should not be forced to pay for more essential services because of the work done at BDO. She asked if the City’s planning staff and City Council were even aware of the project before it commenced.

column3: stated that leadership is very important and she spoke to Council’s consideration of appointing Brandon Cooper to serve
column4: Angel Castillo stated that leadership is very important and she spoke to Council’s consideration of appointing Brandon Cooper to serve as the City’s Community and Economic Development Director, which will be acted upon later this evening. She indicated that Mr. Cooper does not live in Ogden and is not invested in the community; in fact, he was considering employment in another city recently. She recommended the Council hire a consultant to evaluate the Department to determine what is lacking, provide training, and build a succession pipeline for thoughtful and sustainable economic development in the City.

column3: stated that the Community and Economic Development Director position is the second most powerful position in the City, a
column4: Heath Satow stated that the Community and Economic Development Director position is the second most powerful position in the City, after the Chief Administrative Officer position; the Council is considering Mr. Cooper for a position that will oversee and direct hundreds of millions of dollars in deals during a time of massive growth. This why he recommends a vote of ‘no’ tonight, or at least to table the decision for a future date. He stated that Mr. Cooper addressed the Council recently about the Brown’s Ice Cream building redevelopment project and many of the statements he made about the project were false; the Council made a decision to use a certain developer based upon information that they felt was fully accurate and vetted. He noted that he talked to other developers who indicated they would have been interested in the project and would have paid at least six times more than the selected developer paid if they had known about it. Amazingly, the developer allowed that deal to expire and Administration and Mr. Cooper were informed of other developers. However, the Administration then chose to silently sign a deal without input from the Council. This was after property prices had exploded in Ogden City. He noted that Mr. Cooper told him directly that nothing that happened was illegal and if it is not illegal, it is not wrong. He does not believe this was incompetence as he feels Mr. Cooper is too intelligent to make such mistakes. He even suspects the order to slide the agreement through came from higher than Mr. Cooper’s office. This type of thing is exactly what erodes peoples’ trust in government. He stated this is likely not the first time something like this has happened, but the first time Mr. Cooper was caught. The meeting adjourned into Closed Executive Session at 8:11 p.m. The meeting reconvened at 9:28 p.m. Consideration of the appointment of Brandon Cooper as the Community and Economic Development Director for Ogden City Mayor Caldwell summarized his recommendation to appoint Brandon W. Cooper as the Community and Economic Development Director and he is requesting advice and consent of the Council. Mr. Cooper has experience and expertise in all aspects of redevelopment, contract negotiations, strategic planning, community outreach, and executive leadership. He is currently serving as the interim Director of Community and Economic Development. Prior to his appointment as interim director, Mr. Cooper served as Deputy Director for ten (10) years. Before coming to Ogden in 2007, Brandon worked as a serial entrepreneur, as well as a land acquisition/capital acquisition agent for a local development company. COUNCIL MEMBER HYER MOVED TO APPOINT BRANDON COOPER AS THE COMMUNITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR FOR OGDEN CITY. VOTING NO-— CHAIR NADOLSKLI. Chair Nadolski indicated that his vote should not be considered a reflection on Mr. Cooper and he thinks Mr. Cooper is a great guy. He is uncomfortable with the contract that has been proposed for Mr. Cooper’s employment conditions as he feels it sets a bad precedent for other Department Directors. He feels that there is an issue with management above Mr. Cooper and that is why he requested the contract, but he is still uncomfortable with its terms. His ‘no’ vote is not a vote against Mr. Cooper, but against the circumstances surrounding this situation. He looks forward to seeing Mr. Cooper do great things for Ogden City. column4: Kerry Wayne stated he is very supportive of Ogden Soccer and noted that he enjoyed hearing from that group earlier in tonight’s meeting. He added that Marriott-Slaterville’s Mayor has extended an invitation to meet with Ogden City elected officials and he has not received a response. He asked what the Council is willing to do to address the problems with the project that are negatively impacting he and many other residents in that area. He stated this is no way to treat people, especially neighboring property owners. If the Council would take action, it would not be necessary for him and his neighbors to continue to address them in person and via email.

column3: thanked Mayor Caldwell for his budget presentation this evening; she agrees that is so important to take care of the Cit
column4: Kim Buttschardt thanked Mayor Caldwell for his budget presentation this evening; she agrees that is so important to take care of the City’s employees. She loves living and owning a business in Ogden City and she believes those who are working to effect positive change in the community are part of something special. She is appreciative of the leadership of many different City employees and she is especially interested in Community and Economic Development; the difference in economic development over the past 12 years is unbelievable to her and that is due, in large part, to Mr. Cooper’s efforts. She stated that he truly cares about this community and she strongly supports the Mayor’s recommendation to appoint Mr. Cooper to the role of Director. Kim Bowsher also spoke to her experiences working with Mr. Cooper and stated she also supports the Mayor’s recommendation to appoint him as the City’s Community and Economic Development Director. She added she was impressed by the members of the Youth Council who addressed the Council earlier this evening. She then reminded the Council and residents that the annual Farmer’s Market season will commence soon; this is one of the projects that is part of the great improvements that have been and continue to be made in downtown Ogden. She believes the energy around those types of events have created great synergy. She acknowledged some negative input that has been provided through social media channels regarding some things that have happened in Ogden, but those who make those negative comments typically are not willing to get involved personally in helping to improve the City. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, May 3, 2022

column3: stated he is a business and property owner in the City; he is here to speak to the Mayor’s recommendation to appoint Mr.
column4: Nate Harbertson stated he is a business and property owner in the City; he is here to speak to the Mayor’s recommendation to appoint Mr. Cooper to the Director position. As a business owner, he has truly appreciated Mr. Cooper’s efforts and his staff. He has multiple employees and partners who also speak very highly of Mr. Cooper and he has never heard negative feedback about him. He stated he has worked with Mr. Cooper’s predecessors and it has been his experience that Mr. Cooper’s efforts have resulted in greater growth and positive improvement in the business community. Mr. Cooper knows the community development job better than any other Director that he has worked with and it would be a waste of community resources to not appoint him to the position.

column3: addressed the proposed Fiscal Year (FY) 2023 budget and, more specifically, the use of American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) f
column4: Angel Castillo addressed the proposed Fiscal Year (FY) 2023 budget and, more specifically, the use of American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding. She asked why Administration did not take advantage of the one-time $25,000 bonus for first responders; this would have made it possible for employees to buy a home in Ogden or make otherwise investments on their own behalf. She also discussed the adjustments to the HOME program and noted she wished the City would have used available funding for rent relief. She urged the Council to look into this matter further as there is funding available for rent relief that can truly benefit residents of Ogden City. Sebastian Benitez echoed the comments made by Kerry Wayne and he encouraged the Council to hold City Administration accountable to fulfill the promises that have been made to the residents of Marriott-Slaterville City. He stated that Ogden City deserves a new mayor, and he referenced public information that can be reviewed to prove the Mayor has broken rules and told lies in the development of the proposed FY2023 budget. He is very upset with Administration and will stay involved throughout the budget process to provide information in support of his claims.

column3: thanked Ms. Buttschardt for her commitment to Ogden and for continuing to invest in the community by way of operating ex
column4: Heath Satow thanked Ms. Buttschardt for her commitment to Ogden and for continuing to invest in the community by way of operating existing businesses and opening new ones.

column4: Kim Buttschardt stated she has been interested in Ogden operations for a great deal of time and she was happy to hear from the Diversity Commission this evening regarding very important issues in the community. She offered congratulations to those that were acknowledged at the beginning of the meeting and spoke of her personal knowledge of the contribution that Tina and Tony Chen have made to the community through their operation of Tona Sushi Bar.
