column4: Richard Williams stated that on the 28" of April 2022 he submitted a proposal to the City Council to consider alternative water sources and he has not received a response. He submitted the same proposal to Box Elder County and Weber County and received a response. He stated that he is a resident of Ogden and the elected officials work for him; he is concerned by the lack of response to responsible and serious proposals. He does not feel the City government is responsive and has, instead, gone rogue. He stated that people do not trust their government because government does not respond or answer questions. He stated that if the City needed more time to consider and respond to the proposal he made, they could have provided a response and indicated they needed additional time to consider the proposal, but that did not happen. He stated there were many technical things included in his proposal that warranted a response. Andrew Johnson referenced the Council’s action to rezoned property in his neighborhood and he inquired as to the public process moving forward regarding formal plans for development of that area; he is interested in additional opportunities to provide public input. Council member Hyer offered to speak to Mr. Johnson following this meeting to provide him with information regarding that process.

column4: Ed McKinney discussed recent difficulties that he and other hangar owners at the Ogden Airport have experienced. Many people have invested their own money and even retirement dollars to secure and improve their hangars and they are now being reclaimed and rented to other individuals. This is just ‘the tip of the iceberg’ in terms of the many problems that are occurring at the airport.

column3: stated the $5 million expansion of the TSA holding area at the airport is unwarranted since there is no airline located
column4: Jim Peterson stated the $5 million expansion of the TSA holding area at the airport is unwarranted since there is no airline located at the Airport; no airline will locate at the Airport given its current condition as no airline allows their aircraft to perform circling approaches and Ogden is a one-way-in, one-way-out airport. He cannot believe the Council would consider a $5 million investment into something that is not even viable. If the Council had contracts for a new airline to locate at the Airport, he could understand the requested funding and consideration of such a massive investment, but he cannot support the Airport Manager’s position of being glad the airlines have left so that he can build.

column3: commented on the important recognition items that were discussed at the first of the meeting. She then commented on her
column4: Kim Buttschardt commented on the important recognition items that were discussed at the first of the meeting. She then commented on her observance of the budget process this year and she offered a ‘shout-out’ to all the City’s Department Directors for the work they do and the valuable budget presentation they have provided. She also commended Comptroller Stout and Council Executive Director Eller-Smith for crafting budget presentation in a manner that the average resident can understand it. Angel Castillo relayed an experience she had on Memorial Day at the Ogden cemetery; there were many veterans in attendance at a special event at the cemetery and she spoke with some who told her that they had to move their Veteran’s Parade to North Ogden because they cannot afford a parade permit in Ogden City. North Ogden understands the importance of honoring those who have made the ultimate sacrifice and she was embarrassed and ashamed that Ogden would not waive a permit fee for such an important event. Heath Satow also commented on the recognition items at the first of the meeting and thanked Vice Chair Lopez for his efforts. He then addressed the City’s involvement in the redevelopment of the Brown’s Ice Cream Building. He has reached out to Council members who have failed to answer his questions about the failure of oversight and lack of transparency. The public deserves to know why the only developer who knew about the project was a personal friend of Mayor Caldwell as well as one of the biggest donors to his campaign. The public deserves to know why the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) was fed false information and misled into believing only one person was interested in the project. In a recent newspaper article about Brandon Cooper’s promotion to Community and Economic Development Director, Mayor Caldwell commented that the City has been open and transparent about all of its development projects. When asked about Mr. Satow’s concerns, Mayor Caldwell went on to say that he completely disagreed with Mr. Satow and that he did not think he had all the information. Mr. Satow stated that his issue has been that he does not have all the information because the Mayor has not been open and transparent. He is asking, yet again, for transparency. Given that all but one of the Council members agreed to an ‘golden parachute’ clause in Mr. Cooper’s employment agreement, which would afford him $200,000 if he is fired for virtually any reason, he would like them to ‘come clean’ with the information they have about the Brown’s Ice Cream building. He stated he is asking for transparency and reasoning for Mr. Cooper’s promotion and keeping the secret about why the project was given to a personal friend of the Mayor.

column3: stated her hangar at Ogden Airport is one of the newer ones; she and her husband have been involved in aviation for over
column4: Sherry Peterson stated her hangar at Ogden Airport is one of the newer ones; she and her husband have been involved in aviation for over 50 years and they have owned hangars in other cities. Most recently they were debating purchasing a hangar in Ogden or Afton, Wyoming, and they chose Ogden. Unfortunately, this was not the best decision for them. The City will take her hangar and either rent it back to her or auction it off to another user. She stated the Council needs to solicit input from people involved in aviation when considering these types of decisions. She stated she regrets building in Ogden due to this matter.

column3: discussed his interactions with the City’s Airport Managers over the past several years and spoke to some of the recomme
column4: Timothy Felker discussed his interactions with the City’s Airport Managers over the past several years and spoke to some of the recommendations he has made to those individuals about the importance of a contract being legal and binding; if language in a lease is improper, it is the writer of that lease who is responsible and liable for corrective action. The City wrote those leases and should now negotiate with those current lease holders to come up with a resolution to the issues that have arisen. He stated that the Council should be concerned about solving these problems as doing so is what is best for the entire City. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, June 7, 2022

column3: discussed ongoing drought conditions that are causing dry conditions on the hillsides surrounding the City and she sugge
column4: Angel Castillo discussed ongoing drought conditions that are causing dry conditions on the hillsides surrounding the City and she suggested the City make decisions early regarding fireworks restrictions so that vendors are aware of any restrictions before they spend money on fireworks that they may not be able to sell. She then stated she was shocked to hear comments about the Ogden Airport about the time spent mowing grass at the facility, especially during a drought. She asked why the City is spending money mowing grass when there are other options for using artificial turf or grass that is slow growing and drought tolerant. She then discussed the average home cost in Ogden City and stated this is an indictor that the City is not making effective efforts to promote housing affordability in the community. column3: stated that last week during the City Council meeting the Mayor called him a liar rather than publicly answering the que
column4: Heath Satow stated that last week during the City Council meeting the Mayor called him a liar rather than publicly answering the questions Mr. Satow asked him. All he is asking the City government to do is to make a public statement as to why the Brown’s Ice Cream project is ‘such a mess’. He read several statements that he declared to be fact about the project, relative to the marketing of the property, the developer that was selected for the project, the multiple false statements provided by City Administration regarding the project, the misstated value of the building, control over the project, the relationship between the City and the broker for the project, and the information that has been hidden from the Council. He stated that he is not claiming that anything illegal has happened because he knows that all actions that have been taken are legal under the laws governing redevelopment agencies. He is simply saying that he feels that greater transparency and accountability to taxpayers is needed. He asked that the Council and Mayor acknowledge the errors and move forward with developing policies to ensure something similar does not happen again.

column3: stated his comments are directed towards activities of the City’s Redevelopment Agency (RDA); he noted he does not belie
column4: Jason Reyneveld stated his comments are directed towards activities of the City’s Redevelopment Agency (RDA); he noted he does not believe the City should be in the business of real estate development. Rather, the City should be focused on enforcing laws, managing public utilities, and providing public safety. As a small real estate developer who has dedicated his entire life savings to acquiring land and building quality housing in Central Ogden, he has found it difficult to compete with the City and has noticed that private investors are not getting involved. He stated that Ogden City gives itself full benefits through bureaucratic processes that make it difficult or impossible for private developers to compete. The RDA buys land over the term of several years in order to assemble a large parcel that can be redeveloped. He stated there are many people who love this town and need to be given the ability to pursue redevelopment or new development that is not influenced by the RDA. Vice Chair Lopez asked Mr. Reyneveld ifhe has spoken to anyone in City Administration. Mr. Reyneveld answered no and indicated the only City representative he has spoken with about his concerns is Council member Richey.

column3: addressed Mayor Caldwell, noting he has sent several emails asking the City to address the dust that is being created at
column4: Kerry Wayne addressed Mayor Caldwell, noting he has sent several emails asking the City to address the dust that is being created at the project on the western edge of Business Depot Ogden (BDO), which is a great nuisance for Marriott- Slaterville residents living near the facility. He stated something needs to be done as the City should not be immune from abiding by its own ordinances. He provided photographs of the current dust conditions and noted that Ogden City, The Boyer Company, and Marriott-Slaterville are not responding. There is no reason that Ogden City cannot be a good neighbor to the Marriott- Slaterville residents. The residents are looking for a schedule of when Ogden City officials will meet with them and address the problems; he no longer knows who to call about the problems in the area, but Ogden City needs to be responsible for their property and cannot hide behind The Boyer Company. He stated The Boyer Company is installing landscaping in the area, but they are not using dust control methods. The residents have been waiting 16 months without any action from Ogden City.

column3: stated that he would like to talk about renewable energy; it is important to be visionary in planning and preparing. He
column4: Wilson Tolman stated that he would like to talk about renewable energy; it is important to be visionary in planning and preparing. He spoke to the geographical issues the community faces regarding developing renewable energy sources, but one option Weber County, Ogden City, and the State of Utah can embrace is public transit.

column3: stated that she was happy to hear from the representatives of the Imagine Ballet Theater; they did a great job represent
column4: Angel Castillo stated that she was happy to hear from the representatives of the Imagine Ballet Theater; they did a great job representing the theater and are an example of why the City’s arts grants are so important. She then thanked the Council for their approval of the ordinance to provide funding for the Water Conservation Program in the City. She thanked Council member Choberka for her relentless efforts to pursue creation of and funding for that program, which will benefit the community for years to come. It is important for the Council to consider ongoing funding mechanisms for the program in future budget years. Heath Satow echoed Mr. Wayne’s request for a response from the City regarding the issues that he and his neighbors are dealing with. He stated that Mr. Wayne has been mistreated during City Council meetings, as well as outside of those meetings through the inaction of the Mayor, City Administration, and the City’s private partner at Business Depot Ogden. He commended Mr. Wayne for being levelheaded in the way he has addressed the City and he was upset that Mr. Wayne was chastised for the manner in which he addressed the Mayor and Council during the City Council’s meeting last week.

column3: stated that he planned to address Mayor Caldwell, but he will address Chief Administrative Officer Johnson instead; he n
column4: Kerry Wayne stated that he planned to address Mayor Caldwell, but he will address Chief Administrative Officer Johnson instead; he noted that over the last seven days there have been four wind events. When he left here last Tuesday after being assured that The Boyer Company was handling dust mitigation at the project on the western edge of Business Depot Ogden, he was met with a wall of dust from across the street from his home. He mowed his lawn over the weekend and there was so much dust that he ended up with a nosebleed. He has sent a note to the Mayor but has not received a response. He asked what Department in the City is responsible for handling his and others’ complaints and what is being done to enforce ordinances and the agreements that have been made between Ogden City, Marriott-Slaterville City, and The Boyer Company. The residents want something done to protect them from the negative impacts of this construction project. He asked for an answer to his comments and the complaints. He stated that the City Council is responsible to ensure enforcement of the rules they have adopted.

column3: stated he lives near the Ogden River; during the last City Council meeting that he attended, Mayor Caldwell asked the re
column4: Wilson Tolman stated he lives near the Ogden River; during the last City Council meeting that he attended, Mayor Caldwell asked the residents to be kind during their interactions. He stated his request is that Mayor Caldwell also be kind and that he hire a driver and pay for that driver out of his pocket.

column3: stated he has been very interested in the flip-your-strip program; his park strip is 2,438 square feet and he has essent
column4: Danny Beatty stated he has been very interested in the flip-your-strip program; his park strip is 2,438 square feet and he has essentially flipped it after obtaining a land use permit. However, as of last Thursday, the program was not accessible by Ogden City residents because the program had not been formally created and he asked that the City reach out to Weber Basin to inform them of tonight’s action to approve the interlocal agreement; this will make it possible for him to continue with the program and applying for the incentive. He added that local nurseries have a great deal of information about waterwise landscaping. He then noted that Weber State University (WSU) is watering their grass during the day, and he suggested someone from the City reach out to their administration to help address the issue. He concluded that by removing the grass in his park strip, he removed 32 percent of his lawn, which will result in significant water savings.

column3: stated that he the President of the Ogden Regional Airport Association (ORAA) and past member of the Ogden Airport Advis
column4: Ed McKinney stated that he the President of the Ogden Regional Airport Association (ORAA) and past member of the Ogden Airport Advisory Committee and the purpose of his comments tonight is to share thoughts and suggestions from the ORAA Board about improving the Ogden Airport. He discussed the makeup of ORAA and their expertise and indicated that the current Ogden Airport Advisory Committee does not have similar expertise and experience, other than the Airport Manager, Mr. Garrett. He stated that Mr. Garrett has disregarded the input of ORAA and has even indicated they do not know what they are talking about when it comes to the Ogden Airport. He stated that is not true and ORAA is concerned about the risks associated with providing 24/7 access, which is one of the factors that airlines consider when making decisions regarding where to locate. The claims that have been made by Mr. Garrett regarding his ability to attract a carrier to the Airport are not supported by the market. The City Council and City Administration should reach out to experts to substantiate Mr. Garrett’s claims. He has reached out to Mr. Garrett’s former employer who indicated that Mr. Garrett ‘likes to row the boat by himself’; it should be concerning that Mr. Garrett has essentially removed all aviation experts and replaced them by laypeople with no experience. This gives Mr. Garett the opportunity to be the only source of truth and information, and this is concerning. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, July 5, 2022 Heath Satow also thanked the Council for approving the Water Conservation Program but suggested that the intent of the program be reconciled with other City development and redevelopment projects that include heavy water usage. He stated that he would also suggest that the City reach out to property owners who do not live in the community; they are unfamiliar with drought conditions, but they have large lawns that are being water irresponsibly. The same is true in the industrially developed areas of the City.

column3: stated that last year Weber County Patriot’s organization was involved in the City’s Pioneer Days parade; however, their
column4: Kathleen Hohash stated that last year Weber County Patriot’s organization was involved in the City’s Pioneer Days parade; however, their application to be involved this year was denied because last year their float was found to be offensive. She stated that last year her organization followed all of the rules of the parade and cannot determine why it was found offensive. The gentleman who wrote a letter to the City cited their use of the flag, and she is saddened that is the case. She stated that this year they participated in the Layton parade, and they were told they were too loud in their playing of Lee Greenwood’s God Bless America. She stated she will not apologize for the spirit of liberty and unity that her organization is promoting. She asked that the Council use their influence to reverse the decision to deny them from participating in the parade this year.

column3: thanked Mr. Herd for his work on the Water Conservation Plan and the Council for supporting the partnership with Weber B
column4: Kim Buttschardt thanked Mr. Herd for his work on the Water Conservation Plan and the Council for supporting the partnership with Weber Basin. She stated shed is a member of the Weber Basin Water Conservancy Board and she spoke to the efforts to install meters throughout the District. She agrees with the need to expand the program and the partnership between the District and the City to increase the amount of funding available for water conservation efforts each year. Angel Castillo also thanked the Council for approving the flip-your-strip program and agreed with the need to do more to improve water conservation efforts in the community. She then referenced the Council’s decision to deny the boundary adjustment with North Ogden City; she feels that decision was based upon inaccurate information, and she recommended that the Council review the Planning Commission recommendation and the fiscal information that was developed regarding the issue.

column3: addressed Council member Hyer’s comments at the first of the meeting regarding his annual reading of the nation’s foundi
column4: Wilson Tolman addressed Council member Hyer’s comments at the first of the meeting regarding his annual reading of the nation’s founding documents and he suggested review and consideration of an additional document asking citizens to rededicate themselves to sustaining constitutional rule of law. He discussed auditing the City’s financial position and does not believe there is an auditor position adjacent to the City Council positions and he suggested the Council consider creating such a position and hiring an internal auditor.

column3: stated she completely disagrees with the comments in support of raising wages for elected officials; Utah is a fiscally
column4: Angel Castillo stated she completely disagrees with the comments in support of raising wages for elected officials; Utah is a fiscally conservative State and that has served the citizens well. Utah Legislators work for a 45-day session and earn $12,825. The City Council members work 36 days. She stated she knows that the Council spends a great deal of time outside of meetings, but their job is not the same as the State Legislature and it would not be right for them to earn more than them. Being able to serve as an elected official is a privilege, but there are many residents with great value and perspectives who only earn $45,000 per year and could never spend additional time serving as an elected official. She stated it feels disingenuous for the Council to consider a pay increase for themselves.

column3: stated he is a past member of the Ogden Airport Advisory Committee and current President of the Ogden Regional Airport A
column4: Ed McKinney stated he is a past member of the Ogden Airport Advisory Committee and current President of the Ogden Regional Airport Association; last week he spoke to the Council about the lack of experience and education among the Airport Advisory Committee. He has offered to provide input regarding decisions being made about the Airport and the amount of money that is being spent there, but he has heard nothing back from the Council or Administration, which his very disappointing to him. He stated there is an Airport Advisory Committee meeting tomorrow at 6:00 p.m. and he encouraged City Council members to attend to understand what he is talking about and see what happens when the City appoints non-experts to an advisory position. He stated the current Airport Manager has indicated he will have the Ogden Airport at 90 percent of what the Provo Airport is within 18-24 months, and this is a very unreasonable goal.

column3: thanked the Council for having the courage to attend tonight’s meeting in person; he expressed disappointment that the M
column4: Heath Satow thanked the Council for having the courage to attend tonight’s meeting in person; he expressed disappointment that the Mayor was not in attendance. He then discussed environmental changes due to global warming and persistent drought conditions. He noted it is important for the City to put pressure on State leaders to consider policy addressing these matters. He then referenced tonight’s work session discussion regarding homelessness issues; Anna Davidson has been an incredible advocate for homeless individuals, and he wanted to remind the Council of actions taken by City Administration in December of 2020 to uproot homeless individuals living in temporary shelters. The response to his outrage was that he was overreacting, but after listening to Ms. Davidson tonight, it should be clear that the response by he and others was warranted. He disagreed with Chief Administrative Officer Johnson that other cities will eventually handle the overflow of homeless individuals and with the Mayor’s assessment that the City already has a sufficient amount of affordable housing; the City need leadership to address these issues and he suggested the Council work with the League of Cities and Towns to pursue legislation on these matters. David Timmerman also expressed support for participation in the CREP. The City conducted a public survey and 70 percent of respondents said they were supportive of increased access to renewable energy; 45 percent said they were supportive of achieving 100 percent clean energy via the CREP, compared to just 9 percent who opposed it. Ogden is one of 18 cities brave enough to participate in the program and together the communities will equal about 25 percent of Rocky Mountain Power’s total Minutes of Special Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, July 12, 2022 eee energy used, which is largely created by coal and gas extraction. He reminded the Council of the potential benefits and the low cost of participating in the program and encouraged the Council to reiterate their commitment to participating in the program.

column3: stated she is the newest republican nominee for House District 10; it is her goal to meet with all cities in District 10
column4: Jill Koford stated she is the newest republican nominee for House District 10; it is her goal to meet with all cities in District 10 in an effort to get to know them and communicate her excitement about working with them to solve the problems for residents.

column3: stated there are so many things that residents ask for in the community, but when their tax bill is presented, there are
column4: Kim Bowsher stated there are so many things that residents ask for in the community, but when their tax bill is presented, there are disagreements. She stated that Community and Economic Development Director Cooper has done a great job at creating the “Make Ogden” Plan, which includes information about cost and tax basis data, and it may be beneficial to provide similar graphics and messaging for the community at large. She added that with her role with the Ogden Downtown Alliance, discussions regarding her salary are awkward. She stated she is underpaid based upon a national study. She is 28 percent underpaid based upon State of Utah benchmarks and 67 percent underpaid based upon national benchmarks. While she has elected to not increase her pay, it is important to recognize the role that she and many like her perform. The same is true for the City Council members and she spoke to the important service they provide to the community. Kim Buttschardt echoed Ms. Carroll’s support for the CREP. She also echoed Ms. Bowsher’s comments about the importance of increasing wages for elected officials and other leaders. She stated she has attended City Council meetings since February and has gleaned a lot of great information through that participation; she thinks the Mayor and Council are doing a great job and she thanked them for the service they provide. Taylor Knuth echoed the comments made by Ms. Bowsher and Ms. Buttschardt; he believes that the City Council should be compensated fairly, and he would have been supportive of a four percent pay increase. He then discussed recent and ongoing fire events; there are currently five fires raging in Utah, costing taxpayer thousands of dollars. Most of them are caused by fireworks and the current fireworks restriction map is laughable; he encouraged the Council to deliberate the merits of a City-wide ban on fireworks, which will save the City a great deal of money. He has sent the Council an email about this subject and only received a response from one member; he has heard them pontificate about the importance of engagement with constituents, but he finds it incredibly disappointing that most of them did not take the time to engage with him and other concerned residents about this matter. He suggested the Council hire a constituent liaison on their staff who could engage with constituents about these types of comments.

column3: stated she is a resident of the third district of Ogden, and she commented on the importance of the City’s participation
column4: Lynn Carroll stated she is a resident of the third district of Ogden, and she commented on the importance of the City’s participation in the Community Renewable Energy Program (CREP); it will reduce two of the City’s biggest problems: global warming and air pollution. Joining with other communities in the program will cause Rocky Mountain Power to acquire more renewable energy at a faster rate; greenhouse gas pollution will also be reduced. She is looking for confirmation that the City still plans to participate in the program.

column3: stated he is actually in favor of a pay increase for elected officials, and he suggested tying the annual increase to in
column4: Tyler Kunzler stated he is actually in favor of a pay increase for elected officials, and he suggested tying the annual increase to inflation. He asked if the 24 percent tax increase to Weber County is equally distributed according to the pie chart included in Ms. Eller-Smith’s budget presentation; if so, he wondered what percent Ogden City was already receiving.

column3: stated the Utah Department of Transportation is gathering information about the idea of creating a full interchange at t
column4: Wilson Tolman stated the Utah Department of Transportation is gathering information about the idea of creating a full interchange at the 24" Street exit along Interstate-15; he is opposed to this project and has suggested the existing exits be removed. It is ridiculous to have so many exits within 10 blocks along Ogden City. He feels the City can spend its money more wisely and perhaps partner with other communities to fund an overpass over the 12" Street train tracks.

column3: stated he was not surprised by the Mayor’s defensive comments in the earlier Redevelopment Agency (RDA) meeting; residen
column4: Heath Satow stated he was not surprised by the Mayor’s defensive comments in the earlier Redevelopment Agency (RDA) meeting; residents have spoke up about flawed processes and the Mayor is unwilling to consider better processes that are being used in other communities. There is no interest in positive change and the Mayor only wants to keep things exactly how they are because everything seems to be working out quite well for him and his friends. He stated that it was revealed to the Council tonight that one of the members of the development team for the 2524 Wall Avenue project serves on a Board of Trustees for the Utah Sports Commission with Mayor Caldwell; but the residents have been told that this development proposal is random, and City Administration has no idea of how the developer found out about this opportunity. He suggested that the City record information regarding how developers learn of these development opportunities in order to better market Ogden to developers in the future. A level of transparency is very important when there is a perceived conflict of interest. The residents have been told that the property has been empty for decades with no interest from qualified developers, but he wondered if other developers would have been interested ifthey knew they could receive the property for free and receive $2.6 million in interest free financing from the City. He assumes just the subject development group was offered that deal; developers are not looking for hard to develop properties, and rather they are looking for the best deal. Someone offered this developer a deal they could not pass up, but that same information should be publicly advertised and accessible for all developers who are qualified to perform these types of projects. He emphasized competition is good for the entire community. He echoed Ms. Castillo’s comments about trying to keep low to moderate income individuals out of certain areas of the community; taxpayers pay to ensure that tax credits are available, and the City should have applied for them for this project or placed a restriction on a certain number of housing units. This is what happens when there is no oversight and little chance for public input on these types of projects. He asked when the public will see the changes to the development process; those changes have been in process for the last year with no new information. He is glad that the Council updates their rules and norms on a regular basis but asked when the last time was that they carefully reviewed the processes employed by the RDA as those are much more important.

column3: stated that he had the opportunity to review the Utah Transit Authority’s (UTAs) encroachment into the Jefferson Avenue
column4: Travis Pate stated that he had the opportunity to review the Utah Transit Authority’s (UTAs) encroachment into the Jefferson Avenue public right-of-way; a great deal of money was paid for infrastructure in that area, but UTA has been given blanket approval to destroy it. A new crosswalk and sidewalk were completed in the area just two years ago and it is already gone, lost to the placement of underground conduit for the UTA bus rapid transit project. He added that the light fixture at 26" Street and Jefferson Avenue still has not been changed. Additionally, any signage changes in the area are supposed to be submitted to the Landmarks Commission for their approval, but that has not happened. Citizens living in the historic district have carefully adhered to policies and guidelines for property ownership in the area, but the City, State, UTA, and other public entities haphazardly ignore those same policies and that is frustrating for the residents. Angel Castillo referenced the item dealing with the transfer of property to the RDA for a housing development at 2524 Wall Avenue; she provided living wage salary information for working class jobs in the community and indicated that these people will not be able to afford a housing unit in this housing project because the City refused to investigate the opportunity to secure low income housing credits for the project and/or place a restriction on the property requiring a percentage of the units to Minutes of Special Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, August 9, 2022 | be accessible for low to moderate income individuals. The statement that is communicated to the residents of the community is that ‘those people’ do not get to live in the heart of downtown Ogden. All of this is because the City is giving away property to a developer who made a proposal to the City without soliciting other proposals.

column3: thanked the Council staff for their efforts to make City Council meetings widely accessible through Zoom and YouTube bro
column4: Angel Castillo thanked the Council staff for their efforts to make City Council meetings widely accessible through Zoom and YouTube broadcasts. She was grateful to be able to participate in the 4:00 p.m. work session to give input regarding the developer selection process for RDA projects. She then addressed the ‘flip your strip’ program; if the City wants to encourage people to perform projects aimed at conserving water, it is up to the City to make sure that it is accessible to all taxpayers. Those who live in the private community referenced by Mr. Mueller are taxpayers who contribute to the community and if they are interested in creating a ‘model subdivision’ as he mentioned, they should be rewarded.

column3: stated he is a resident of Ogden City and a graduate of Weber State University (WSU); he has operated a real estate appr
column4: Don Mueller stated he is a resident of Ogden City and a graduate of Weber State University (WSU); he has operated a real estate appraisal business for the past 45 years in Ogden and he wished to address the ‘flip your strip’ program this evening. He lives in the Mountain Pines Subdivision, which is located at roughly 46" Street and Skyline Drive. He made an application as soon as the program was launched; he believes he followed all program guidelines, but his application was rejected, and he was Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, August 23, 2022 informed he would not receive a rebate. He is aware that the City has $100,000 available for rebates, along with a matching $100,000 from the Weber Basin Water Conservancy District. He acknowledged that his community is gated and private, but beyond those gates, there are yards, sidewalks, and park strips just like in every other neighborhood in the community and the residents that live there are very intent on saving water. The homeowner’s association (HOA) for the neighborhood has assessed every homeowner $1,800 to remove sod and install appropriate landscaping. The HOA was dismayed that their application was rejected because he knows that there is money available. He stated that after continued discussion with a City staff member, he was able to get approval for the section of park-strip along Skyline Drive, but he would like to make the entire subdivision a model subdivision for the community, and he hopes the City will consider amending the program to make funding available for private subdivisions.

column3: stated he was glad to hear the Redevelopment Agency developer selection process discussed during the work session this e
column4: Heath Satow stated he was glad to hear the Redevelopment Agency developer selection process discussed during the work session this evening. He agreed with Council member Hyer on anumber of the points he made during that discussion, but he believes this is only the beginning of the process; unfortunately, he sees little improvement coming from this discussion unless the City drastically increases the percentage of the projects that are widely advertised through a request for proposals (RFP) process. He appreciates the new requirement for the Board to be notified when the Agency enters into an exclusive negotiation with a party, but he truly wants to see more developers selected through a public process rather than a private process. The chart information that was presented to the Council tonight were somewhat misleading; no matter how the information is sliced up, only 20 percent of the properties that have been acquired using public funds have been publicly advertised to for proposals from developers to determine who has the best idea and will provide the best level of investment. He would prefer that each property is publicly advertised in order to ensure the best option for each property; the Board should value the properties more than they currently do. He concluded competition is healthy and should be encouraged.

column3: stated tonight he is here to thank the Mayor and Council for making a dream possible by completing the sidewalk around W
column4: Sebastian Benitez stated tonight he is here to thank the Mayor and Council for making a dream possible by completing the sidewalk around Wasatch Elementary; this will improve the safety of children that walk to and from the school. He thanked several individuals who were instrumental in bringing that project to fruition. He then stated that he would like sidewalk along Taylor Avenue between 32™ and 36" Streets, but for now he is grateful for the work that has been completed thus far.

column3: discussed the City’s activities at the Ogden Airport; starting in 2013, he began to create a plan for his retirement in
column4: Timothy Renee Felker discussed the City’s activities at the Ogden Airport; starting in 2013, he began to create a plan for his retirement in 2019 or 2020. His business relates to maintenance and repair of aircraft, and he purchased a hangar at the Airport to house his operations. He visited with the current Airport Manager to discuss moving the fence line near his hangar to provide public access to Airport Road, similar to arrangements for other hangars in the area. The Airport Manager told him that would not be a problem and that it could be worked out, but as part of that discussion they discussed hangar leases for the long-term and he learned that the City considered the residual value of hangars to be theirs and that lease renewals would be ending in the near future based on a ‘yet to be released’ plan. He stated he was shocked to learn this since the three previous Airport Managers had told him he would be able to renew his lease so long as he was meeting the terms of the lease. Shortly after learning this new information, he changed his business plan because he feels the hangar is critical to his success. He has spoken with other hangar owners and listed his hangar for sale, but the best offer he got was 50 percent of his asking price. His asking price was only slightly higher than his original investment in the hangar, which was $82,000 in 2014. He had always planned to get most of the money he had invested, if not all of it, back to fund his retirement. The way it looks now is that he will not be able to do that; Ogden City included a provision in his lease that requires the improvement to be removed within 60 days of the end of the lease. The City Attorney has stated in public meetings that the hangar owners would not take their hangars down, but that is incorrect, and he plans to take his hangar down.

column3: discussed historic preservation efforts in the Ogden School District in the last years; citizens have voted against bond
column4: Travis Pate discussed historic preservation efforts in the Ogden School District in the last years; citizens have voted against bonds that would have eliminated historic schools. But, when presented with a bond that would preserve and improve upon existing historic schools, the bond passed. Ogden City’s efforts should mirror those of the school district when it comes to opportunities to redevelop and improve historic buildings in Ogden’s downtown. He suggested that the fire prevention systems at various historic buildings be inspected to determine if improvements should be made to prevent devastating fires. He then provided information about the Art and Bloom event that will be held in downtown Ogden this weekend.

column3: thanked Council staff for their efforts to provide electronic means of participating in open meetings of the Council; sh
column4: Angel Castillo thanked Council staff for their efforts to provide electronic means of participating in open meetings of the Council; she is typically unable to attend the 4:00 p.m. work session meetings. Tonight, she listened to the meeting and paid careful attention to the discussion regarding the City’s receipt of $1.3 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds and the various entities in the community that should be eligible to receive a portion of that funding. She discussed the current operations of Your Community Connection (YCC) and stated they desperately need funding; they have been directly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and they are working to secure additional housing units for the clients they serve. She stated many people are purchasing housing units and using them as short-term rentals, so it has made it difficult for non-profits to secure available housing units. She recommended the Council consider crafting a grant program that will make the funding accessible for non- profits that truly need it. She then addressed the ongoing discussion of the proposed annexation of property that sits on the border between Ogden and North Ogden cities; she agreed that the City should not be simply giving land away to another community, but if an agreement is reached to allow that property to be annexed into North Ogden, the City needs to craft some type of agreement that provides for aesthetically pleasing design of the development project so that Ogden residents are not forced to live near the back of a building that is not pleasing to look at.

column3: presented the Council with photographs of deteriorating asphalt on 2™ Street near the Bingham Fort markers. He stated th
column4: Bob Giboney presented the Council with photographs of deteriorating asphalt on 2™ Street near the Bingham Fort markers. He stated that he feels the asphalt was not poured correctly or did not cure; it is more pea gravel than it is asphalt, and it is cracking and the conditions will only worsen over the coming winter months. The person who is responsible for the issue is ignoring pleas to improve/repair it, but other residents will soon be taking him to court regarding other problems he has created. Mayor Caldwell referred Mr. Giboney to City Engineer Anderson to discuss the asphalt conditions. Chair Nadolski thanked Mr. Giboney for his input.

column3: thanked Chair Nadolski for his continued support of youth sporting programs in the community and his efforts to keep the
column4: Heath Satow thanked Chair Nadolski for his continued support of youth sporting programs in the community and his efforts to keep the Marshall White Center project moving forward.

column3: addressed issues at the Ogden Airport; on June 28 the Council participated in a discussion with Airport Manager Garrett
column4: Jordan Silver addressed issues at the Ogden Airport; on June 28 the Council participated in a discussion with Airport Manager Garrett regarding the reasons that airlines are leaving the Airport. One reason he offered was the pilot shortage, which he acknowledged is real, but the actions of the Airport Manager and Ogden City regarding the revocation of hangar leases at the Airport have contributed greatly to the pilot shortage. The Ogden Airport has gone from a beautiful and thriving Airport where Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, September 6, 2022 a ______| general aviation has flourished to a dead airport. He issued a call to action to the City Council to reach out to people other than the Airport Manager to get correct information about the real issues at the facility. He stated he has a PowerPoint presentation from Heber City about similar things they experienced at their airport; they ultimately changed course to correct the negative things that were occurring at that airport and he recommended something similar in Ogden City. He wants to see the Ogden Airport thrive as it once did.

column3: thanked Council staff for making it possible for the public to participate in Council meetings via electronic means. She
column4: Angel Castillo thanked Council staff for making it possible for the public to participate in Council meetings via electronic means. She referenced tonight’s work session discussion regarding the Stock Exchange Building; she is pleased that everyone is concerned about historic preservation of buildings such as this one, but she was surprised to hear that the Council was asked to change zoning for the building without a rendering and scale of the project. The Landmarks Commission has expressed similar concerns about other projects in the past; without scale models, it can be difficult to determine the impact of a new building project or redevelopment. While these types of projects are needed to improve the economy of the City, they should be completed in a practical and respectful manner. She then noted that winter is coming, and the homeless population of the community will be freezing to death; she has not heard any recent discussions in the City about what will be done to protect them. She discussed the State’s use of available funding to provide aid to the homeless population and she suggested the City of Ogden have a work session discussion about proactive measures that can be employed to avoid situations that have occurred in the past. She would like that discussion to take place in a public meeting prior to the winter.

column3: thanked Council staff for providing the public with the opportunity to participate in open meetings of the Council via e
column4: Angel Castillo thanked Council staff for providing the public with the opportunity to participate in open meetings of the Council via electronic means. She referenced tonight’s work session discussion regarding new market tax credits. There seems to have been a breakdown in communication regarding the City’s ability to secure new market tax credits; though they are difficult to get, she believes that the housing development around the Marshall White Center (MWC) would qualify. She was contacted by the president of the Community Development Finance Alliance (CDFA), Amy Rowland, who indicated that she wants to put the MWC project in her portfolio; if her portfolio is not big enough to finance 85 percent of the project, she would partner with another CDFA to finance that amount. She does not know why Ogden City has not reached out to Ms. Rowland, though she has forwarded her contact information to City Administration. This is a company that is willing to give the city new market tax credits and she is disappointed that the City has not followed up on that opportunity. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, September 20, 2022 Kym Buttschardt highlighted the quality of special events produced over the past weekend by the Ogden Downtown Alliance (ODA); they have a tiny team of members, but they produce such high-quality events that contribute to the quality of life of the entire community. The ODA received support from the City’s Arts, Culture, Events Division, and this has become a beautiful partnership that has made Ogden shine. She is proud to be an Ogden resident and she publicly thanked everyone who contributed to such a positive weekend.

column3: stated that there will be a Dia de los Muertos festival this week at Ben Lomond High School; there will be many activiti
column4: Angel Castillo stated that there will be a Dia de los Muertos festival this week at Ben Lomond High School; there will be many activities at the festival, and she encouraged all to participate. She then noted that she has contacted the City’s Planning Division about the negative impact that the Utah Transit Authority (UTA) construction has been having on businesses in the community. She stated it is her understanding that UTA has funds to help support businesses, but the businesses she has spoken with have not heard of those benefits. She suggested that Council members reach out to the businesses in their district to help guide them in the right direction. She then congratulated the City’s housing authority on receiving a LIHTC project award; she understands the LIHTC program is very complicated and suggested the City Council familiarize themselves with the program because it can be a source of free money for vital projects in the City.

column3: thanked the Mayor, Council, and City Administration for the work they do for the community; he recognized that elected o
column4: David Willis thanked the Mayor, Council, and City Administration for the work they do for the community; he recognized that elected officials are often criticized and rarely get recognition for the work they do. He stated when he came to Ogden in 2006, the trajectory of the City was incredible and much of the great plans for the community have come to fruition under Mayor Caldwell’s leadership and support from the City Council. Improvements were made much quicker than he thought possible and in ways he never thought possible. He has lived in other large cities, such as Chicago, and has found their quality of life unsustainable; crime has increased, and public safety officials were not supported in those communities. He thanked Ogden City officials for recognizing the need to prioritize public safety in order to provide a great quality of life for the residents here.

column3: stated that the Union Stock Exchange Building was discussed during tonight’s work session meeting; he likes the develope
column4: Heath Satow stated that the Union Stock Exchange Building was discussed during tonight’s work session meeting; he likes the developer’s vision for the building, and he feels that it will provide a great boost for the surrounding area. He hopes the project goes forward as shown, but he is still concerned about the developer selection process employed by the City’s Redevelopment Agency; the developer of this project will be receiving very large perks funded by Ogden taxpayers and the City will essentially be buying the same piece of land twice. He referenced another project in Ogden’s downtown; an acre of property was given to a developer free of charge. There is a great deal of unknown information about the developer in that scenario and this is why it is important to demand increased transparency in the developer selection process.

column3: stated that he owns hangar 2808 at the Ogden Airport and he referenced commitments that have been made to the community
column4: Kelly Crozier stated that he owns hangar 2808 at the Ogden Airport and he referenced commitments that have been made to the community regarding the Ogden Airport that have never come to fruition. He noted the Airport Master Plan has a great deal of data and charts that are inaccurate and could lead to improvements that are not sustainable. Such improvements will not be supported by private carriers locating at the Airport and this will be a very negative situation for the residents of the community. He stated Ogden’s answers to these problems has been to get rid of its Airport Advisory Committee, which had over one hundred years of experience; old members have been replaced by new members who have no experience. He encouraged the Council to reach out to other communities that have successful airports to see what they are doing differently from Ogden City. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, October 4, 2022

column3: stated she has been talking with the City Engineer about some traffic safety concerns she has; there are several streets
column4: Sarge Morialli stated she has been talking with the City Engineer about some traffic safety concerns she has; there are several streets in Ogden with solid lines that prevent a left turn, but many people are crossing those solid lines, which could result in a traffic ticket if a police officer is present. She stated that the City needs to identify funding to correct these issues; there are many areas where solid lines are not appropriate because it is necessary for traffic to make a left turn into a business. She added that speeding is a problem in the City and last week a neighbor of hers was nearly killed while walking in the bike lane on the side of the road. Something needs to be done to slow traffic down. Additionally, the City needs to hire more employees that can take care of aging trees in the City cemetery before they fall and kill someone. These issues could result in a situation where the City is sued. She identified other traffic safety issues she has noticed in the community and thanked the Council for their attention.

column3: stated he is present this evening to ask if any Council member, Administration, or City staff is aware of any intent to
column4: Steven Van Wagoner stated he is present this evening to ask if any Council member, Administration, or City staff is aware of any intent to develop properties located at the Grandview Elementary, Lynn Elementary, or North Jackson Elementary sites that have been designated as surplus parcels by Ogden School District. On behalf of the community’s youngest children, he implored the City to take immediate action to secure the properties in accordance with State Code; if the City acquires the land, it cannot be used for any other purposes other than a town hall, park and open space, cultural center, or community center. The ‘clock is ticking’ for the City to purchase the land as it received the notice of the opportunity to purchase the land on September 15, 2022; the community has less than 72 days to provide written intent to Ogden School District before the property/open space is lost forever to a developer and vertical structures. Last week during a meeting with Chief Administrative Officer Johnson, Public Services Director Lowder, and Recreation Manager Bridge, they proclaimed that recreational fields are maxed out and the City is out of usable/programmable space and that next year they may need to limit participation in youth sports programs in the City. Outdoor activities and lifestyle are important to the community and the City has an opportunity to increase the amount of open space that can be used for programming.

column3: stated she is present tonight on behalf of the Union Station museums; she does not want to see the museums gutted and mo
column4: Teresa Holmes stated she is present tonight on behalf of the Union Station museums; she does not want to see the museums gutted and moved out of the building. Most of the people who arrive in Ogden via the Front Runner stop at the museums at the Union Station. She has been volunteering in the Union Station for over 21 years and was forced to sign a non-disclosure agreement about this issue, but she chose to speak. She has every right to speak, and she will make her voice loud when it comes to saving the museums. She stated the volunteers have been treated horribly under new management and they are ruining the facility; people come to Ogden from all different countries and states, but their access to the many great things at the Union Station has been limited. The new management of the Station is misrepresenting the number of visitors who come to the facility, and she encouraged the Council members to visit the Station on their own to gather their own information. She will be at the meeting on October 19 to talk about saving the museums and many of her friends will be there with her. She has been watching the dismantling of the Union Station for the last four years and she is very upset.

column3: stated there are lot of great things happening in Ogden; LUPEC is holding its Hispanic Festival this weekend at the Unio
column4: Angel Castillo stated there are lot of great things happening in Ogden; LUPEC is holding its Hispanic Festival this weekend at the Union Station, and she encouraged all to attend.

column3: stated that it is his understanding that earlier this evening, the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) purchased land from a deve
column4: Heath Satow stated that it is his understanding that earlier this evening, the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) purchased land from a developer or property broker, gave land to him across the street, and the person that was given the land did not perform as promised, so the City must purchase the land again. This is the use of taxpayer money for purchase of the same property two times, resulting in millions of dollars wasted. The same developer has also received an acre of land in Ogden’s downtown free of charge and many other incentives. The City’s Community and Economic Development Director hid this from the RDA Board; he suggested that the RDA ask some tough questions as it seems as if the RDA is more concerned about hurting the feelings of these developers than being responsible for taxpayer money. He has heard the Mayor say that the City has been working towards having the land developed for many years, but he asked if the City has advertised that they would give any developer $1 million to take on the project. There is no transparency related to these types of projects and he is very uncomfortable with the same developer participating in consecutive redevelopment projects, though that fact was hidden from the Board. The Board cannot do their job appropriately if they do not have all the information. He concluded by thanking the Police Department for moving traffic at the intersection of 26" Street and Harrison Boulevard when the traffic signal was malfunctioning; they did a great job. column4: Teresa Bramwell stated that she was in attendance last week to talk about her property on 25" Street and Monroe Boulevard and the extreme amount of crime that has occurred in that area as well as two fires that have occurred at her home and inside Topper Bakery. When the Fire Department responded to the Topper Bakery fire, they damaged the back of her home, which was not on fire. Today she wished to let the Council know where the crime is coming from; over the course of the 25 years that she has owned the property, there has never been this much crime. There were previously two single-family homes located next to her property that were demolished in order for a Family Dollar store to be constructed. The Family Dollar is 60 feet from her property line and their dumpsters are right outside the bedroom window of her home. The area behind the dumpsters is an open area with grass and garbage and the garbage is never cleaned up; it is taken out of the dumpsters by homeless people nearly every day. There is a vast amount of garbage and drug needles in the area. About half of the crime is caused by homeless people attracted to the area because of the dumpsters that are not secured. The other half of the crime is related to the nearby apartments on 25" Street and Monroe Boulevard; recently some people from the apartments have been arrested for crimes that have been committed on her property. She then presented a document she found on her door today; it is an affidavit for an administrative search warrant by Ogden City’s Code Enforcement Division. On the back page of the document, it states the City has spoken with her and she has withheld consent for the inspection of the property. She stated this is entirely false; she has never been asked for

column3: addressed the condition of Ogden’s roads; he understands it is very expensive to maintain and improve roads, but the rea
column4: Alan Jones addressed the condition of Ogden’s roads; he understands it is very expensive to maintain and improve roads, but the reason the roads are so deplorable is the sheer amount of work being done in the road. So many different entities are cutting into the roads for various reasons and the patch jobs performed after that work is done is insufficient. This leads to disrepair and damages to vehicles and adjacent properties and he inquired as to the City’s role in supervising the work being done to repair roads after they are cut. He asserted that whoever is responsible for performing that oversight is not doing their job properly. Ryan McDonald echoed the comments made by Mr. Van Wagoner; he has witnessed the loss of various properties to high density residential development, but there has been a lack of effort to preserve open spaces and provide parks responsive to residential growth. He understands there are no economic benefits associated with increasing open space, but it is very important to the community to do so. Colin Chapman advised the City Council to visit the neighborhood in which he lives to observe the current on-street parking conditions and the dangers created by this activity. He stated the Council may also notice how bad the road conditions are in his neighborhood, as expressed by Mr. Alan Jones. Terry Gartens echoed the comments made by Mr. Van Wagoner and others; she is very passionate about natural resource preservation and open spaces, but added she also cares deeply about the youth and fitness. She has worked with at-risk youth for nearly 25 years and community connection is so important for this group of residents and it is much easier to accomplish that connection if they have access to open spaces and recreational opportunities. She implored the City to preserve existing green spaces and expand/improve other open spaces in the community. Oliver (no last name given), also spoke to the need to preserve open spaces and expand parks in the Ogden community; he supported the recommendations made by Mr. Van Wagoner. D.S. Anderson concurred with many of the comments made during the public comment period relating to the Union Station, open space preservation, the condition of City roads, and the need for the City to be more responsive to the concerns of the residents of Marriott-Slaterville.

column3: stated she would have liked to attend tonight’s meeting in-person because of the importance of many of the topics discus
column4: Angel Castillo stated she would have liked to attend tonight’s meeting in-person because of the importance of many of the topics discussed tonight. She was told that tonight’s open house meeting would be open for virtual attendance or that the conversations happening would occur at the dais and podium so that those observing online could hear what was being said, but that did not happen and she is somewhat upset by that. Part of the reason she wanted to participate in those discussions is due to her concern about the WonderBlock project and associated bonding actions. The MakeOgden Plan is a great plan, but some things are happening that are contrary to that Plan and the episodes identified in the Plan. She advised the Council to read the plan to understand that the WonderBlock project is intended to be developer-led. She also spoke to the rules surrounding bond actions and noted that there are several steps or rules that the City has overlooked leading up to this point or evidence of conformance with those rules is not publicly available. She stated there are many people in the community expressing their desire for parks and recreation, but the City is choosing to invest millions of dollars into economic development projects instead.

column3: spoke to the importance of open green space. She noted she has lived in Ogden her entire life and has enjoyed recreating
column4: Eloise Braden spoke to the importance of open green space. She noted she has lived in Ogden her entire life and has enjoyed recreating outdoors and having access to nature through the many publicly accessible tails and park spaces. Ms. Braden’s mother echoed her daughter’s comments and expressed that she shares the same love for the outdoors and the green spaces in Ogden City.

column3: thanked those involved with organizing the open house event for the WonderBlock project; he was able to gather some good
column4: Heath Satow thanked those involved with organizing the open house event for the WonderBlock project; he was able to gather some good information and to speak to elected officials and the City’s development partner. He then addressed the comments that have been made about deplorable road conditions in the City and stated that he does not think that is due to the failure of someone to perform their job; rather, it is because there is not proper budget to complete road improvement projects. He stated that he signed up for water outage alerts several months ago and has been shocked by the number of alerts he receives, nearly daily and multiple times per day. He is amazed by the amount the City is willing to charge its ‘infrastructure credit card’, or using tax increment financing (TIF) that has resulted in infrastructure collapsing beneath the City’s feet. Property taxes have been raised to a limit above what residents can stand and it is not possible to increase them higher to pay for infrastructure. He stated he believes in growth and progress, but his concern relating to the WonderBlock project is increasing the load on the City’s infrastructure and robbing from funding that should be reserved for infrastructure projects.

column3: addressed the ongoing construction on the west end of Business Depot Ogden (BDO) where the business park borders Marriot
column4: Kerry Wayne addressed the ongoing construction on the west end of Business Depot Ogden (BDO) where the business park borders Marriott-Slaterville. He stated he and other residents are still experiencing dust, a great deal of water ponding along the roadside, an increase in the mosquito population, and the landscaping on the west side of the buildings has not been installed. He has emailed the Mayor, City Council, and other City officials several times with no response or action. He is very angry due to the lack of response or being passed to other Divisions of the City or other agencies who have no control over the matter. Something needs to be done and the City and The Boyer Company need to quit ignoring him and other residents. All summer long, the residents have dealt with the dust and other nuisances on the property and Ogden City, as the property owner, needs to do something to resolve it. He wants to be a good neighbor, but Ogden City and The Boyer Company are not good neighbors. The residents were first insulted by the construction of the warehouses and the lack of response is further insulting. column3: stated he is present to discuss what he feels is a lack of trust in the City’s Police Department; he relayed a personal
column4: Nathan Sutherland stated he is present to discuss what he feels is a lack of trust in the City’s Police Department; he relayed a personal story about a break-in involving his vehicle two weeks ago, after which he called the Police and was told that the Police Department does not respond to vehicle thefts and break-ins unless there is significant property damage. He stated that this is much different from the experience he had while living in Savannah, Georgia, where the Police Department there encourages residents to call them after a vehicle break-in so that they can observe the situation and look for patterns. This builds trust in the community and encourages engagement; they were also able to build information in a database about suspects or repeat offenders. If an offender is caught and is found to have been related to other past crimes, he or she can be charged for those crimes as well. He stated that he called Ogden City twice and was told that the same thing does not happen in Ogden and that his only option was to file a complaint online at a website hosted by the City; he found the site to be antiquated at best and he was ultimately unable to file his complaint. He later learned that another resident experienced a break-in during which she lost jewelry and other valuables and the Police Department quickly closed that case without solving it. He stated he left his car unlocked and he assumes fault for the break-in; however, he believes he knows who performed the break-in and he called the Police Department a second time to report them and was told that he should only call when the offenders are present and can be apprehended. He stated that through this experience he has lost quite a bit of faith in the Police Department and their ability to actively respond to incidences.

column3: reiterated comments he has made at the last two public meetings of the Council and Redevelopment Agency Board regarding
column4: Steven Van Wagoner reiterated comments he has made at the last two public meetings of the Council and Redevelopment Agency Board regarding his support for Ogden City acquiring properties that are being disposed of by the Ogden School District; he desires for these properties to be used to expand the City’s current stock of public parks and open space. He noted parks and open spaces are essential elements of a community providing a range of benefits not only as a place to recreate, but as a place to get away from the hustle and bustle of a City, meet friends and family, come together for community and neighborhood events, and be part of the great outdoors within earshot of home. More specifically, parks and open space promote health and wellness, foster human development, provide places to celebrate cultural activities and diversity, strengthen community image, and create a sense of place. He provided additional reasoning for adding park acreage commensurate with growth and stated that if the City were to maintain its current level of service, an additional 32 acres of park land will be needed by 2028 and 20 more acres at the time of buildout in 2045. He cited deficits in citizenry access to open spaces and recommended that the City acquire the properties to provide programmable space and open, passive space. Oscar Gonzalez echoed Mr. Van Wagoner’s comments and his passion regarding the need to expand the City’s open space offerings.

column3: stated that she has submitted an application to the City, along with a $500 application fee, for consideration of a non-
column4: Teresa Bramwell stated that she has submitted an application to the City, along with a $500 application fee, for consideration of a non-conforming use, but that issue has been ‘sidetracked’ before it reached the level of Council involvement. She stated she feels discriminated against because many of the land use issues that have been discussed and acted upon during tonight’s meeting are the same improvements that she desired to make to her property, but her requests were denied. She has a home that was burned in a fire caused by homeless individuals; she has a need to rebuild it as it is a historic home that was constructed in 1912 and she asked for permission to build a garage on the back of the home to increase safety and the ability to store things indoors rather than on the exterior of the property. She also wanted to build an ADU on top of the garage. This request was immediately ‘shot down’ by the Planning Commission, who also told her she needs to eliminate a portion of the parking area on her property. She stated that she was trying to do the same things that are included in the new East Central Community Plan, but she was denied and was not even allowed to come to the Council to communicate her concerns. She stated she has been treated unfairly by the City and this is a problem that needs to be fixed. She asked for advice on improving the situation. Jason Long echoed the comments made by Mr. Van Wagoner and others about the need to increase the amount of open and park space in the community to provide recreational opportunities for residents, especially the youth of the community. The properties being sold by the Ogden School District are great options for achieving this goal. Adam (no last name given), referenced the Council’s action earlier in the meeting relating to the zoning of 305 Harrison Boulevard; he stated that he spoke to the owners of that property about residential concepts that would be suitable for the property and would also serve to bring the surrounding community together. He is concerned about irresponsible developments being completed that will result in Ogden turning into something like Salt Lake with little open and green space and poor air quality. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, November 15, 2022

column3: stated that the health fair held recently at the Golden Hours Senior Center was phenomenal and he was happy to see infor
column4: Travis Pate stated that the health fair held recently at the Golden Hours Senior Center was phenomenal and he was happy to see information about the Marshall White Center (MWC) project while he attended that event. He stated that both facilities have experienced deferred maintenance and he is excited about the plans to improve the MWC. He suggested that the City try to partner with Weber State University (WSU) to complete additional improvements and create a joint use facility that will serve the entire community. He discussed costly improvements that have been made throughout the City using varied funding sources and noted that many of those improvements have not been properly maintained, which is very concerning.

column3: stated he understands the job performed by City Council members is very difficult and he applauded them for their servic
column4: Al Jones stated he understands the job performed by City Council members is very difficult and he applauded them for their service. He loves Ogden and so do many other people; he loves to see so many people getting involved in their local government and will always encourage people to stay involved. Ogden is very unique and has more potential than any other place he has visited; it takes leadership to maintain that uniqueness and residents do not want Ogden to be like other towns. It is not possible to solve today’s problems with yesterday’s solutions; new solutions need to be explored. There is a great deal of work to be done responsive to many projects being considered in the community and he suggested that City government slow down and carefully examine reasonable solutions. He referenced projects such as development of the Stock Exchange area, Union Station, WonderBlock, Nine Rails, and more. He applauded the Council for the work they do and hopes that they can work with all other parties to come up with the best solutions moving forward.
