He agreed that the project should be listed on an election ballot for a vote of the people, and he suspects the majority of citizens would not support it. \ Mayor Comments B Chief Administrative Officer Johnson indicated he had no additional comments.

column3: discussed the need to increase the amount of park space in the community and the economic value i that parks contribute
column4: Steven Van Wagoner discussed the need to increase the amount of park space in the community and the economic value i that parks contribute to the community; the City is deficient approximately 28 acres of park space based upon master planning documents and to not address that deficiency before issuing debt for economic projects is very concerning. Parks contribute to the overall value and connectivity of the community, and he looks forward to discussing the issue further. ;

column3: thanked the Council for entertaining so many public comments tonight. Al Jones also thanked the Council for allowing thi
column4: Susan Daley thanked the Council for entertaining so many public comments tonight. Al Jones also thanked the Council for allowing this level of public input, even though he does not necessarily agree with : the decisions that were made tonight. Now that the project has been approved, the City needs to ‘keep its finger on the pulse’ of the project to ensure it is successful. He noted there are many other redevelopment projects underway in the City and it is important to closely monitor the status of those projects to see that they are completed and can begin contributing to the economy of the community.

column3: stated that he is frustrated with the lack of involvement and response from the City’s development partner for the Wonde
column4: Travis Pate stated that he is frustrated with the lack of involvement and response from the City’s development partner for the WonderBlock project. They came to the City with their hand out, but failed to stay for the rest of the meeting to thank the : Council for the action they took tonight. Council member Blair stated that during the break earlier in the meeting, he visited with representatives of J. Fisher and indicated he believed that a vote on the project would be tabled tonight, and he advised them to leave the meeting. He stated they were not being disrespectful by leaving the meeting. Chair Choberka asked for decorum during this point in the meeting and indicated she will cut off public comment if civility is not preserved.

column3: emphasized his support for moving forward with the Union Station project correctly to ensure that it is successful. He a
column4: Al Jones emphasized his support for moving forward with the Union Station project correctly to ensure that it is successful. He also echoed Mr. Van Wagoner’s comments about the importance of open space; he encouraged the Council members to visit Ogden’s parks and trails to observe how much they are used. The trail system specifically is a great benefit to Ogden residents, and it is desperately in need of expansion and improvement. These are investments in Ogden that make it a fantastic place to live. He thanked the Council for all they do for the community.

column3: stated she would also like to encourage the Council to consider all opportunities to acquire land for open space and par
column4: Amy Wicks stated she would also like to encourage the Council to consider all opportunities to acquire land for open space and parks; land prices will only increase in the future. When she was a member of the Council, the City had an opportunity to approve an open space bond initiative and the current City Administration ‘dragged their feet’ and ruined the possibility of placing a question on the election ballot. She encouraged the City Council to invest in parks and open space, which will add fuel to Ogden’s economic engine. These types of things are what make the City a community of choice; not spending millions of D dollars on a lackluster development that residents will be indebted to for decades. The City will need to take money from other areas to shoulder that burden and services will suffer; the taxpayers will be absorbing the burden of providing tax funds to the developer. The only thing that is attractive about the housing in the project is that residents will have access to open space nearby; with the increased population and the increased pressure on open spaces, it is foolish to not invest in parks and open space when the access to school district surplus property is an option. FEE. ___) Nathan Sutherland echoed the comments about the need to increase park and open spaces in the community. Putting money into parks and open spaces will bring people to the community that will be interested in building here; Ogden should not ( be putting money into trying to solve the housing crisis and should, instead, be improving its outdoor recreation offerings. The housing problem will solve itself.

column3: stated she is not opposed to developing downtown Ogden or opposed to a project that will result in increased tax revenue
column4: Angel Castillo stated she is not opposed to developing downtown Ogden or opposed to a project that will result in increased tax revenue for the City, but she is concerned about how everything has changed lately. She noted there are only two people in this room who attended the Utah Economic Outlook Summit: herself and Council member White. There was a great deal of discussion about the housing problems in the State of Utah and Governor Cox is allocating $150 million to the entire State for | j housing. She contrasted that with the amount of money the City is spending on a parking deck and a project that includes office space. The Community and Economic Development Director has bragged that this project will include the ‘most expensive apartments in Ogden’ as if that is a point of pride. She finds that problematic and she asked how the Council could improve a project that does not have any percentage of affordable housing. She encouraged the Council members to reach out to elected ee ee nnn . ; officials in Boise, Idaho; she contacted him after learning that the WonderBlock developer built a project in that community. The +) initial proposal did not include any affordable housing and Boise officials pushed back until they were willing to include an “4 affordable housing component. She suggested that the Council stick up for first responders, teachers, hairdressers, and other i working-class citizens who earn less than $53,000 per year and can qualify for a low-income housing tax credit (LIATC) to live in i Ogden.

column3: stated she is the Division Manager for Ogden City Arts, Culture and Events (ACE), which includes Union Station as of Aug
column4: Christy McBride stated she is the Division Manager for Ogden City Arts, Culture and Events (ACE), which includes Union Station as of August of 2022. She stated that she understands it is not traditional for the Council to hear from Division Managers in this manner, but she was encouraged to speak by Council member Hyer after his recent visit to the Union Station. She wished to provide positivity about the facility; she understands this format is available for any resident to provide their opinion or voice on an issue and she is also a resident who has chosen to live, work, and raise her family here. She considers herself to be a very strong Ogden voice and lately as she has attended City Council meetings, she has become concerned about the negative energy surrounding the Union Station. She thought it would be helpful to share a sneak peek into what has been happening in the Union Station during the annual closure for maintenance and cleaning. No exhibits have been removed from the museums and, in reality, there are three new gun displays in the Browning Museum that will be open to the public for the first time tomorrow. The children’s hands-on play area will also reopen to the public tomorrow for the first time since the COVID ; ) pandemic. She has created a one-page report that lists all of the work accomplished by a very small team of staff members over the course of ten days. This document will be publicly shared with the volunteers that have been on a short break. There were 21 workers working for 241 project hours and 800 staff hours; the Union Station matters to them and over the 10 days, they were also able to write three RAMP grants totaling $195,000 in funding requests. One of the projects to be accomplished if funding is awarded is the Merci Car restoration. Attendance at the facility has been tracked very closely and in 2021 there were 18,865 people who bought a ticket to museums at the facility; in 2022, there were just over 22,100 people and that is an increase of 3,200. Her request is for the public to visit the Union Station and to do so from a place of kindness.

column3: thanked the Council for their careful review and consideration of the many proposals that come before them; he has revie
column4: Heath Satow thanked the Council for their careful review and consideration of the many proposals that come before them; he has reviewed the contracts that have been presented to the Council tonight and which will also be considered by the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) in their meeting following this meeting, and it is his opinion that the deal is fiscally irresponsible. The City is spending over $50 million on a parking structure with no competitive bids whatsoever; the builder is the developer of the WonderBlock project, but under a different name. He doubts anyone would do a major project on their home without getting multiple bids. He has reviewed costs for similar projects and has found the average cost to be about $35,000 per parking space, but the cost of this project equates to $47,000 per parking space. This is the residents’ money, and it is a lot of money, and he would like to hear real world examples of when a return on this investment can be expected. He is also very concerned about including office space in the WonderBlock project given the reduced demand for that use.

column3: stated he wished to be clear about his opinions about the Union Station and WonderBlock; he feels improvement of the Uni
column4: Sebastian Benitez stated he wished to be clear about his opinions about the Union Station and WonderBlock; he feels improvement of the Union Station will be great and it will continue to be a jewel in the Ogden community. He then encouraged the Council to stand by on the WonderBlock project until after the next election cycle; it would be best to place an opinion question on the next election ballot to allow residents to weigh in.

column3: thanked Ms. McBride for her report and for the efforts of the individuals who have been working at the Union Station.
column4: Steve Jones thanked Ms. McBride for her report and for the efforts of the individuals who have been working at the Union Station.

column3: discussed parks in the Ogden community; he referenced a period of time from which the entire world is still recuperating
column4: Steven Van Wagoner discussed parks in the Ogden community; he referenced a period of time from which the entire world is still recuperating and healing. During this time, the only places to gather were City parks and those spaces were : instrumental in building back the sense of community. After the pandemic, the Ogden leaders listened to the cry of the residents for expansion of park space, creating the largest impact on recreation in Ogden’s history. He asked if the Council was envisioning the COVID-19 pandemic and stated if so, they were incorrect as he was referencing the period of Ogden’s history when efforts ; were underway to build back after world wars. The priority at that time was leisure and the last time Ogden made a major : investment in parks was from 1908 to 1948; citizens were pleading for help to expand recreational space for baseball and golf; the , Mayor and Council worked together to create both of Ogden’s golf courses, Mount Ogden Park, 4" Street baseball complex, and other public spaces. It was the largest park expansion in Ogden’s history. ‘We’ are just coming out of a generational battle with the COVID-19 pandemic, and everyone is still healing; everyone has retooled how they feel about time and how they want to spend it, and, like our forefathers, ‘we’ are trying to build a community and build teams. Citizens require more space, and he advised the Council to embrace the courageous Ogden spirit by coming together like leaders of the past to help prioritize citizens and park space. He stated this issue is not going away and it will be part of every election cycle in the City going forward. He : encouraged all residents to embrace initiatives for better parks and more open space within an increased accountability of every elected official serving Ogden. As of today, www.andparks.org was launched and is committed to the Ogden parks initiative until all park space has been secured for citizen enjoyment now through 2045. Marissa Loving-Fosse also discussed parks and echoed the comments of Mr. Van Wagoner about the need for increased park space. She noted that this need is also identified in the City’s Master Plan regarding park space; the needs analysis indicated the City needs 605 to 685 acres of open space by 2028. At buildout, the City will need 735 to over 1,000 acres of open space land. She asked where this open space will come from; in 2018, the City was 20 acres short, nine soccer field deficient, one baseball field deficient, and 14 public bathrooms in need of full replacement. By 2023, the first 20-acre phase was to be implemented. She asked how many new soccer fields have been added since 2019; based upon the analysis, the City would have needed 20 acres of \ land to provide the nine soccer fields. The City currently has the opportunity to acquire the acreage needed at $238,000 per acre } and land will never be less expensive. The needs analysis states “the City should be opportunistic and have long-term outlooks , about acquiring land when it is available and picking away at a small segment of the system until it is complete.” She asked ifthe Ogden School District surplus plans do not meet this requirement; ideally the City would maintain its current level of service of 3.01 acres of land per 1,000 residents, but a decision has been made to provide a lower level of service at 2.0 acres per 1,000 residents. She asked if the citizens had an opportunity to vote on that decrease in level of service. She also encouraged elected officials and the public to visit www.andparks.org for more information on this issue. Brock Loomis, J Fisher Companies, noted he wished to address comments made earlier about the need for affordable housing; he understands the need for affordable housing and his company is one of the largest providers of low-income housing and LIMTC housing in the State of Utah. They currently own over 1,000 LIHTC units with another 300 being designed. That does not negate the need for market rate housing or catalytic development in Ogden City. He also wished to clarify that the project ) referenced by Ms. Castillo in Boise, Idaho was an affordable project from the day that J Fisher started working on it; it was never renegotiated in any way and is being built as an affordable project today.

column3: stated that it has been her goal to save the museums at the Union Station; she discussed her efforts to access documenta
column4: Teresa Holmes stated that it has been her goal to save the museums at the Union Station; she discussed her efforts to access documentation for the museums and other historical facilities in the City. It was difficult to do that and that is concerning to her. She stated it was very hard for her to be closed out of the museums after dedicating so much time there and she was worried about what was happening, She is glad to hear from Ms. McBride tonight, but she still believes strongly in preserving the heritage of the community.

column3: stated that when she was a member of the Planning Commission, she ‘lost her mind’ when the Commission considered a chang
column4: Angel Castillo stated that when she was a member of the Planning Commission, she ‘lost her mind’ when the Commission considered a change of use for property next to the fire station on the north end of town. The property was ultimately developed as a car wash, which she opposed. She wanted to pursue people-oriented design, which a car wash is not, and once a use changes it is impossible to recapture the former use. The City needs to avoid car-centric design and work to preserve green space to provide room for children to play and recreate. She agreed with Mr. Van Wagoner about the need to have accurate data and she asserted that the data the Council has been relying upon is incorrect and inconsistent with the General Plan. Once the School District properties are gone, they cannot be reclaimed, and the City needs to take advantage of opportunities to purchase the properties and partnering with other agencies to build amenities that will benefit the entire City.

column3: spoke to the need to reduce government regulation and taxation of residents. She discussed socialism and the preservatio
column4: Carolyn Lietuvininkas spoke to the need to reduce government regulation and taxation of residents. She discussed socialism and the preservation of fundamental rights; the power of legislature is in the people and if the government ‘goes rogue’, the people have the power to take it back. The Declaration of Independence is being used as a checklist for constraining people and socialism. She agrees that green space is important, but residents should encourage developers to pursue these projects. The populace has been conditioned to believe that such projects can only be handled by the government.

column3: stated that after hearing the comments made by those who have spoken before him, he is reminded what makes Ogden great.
column4: Heath Satow stated that after hearing the comments made by those who have spoken before him, he is reminded what makes Ogden great. He has chosen to make Ogden his home because of the people who live here. He referenced the Council’s discussion about the purchase of the School District properties during tonight’s work session and thanked the Council for being thoughtful when considering each property and unintended consequences of purchasing it. He also thanked the Council for promoting the idle-free initiative in local schools and considering the need to mix people from various income levels in the | } community. He noted, however, he is perplexed by the Council’s hesitation to purchase a $1.8 million property from the School District so soon on the heels of voting to bond for potentially 100 times that amount for the Wonder Block project, a development that was described by a member of City Administration has having the most expensive apartments in Ogden. The Council has been told that developers are scrambling to buy property in Ogden, yet the Council is not imposing any requirements on the a ; ; project that will preserve benefits for other residents. The Council needs to demand current market research to inform decisions ) that are financially wise. _ t

column3: stated she wished to talk about planning, zoning, foresight, and the Council’s role in the preservation of open space; C
column4: Angel Castillo stated she wished to talk about planning, zoning, foresight, and the Council’s role in the preservation of open space; Council member Hyer is a former Planning Commissioner, as she is, and she is aware that the City’s planning documents are grossly outdated. There are many matters that the Planning Commission or City Council do not have a choice on . because the decisions are dictated by outdated codes and plans; in 2018 she asked former Planning Manager Montgomery what it ) would take to update the City’s land use codes and General Plan and he told her it would cost $500,000 and he would need two full-time contract employees. The City would not be in the position it is today regarding the Ogden School District surplus property matter and other zoning issues if that project had been undertaken. She agrees with Mr. Van Wagoner that the Council owes it to the citizens to take some sort of action, even though the acquisition of property is technically not in the Council’s purview. The Council should set aside funding and perhaps the Mayor will come around and agree that acquisition of the property is appropriate. She noted there is a great deal of data that indicates that open space and recreation opportunities are important in terms of improving mental and physical health. She stated that the Council voted to address the Marshall White Center (MWC) because she made a motion to reorder the City’s Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) to prioritize that project. She asked that the Council have a similar commitment to the residents in terms of the acquisition and preservation of open space currently owned by . the School District.

column3: stated that he is the owner of West Ogden Market, and the City recently revoked his license, which led to litigation of
column4: Hamza Khalid stated that he is the owner of West Ogden Market, and the City recently revoked his license, which led to litigation of the matter. He recently submitted a Government Records Access and Management Act (GRAMA) request to the City to obtain records about the case and the documents showed that the reason the City revoked the license was that he did not have : proper tobacco licensing. However, in the email from the Assistant City Attorney, it is clear that she decided to proceed with the : revocation well before being aware of the lack of the tobacco license. This is the first of any revocation that the City has pursued in the past four years, and he has found there are other operations that have many significant violations, but they have not faced revocation of their license. He noted that the main response that he has received is that the Mayor does not want to reissue his license, but his lawyer has been unable to make contact with the Mayor. He noted that he has spent about $20,000 on this issue and the City has spent about the same amount; he has been operating in Ogden City since 2002 and his is literally the only store in West Ogden. He has gathered over 2,500 signatures on a petition supporting the licensure of his business. He has given over : $30,000 in groceries to people who live in West Ogden because they rely on him. He stated that he is frustrated that he cannot speak with anyone in the City, verbally or through email, and he feels that he could have a meaningful conversation with someone if that were simply permitted. He stated he feels he has been discriminated against based upon the fact that other businesses have had significant violations but have not had the same experience as him. Chair Choberka invited Mr. Khalid to stay until the end of the meeting and she noted she will speak with him and try to help him make some connections.

column3: stated that green space is disappearing at a rapid pace and the Council needs to consider the value that green space con
column4: Laura Lewis stated that green space is disappearing at a rapid pace and the Council needs to consider the value that green space contributes to the community, even if dollar amount cannot be assigned to that value. When the City has the opportunity to purchase open space and turn it into a park, that should be a priority for both the Administration and City Council. The increase in residential development will increase the demand for park space. Chair Choberka addressed Mr. Satow’s comments about the developer selection process and indicated she believes there will be a follow-up agenda item regarding that topic in the coming weeks. She also addressed the comments about the Ogden School District properties and noted that the Council recently learned that the appraisal of those properties is not based upon the current zoning or use of the property, but it is based upon the uses surrounding the properties. She addressed Ms. Bramwell’s comments about the properties owned by the City between 24" and 25" Streets on Monroe Boulevard and noted that the City is not currently receiving any property tax revenue from those properties. Council member White then noted that it is important for the residents to understand that the City must pay fair market value for the surplussed properties, even though the taxpayers have already paid for those properties through their taxes paid to the Ogden School District.

column3: stated he recently visited Mesquite, Nevada for a soccer tournament; the soccer complex there is beautiful, and it has a
column4: Steve Van Wagoner stated he recently visited Mesquite, Nevada for a soccer tournament; the soccer complex there is beautiful, and it has also served as an economic driver for that community, resulting in a great deal of commercial development surrounding the soccer complex. He stated that he understands that the City Council cannot force the purchase of the Grandview Elementary property from the Ogden School District, but they can set aside funding to provide a pathway for Administration to move forward with the purchase. He stated the Council has a choice and he urged them to exercise that option. He added that he already feels good about the headway that has been made relating to the surplus properties; last fall, Administration was only interested in acquiring the properties for development purposes, but that mindset has been changed and at least one of the properties will be used to expand the park offerings in the community. He asked ‘what if? the Council adopted a resolution that would provide for the acquisition of the Grandview property and ‘what if? the Mayor changed his mind about that property as well. He stated the ‘what if lies with the Council and he urged them to take a different approach to this issue. He stated that he respects all Council members, and he thanked them for their service. Teresa Holmes referenced historical decisions made by past Mayors relating to parks and open space; she organized a petition drive aimed at saving parks, trails, and other open spaces and it was successful. She stated that Mr. Van Wagoner is trying to do something similar, and she suggested that the Council take any action they can to urge City Administration to purchase the Grandview Elementary property. She added that she is very concerned about the preservation of the museums at the Union Station; she has served as a volunteer at the facility for 21 years and has logged over 7,000 volunteer hours and she has been treated very disrespectfully over the past several months. The City seems to be more concerned with development than preserving the things that are truly valuable to the community.

column3: discussed some recent experiences she has had on her property at 25" Street and Monroe Boulevard; ( she has reached out
column4: Teresa Bramwell discussed some recent experiences she has had on her property at 25" Street and Monroe Boulevard; ( she has reached out to different entities in the community who are looking for space for a business to open, but she never received a response and she thinks that is because those entities do not want certain people to be involved. She added that the City owns vacant land between 24" and 25" Streets and Monroe Boulevard; all of the businesses that were located on that block and were generating tax revenue for the City are now vacant for the past 14 years and she asked who is paying the taxes for that property Minutes of Reqular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, February 21, 2023 Tn __— now. She was recently at her home on 25" Street and Monroe Boulevard and was approached by an elderly disabled woman _) accompanied by a henchman’; the woman asked her companion to go onto Ms. Bramwell’s property to retrieve laundry that she - ‘ had left on the porch because she was unable to get it home. i Chris Barrigan echoed the recommendations communicated by Mr. Van Wagoner to the Council regarding the options ; available to them to promote the acquisition and preservation of the Grandview Elementary property; he hopes the Council will acquire accurate data regarding the amount of green space currently available in the community and the desires of the citizens when it comes to the use of those spaces. He hopes the Council will take their time and carefully consider this issue because the youth in the community really need space to grow and play.

column3: stated that she is grateful for the Council’s discussion during tonight’s work session regarding the honorary street nam
column4: Angel Castillo stated that she is grateful for the Council’s discussion during tonight’s work session regarding the honorary street naming ordinance. She is concerned that the ordinance language will change from ‘shall’ to ‘may’ regarding the Council soliciting a recommendation from the Diversity Commission on any honorary street naming application. The City has assembled committees, but they are not being empowered to do their job. She added she is also concerned that the City will only retain the land under the Union Station, but that a private developer can own the building and do whatever they want with it. She then asked for the status of the City’s participation in the Community Renewable Energy Act (CREA) project; there is a deadline looming and in order for the City to remain in the project, it must sign a utility agreement. She encouraged the Council to look into that deadline to ensure that this is something that is handled timely.

column3: stated that communication is most effective when it is two-way and is transparent; she referenced the City’s website and
column4: Heather Barnett stated that communication is most effective when it is two-way and is transparent; she referenced the City’s website and suggested that residents have the opportunity to provide input through the website rather than being required to attend a City Council meeting to provide input. This would help to improve the trust the community has in its elected leaders. Chair Choberka asked if Administration wished to address the comments about the Union Station Campus project and concerns about a private developer owning the Union Station building. Community and Economic Development Director Cooper stated there may be a misunderstanding about that aspect of the joint resolution and the subsequent project; thereare many options | i available to the City and as Administration looks at developing the Campus and buildings, it will explore all financing options available and as options become known and available, they will be brought to the Council and Redevelopment Agency (RDA) Board. Chair Choberka asked where residents can go to stay up do date on the Union Station plans and to engage with the City to provide their input. Mr. Cooper stated the MAKE Ogden meeting series will begin soon and residents will have the opportunity to Minutes of Requiar Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah, March 7, 2023 ee eee ee eee eT EE i engage with City staff on all MAKE Ogden project, including the Union Station. Each significant project will have its own public ~~, engagement process as well. The development partner that has been selected has sent a mailer to every household and they are an, very well versed in the importance of public engagement. He believes there will be sufficient opportunities for public it involvement. : Chair Choberka then addressed Ms. Castillo’s question about the City’s involvement in CREA; she noted that she, Council staff, and the City Attorney’s Office have been involved in weekly meetings about the project and one of the challenges that has been encountered is that once the utility agreement is approved, there is nothing the City can do to change it. That . concerns her and others from the City and any new information will be presented to the Council. Mayor Momments Mayor Caldwell stated some very strong public statements have been made through the actions taken by the Council : tonight; many emotional issues have been addressed and he applauded Administration and the Council for their response to those issues.

column3: stated he is a private developer and has done work in Ogden; in recent years, he has been shocked by the number of bligh
column4: Mike Anthony stated he is a private developer and has done work in Ogden; in recent years, he has been shocked by the number of blighted homes and properties in Ogden City. He is a retired veteran and has been in real estate for over 47 years and it would be his suggestion to pursue a land lease for the properties around the Union Station rather than sell them. At the end of the land lease, the properties and their improvements would be the ownership of the City. He cited projects in other states that were handled with a land lease and now those state or cities own projects that are very valuable. He expressed a willingness to participate in the Union Station project or advise the City on programs it could take advantage of to renovate blighted and historic properties and perhaps repurposing them for veteran housing.

column3: addressed low- and moderate-income housing; she noted that Ogden City has 69 percent of the low- income population in We
column4: Teresa Bramwell addressed low- and moderate-income housing; she noted that Ogden City has 69 percent of the low- income population in Weber County, but only 38 percent of the County’s population resides in Ogden. She can see this leading to problems around her neighborhood surrounding 25" Street and Monroe Boulevard. She noted the Council’s action to acquire 605 North Jackson will take money from the Quality Neighborhoods Initiative, which was specifically designated for the East Central Community, which is where her property is located. The East Central Community is likely the most destitute in the City; it contains most of the City’s abandoned properties and needs the money that has been allocated to it. She likes the idea of building single-family homes in the community that can be purchased by moderate income individuals and noted this is missing in the East Central Community. However, she feels these types of projects should be accomplished by private developers if land is available to them to purchase. She emphasized the money is desperately needed in East Central and it should not be diverted to other areas of the City. She added she recently learned that the James Madison Elementary School will be closed at the end of the school year, and it is likely that property will be made available for purchase in the future and she encouraged the Administration and Council to start thinking about the future use of that property now because its future use is very important to the City’s future and has the potential to ‘make or break’ the City. Heath Satow also spoke to housing affordability; the City is receiving incomplete information about this issue. He also } addressed the Union Station project and noted he has learned from the City’s Community and Economic Development Director that the City will retain the land at the Union Station Campus, but a private developer will own the Union Station and the City will rent it from them. This means the City will be at the whim of a private developer relative to the museums located in the facility. He noted it is important for the Council to stay alert, ask for complete information, and make the best decisions for all of Ogden rather than for big developers.

column3: thanked Council Communications and Public Engagement Coordinator Garside for his efforts to provide as much public infor
column4: Angel Castillo thanked Council Communications and Public Engagement Coordinator Garside for his efforts to provide as much public information as possible regarding the proceedings and actions of the Council. Leadership is about accountability and transparency, and she appreciates the value Council staff places on those things. She then noted that during tonight’s work session she does not feel enough questions, or the right questions, were asked about the proposed Land Transfer and Development Agreement relating to 550 24" Street; she does not have a problem with the developer of that property, but with the process by which the developer was selected. She has spoken with other developers who were not aware of the opportunity to bid on the project and one developer who has indicated a willingness to actually pay for the property before developing it, rather than having it gifted to him. There are two other developers who are very well qualified and who are willing to pay the City up to $1.9 million for the property, but those offers have been rejected. Transparency is important and accountability to the taxpayers is vital; giving away public equity should only be considered when there are no other options.

column3: stated he is the Chair of Latinos United Promoting Education and Civic Engagement (LUPEC) and he wished to announce the
column4: Eulogio Alejandre stated he is the Chair of Latinos United Promoting Education and Civic Engagement (LUPEC) and he wished to announce the Hispanic Festival in Ogden on September 30 from 2:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Ogden Amphitheater, which will include mariachi music from bands from Utah and South America, authentic food, vendors, and information booths. He also thanked the City for its continued support of LUPEC and sustaining Hispanic culture and language in Ogden City. He . thanked Council member Lopez for his leadership in the community and in LUPEC. He announced LUPEC is prepared to : collaborate with the City to enhance their partnership and improve the journey of life for all of those that call Ogden home. He recognized members of LUPEC who were present in the audience and thanked the Council for this opportunity to speak.

column3: stated he was glad to hear the Council’s discussion in tonight’s work session about choosing a flag for the City and ack
column4: Heath Satow stated he was glad to hear the Council’s discussion in tonight’s work session about choosing a flag for the City and acknowledgement that the Council members are no experts on flag design and that it may be appropriate to solicit outside expertise. He was led to be curious about past discussions about the developer selection process and he encouraged the Council to reach out behind the ‘echo chamber’ of City Administration regarding that topic. He suggested they speak to other developers to learn their feelings about past developer selections and the failure of some developers to deliver on the terms of the agreements they have entered into with the City. He stated it is important for the Council to be aware that they are not always getting all the information they need. ,

column3: thanked the Council for their recent votes to preserve green space and parks. He then noted he recently sent an email to
column4: Sebastian Benitez thanked the Council for their recent votes to preserve green space and parks. He then noted he recently sent an email to the City Council regarding the Grandview Elementary property, but he received a response that his email was not delivered. He communicated the subject matter of that email, which was to urge the Council to purchase the Grandview property and freeze any construction activity on that property. He then congratulated Chief Administrative Officer Johnson on his _ retirement and urged the Mayor to wait to appoint a new Chief Administrative Officer until after the 2023 Mayoral election. p Teresa Holmes addressed efforts of the community to save the museums at the Union Station; the City should consider allowing any interested resident to participate on the citizen’s committee that will be assembled to participate in the Union Station Campus project. Steve Jones has asked to be able to participate and City Administration denied him that opportunity.

column3: stated she is the owner of the home at 136 West 2" Street, and she missed the Council’s discussion of her historic desig
column4: Terry Lanier stated she is the owner of the home at 136 West 2" Street, and she missed the Council’s discussion of her historic designation petition. She inquired as to the Council’s action earlier in the meeting. Chair Choberka reported the Council approved the ordinance to place the home on the historic register.

column3: thanked the City for repairing a light fixture on Jefferson Avenue at his request. He then asked that the City : study J
column4: Travis Pate thanked the City for repairing a light fixture on Jefferson Avenue at his request. He then asked that the City : study Jefferson Avenue and the damage that has been caused by heavy trucks using the roadway for recent construction projects; : specifically, the crosswalk was damaged, and he suggested that the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT) examine the area before concluding the project. Mr. Pate also addressed historic preservation actions and indicated that noticing of these actions should continue in the newspaper because the record of such notices is permanent. He stated that even if the decision is made to : cease newspaper noticing for other types of land use matters, the practice should continue for historic designation issues to ensure permanent access to those notices. Permanent retention cannot be assured when all noticing is handled on the internet.

column3: thanked the Council for listening to the input provided by citizens, even of some of the comments made may sound accusat
column4: Heath Satow thanked the Council for listening to the input provided by citizens, even of some of the comments made may sound accusatory or negative; the public cannot be expected to know all information, especially information that is discussed in closed sessions, and that can cause frustration that leads to toxicity. Citizens can only affect change through elections, but for the years during elections the public can only ask questions and provide input and hope they are heard. He addressed a few items that were originally included on the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) agenda for this evening; there is a single company that is slated to develop at least four major properties that Ogden City has pledged to them, and these projects could total upwards of a half-billion dollars or more. This includes the development of Union Station, which is the touchstone of the community’s history. Additionally, there were to be updates to the developer selection process tonight due to ongoing concerns about the transparency of that process, but yesterday these items were removed from the agenda, likely due to the Board’s concerns to place so much of the City’s future into a single basket. While he appreciates the care taken to address these situations, he feels itis prudenttotakea step back and reassess the situation; he understands many projects are brought to the Board very late in the process and they have little time to make decisions and that is why he has encouraged them to contact outside experts, such as Urban3, Weber County, and commercial retailers who have financial interest in the projects. By doing so, the Board could gain new insight and possibly avoid identifiable problems that may have been overlooked. As elected officials, the Board has a covenant with the citizens of ; Ogden to prioritize their wellbeing and fulfilling this promise requires a willingness to change course when new evidence comes : > to light. It is a sign of strength, not weakness, to reassess and make adjustments when necessary. He asked the Board to take time \ and seek out as much outside expert opinion as they can gather; doing so will help them to make the best possible decisions for the i community and ensuring it continues to thrive and grow as the heart of Weber County. :

column3: stated the federal government will meet tomorrow to make decisions about interest rates; taxable values for real estate
column4: Mike Adlay stated the federal government will meet tomorrow to make decisions about interest rates; taxable values for real estate are based on one-year arrears of sales that occurred prior to the assessor’s evaluation. He asked the Council to be aware that things will drastically change as real estate values are impacted by interest rates; as rates climb exponentially away from a certain market, there is a very real negative impact on values. When interest rates were below three percent, property values were unrealistic, and this is exactly what happened in 2008 before the market crashed. As rates climb above five percent, there will be a negative impact on residential values, and this is what is causing many banks to be in default on loans they have made. He is . starting to believe that something similar to the crash in 2010 will be happening soon.

column3: discussed the history of the Union Station and efforts of many volunteers in the community to locate museums in the faci
column4: Tereas Holmes discussed the history of the Union Station and efforts of many volunteers in the community to locate museums in the facility in order to save it; she is concerned about the museums being removed from the Union Station at this time and she hopes the City is committed to preserving them. Angel Castillo referenced discussions during tonight’s work session meeting; the My Hometown Ogden group shared great information about their cause, and she suggested that Ogden City follow their lead and share information about important resources available to the community. She noted that there is an imminent threat of flooding in the community this spring and she encouraged the City to begin preparing to respond and help residents respond to protect their own property. She also referenced the Airport Community Reinvestment Area (CRA) and noted the State of Utah is evaluating how cities are using tax increment financing (TIF) in these types of project areas. Ogden City has been listed on a webpage maintained by the State as having provided no evidence that project area plans and objectives have been tracked. She is not saying that something has been done wrong, but until the City’s ‘house is in order’ and the Council can verify that all reporting is being properly handled, the City should pause future projects or extensions of existing project areas.

column3: discussed what happened in a recent Planning Commission meeting when she was seeking permission to rebuild her home at 2
column4: Teresa Bramwell discussed what happened in a recent Planning Commission meeting when she was seeking permission to rebuild her home at 25" Street and Monroe Boulevard; she was disturbed by some of the things that happened to long term property owners who were seeking approval from the Planning Commission to simply use their property, including placing a tenant in their commercial building or even acting as a tenant in their own commercial building. These people own one property, : but they are being classified as developers and being required to meet an entire host of development requirements; one property owner was required to tear up his parking lot and replace half of it with grass and install an irrigation system for the new grass. This person simply wants to use his property to clean cars and sell them at a wholesale auction. He cannot believe the hoops that individual property owners/taxpayers are being required to jump through in order to use their property. It broke her heart to see that people are being forced into a classification and spending a great deal of money just to use their own property, yet true developers are being allowed to take property that is owned by the City of Ogden and make millions of dollars on that property while ignoring zoning laws. Developers are getting rights that individual property owners will never have and that is not right. Laura Lewis referenced a note on her most recent water bill regarding the Wonder Block project; the messaging was quite confusing and references ‘defense ecosystem’, but she could not find information about what that is. The only thing she S could find online was a reference to defense contractors who help subsidize manufacturing and development. There is another ) quote about the developing bringing high paying jobs to the community, but from what she knows of the development, it includes retail, office space, grocery, boutique hotel, and other service-oriented businesses, which typically provide low paying jobs and she asked what will be included in the development that will entail high paying jobs.

column3: discussed historical actions in Ogden City associated with the creation of the Redevelopment Agency; he also . discussed
column4: Travis Pate discussed historical actions in Ogden City associated with the creation of the Redevelopment Agency; he also . discussed the importance of utilizing all options available to provide public notice of pertinent actions being considered by the Council and the RDA. Just because something is allowed by Jaw, does not mean it should be done; the State of Utah has changed noticing requirements, but that does not mean Ogden City should reduce its efforts to provide adequate public notice of important actions. He has found historical notices regarding the Union Station when it was first dedicated as a museum, and if the City were to changes its noticing processes now, such notices would no longer be provided and available to tell the history of the City in the : future. There have been problems with notification in the past and the City Council needs to take ownership of those matters. He : then added that requests for qualifications (RFQ) documents should only be published after a request for proposals (RFP); the City is shoehorning inappropriate projects into neighborhoods in the City where they do not belong, and he encouraged the Council to take a step back and evaluate accordingly.

column3: stated she serves on two Committees at the State level after having been appointed by the Governor; she is proud of the
column4: Angel Castillo stated she serves on two Committees at the State level after having been appointed by the Governor; she is proud of the work the Governor has done with regard to equity, inclusion, and diversity and noted he was one of the first to sign the Utah Racial Compact. She referenced conversations over the past several years that have involved the Diversity Commission, some of these conversations have been hard, but the Commission fulfills a very important role. It is egregious that Mr. Lundell has not been reappointed; he is a long-standing member of the community with a history of service and the fact that the Mayor would not take a meeting with him to discuss it is egregious. She cited other instances where City committees have been used in a ; performative way and she challenged the Administration to do better in this area. She also encouraged everyone to avoid being punitive towards those who are asking questions and challenging opinions. As long as a matter is handled with respect and politeness, it is ok to disagree, but conversations are imperative.

column4: Dave Timmerman shared similar concerns regarding the treatment of current and former members of City committees; City leadership must be respectful and communicate to those who are not being reappointed to a position. He then addressed the notice to vacate that was provided to the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center recently; he offered his own personal observations about the Center and the benefits it provides to young people of the community. He encouraged the City to extend the eviction period and give the Center more time to find properties within the City that would accommodate their needs. He concluded with a quote from Mark Twain: “Of all the animals, man is the only one that is cruel; he is the only one who inflicts pain for the pleasure of , doing it.” y Teresa Holmes echoed Mr. Timmerman’s comments about the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center. She also reiterated the point she has made several times about the need to preserve the Union Station and the museums located within that facility.

column3: stated that Mr. Lundell is not the first person to be removed from a committee for speaking their mind. He then stated t
column4: Heath Satow stated that Mr. Lundell is not the first person to be removed from a committee for speaking their mind. He then stated that there is a developer who could not assemble the funds needed to purchase land on the former Rite-Aid block, so he came to the City asking the City to buy the land for him and the City did. The same developer was given the Wonder Block property and now there is a proposal to also give him property at 550 24" Street, which will be discussed later tonight. This developer is also part of the same team that has been selected for the Union Station project and he is concerned about whether it is wise to put all of the City’s eggs in the same basket without knowing if the other projects are going to be successful; no work has been done on the Wonder Block or the Rite Aid property and these blocks are blighted. He asked if the State of Utah is monitoring the City’s redevelopment activities to ensure they are legal. He then advised the Council to ask more questions about the 550 24% Street project; they should ask why J. Fisher Companies was not mentioned in the presentation about the property transaction. He also encouraged them to urge Administration to select developers who have a proven track record of performance. Taylor Knuth echoed the comments that have been made about the Diversity Commission and the failure of the Mayor to reappoint Mr. Lundell; he cited the advice and consent process as it applies to committee appointments and indicated that it is inconsistently applied and is unfair if not borderline unethical. The actions of the past several weeks have caused Commissioners and the public to lose trust and faith in elected officials. Most concerning is Administration’s rejection of a meeting on the topic without reason, logic, or common sense. He concluded he stands with Mr. Lundell and the other Commissioners who have spoken \ this evening. This action disrespects the time that volunteers dedicate to the committee to which they have been appointed. _ Sebastian Benitez stated he has also requested meetings with the Mayor and with the City Attorney and those meetings have been refused; he would like to speak with Administration about the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center. He noted that Mayor Caldwell will not be the Mayor next year and Chief Administrative Officer Johnson will no longer be serving in his capacity, and they should let the individuals who fill their roles to make decisions about the Center. He also echoed the comments made about Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah April 4, 2023 nnn nnn nnn nnn ___________t Mr. Lundell and suggested that the decision not to reappoint him be reconsidered. He also encouraged the Council to take action necessary to stop any movement on the Wonder Block project. Amy Wicks also echoed the comments made about the Diversity Commission and asked that the Council ask for information about the ethnicity and background of people who are being appointed to the Commission. She noted she is Native American and is unsure whether her ethnicity is represented on the Commission. She added that the meeting times of the Commission are difficult and that is why some former members have stopped serving in that role; she suggested that the meeting times be changed to suit the schedules of the Commissioners. She then addressed the eviction of the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center and noted that she is upset about the information provided in tonight’s work session about the Dinosaur Park. She asked if City employees have the right to decide what can and should be done with property that is owned by the citizens of Ogden; the facility currently occupied by the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center was formerly used as an animal shelter and it was built with money that was assumed largely due to private fundraising. She asked why there was no public process about evicting the Center, demolishing the building, and expanding the Dinosaur Park. She encouraged the Mayor to extend the eviction timeline and noted that if the Center is forced to move out of Ogden, wildlife in the area will suffer.

column3: stated he is the former Vice Chair of the Diversity Commission; he thanked the Council for voting to table appointments
column4: Kevin Lundell stated he is the former Vice Chair of the Diversity Commission; he thanked the Council for voting to table appointments and reappointments to the Diversity Commission earlier this evening. On March 28 he received a letter from Mayor Caldwell informing him he would not be reappointed to the Diversity Commission; this was a surprise as he was recently voted to serve as the Vice Chair by his fellow Commissioners and he has served for less than one year. After requesting a meeting with Mayor Caldwell to ask why he was not being reappointed, he was told a meeting would ‘not be productive’ and that ‘turnover is common’. While turnover is common, it is unprecedented for a City Commissioner in good standing with his fellow Commissioners to not be reinstated, let alone a sitting Vice Chair. While the Mayor has full discretion as to who is appointed to the Diversity Commission, he refused to reappoint him without consulting the Chair, Diversity Affairs Coordinator, or the Commission. A good leader utilizes their colleagues when making key decisions, like appointments. Without an explanation given by the Mayor, he has spent a lot of time pondering what he may have done to warrant being expelled from the Commission. Last month he wrote an op-ed defending diversity efforts from the likes of Senator John Johnson that would have outlawed diversity programs in higher education. He unapologetically used language comparing Johnson to some of the most notorious politicians in the past who have stood in the way of racial progress. Given the fact that Senator Johnson was protested last week by students at Weber State University (WSU), it seems his opinion is in line with many who care about diversity efforts in the community. It is \ his perspective that he was expelled from the Diversity Commission for defending diversity. He spent many hours this weekend discussing the issue with past and present Diversity Commissioners and the words he keeps hearing to describe the Commission are ‘performative’ and ‘tokenizing’; it leads him to believe this is just the tip of the iceberg. During his year of service, the Mayor has not attended a single Diversity Commission meeting, nor has he had any interaction with Diversity Commission leadership. Minutes of Regular Meeting of Council of Ogden City, Utah April 4, 2023 7 He called upon Mayor Caldwell to reengage with the Commission in good faith and find a path forward that allows them to fulfill > the mission of the Diversity Commission charter. ; \__ Kari Harbath shared her story as an Ogdenite and relayed the benefits she has received due to the culture of Ogden City. 4 She shares her story in an effort to highlight the reasons that she volunteers her time as a member of the Diversity Commission; : she wants to give back what Ogden has so wonderfully given to her. She is not alone in this mission as every member of the = Commission has their own story and lived experience and wants to give back. She reiterated Mr. Lundell’s comments about the fact that the Commission feels more performative in recent months, and she would rather that the group truly provide a meaningful impact and be service oriented. She nominated Mr. Lundell to serve as the Vice Chair for the Commission because he is making a positive impact on the community and using his voice for good; the lack of communication and transparency around not reappointing Mr. Lundell has been extremely discouraging and has her questioning her role on the Commission. She asked Mayor Caldwell to address these issues and speak to the manner in which diversity inclusion efforts will be included in Ogden : City’s mission going forward so that current Commissioners can decide if serving on the Commission is right for them.

column3: spoke to her involvement as a member of the Diversity Commission and echoed the comments made by others about their desi
column4: Shardae Jones spoke to her involvement as a member of the Diversity Commission and echoed the comments made by others about their desire to participate with the Commission in order to make change. She supports the reappointment of Mr. Lundell and indicated the message about the purpose of the Commission be reinforced in the community.

column3: shared information about Awesome Autistic Ogden’s participation in the upcoming Arts Stroll; students have created art t
column4: Stacy Bernal shared information about Awesome Autistic Ogden’s participation in the upcoming Arts Stroll; students have created art that will be on display in the community at The Bonneville on 25" Street. She then echoed the comments that have been made tonight about usage of and appointments to the Diversity Commission; she is dismayed that someone is being punished for their viewpoints on a diversity matter. Bills like the one that was sponsored by Senator Johnson would have harmed her child and it is necessary for people to speak out about elected officials who feel a certain way about diversity, equity, and inclusion. She stated that more people like Keven Lundell are needed in this community.

column4: Bill Dodge stated that he is concerned about the action that was taken on the zoning of the Union Station property; the commercial/mixed-use zone will allow for 10-story buildings, while the zoning that has been assigned to other properties on 25% | : - Street would only allow for four-story buildings. He stated there is a MAKE Ogden meeting scheduled for next week and he +) assumed it will be held in the Union Station building; he note the parquet floor that is in the Station is original to the Station from : So the late 1800’s and it has been ‘put on the chopping block’ to be removed upon development of the site and the congratulated the i Council on voting to allow that to happen. i

column3: addressed the developer selection process and policy, which will be discussed during the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) meet
column4: Heath Satow addressed the developer selection process and policy, which will be discussed during the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) meeting tonight; during the March 14 work session, the Community and Economic Development Director informed the Council that Henry Walker Homes was the selected developer for the 550 24" Street project, but he did not feel it relevant to mention that they are owned by JF Capital, which is the developer for the Rite Aid Block, Wonder Block, and Union Station projects. The Director told the Council that the full market value of the land is $655,000, which is incredibly low, similar to the Brown Ice Cream building that was undervalued several years ago. The Director told the Council that the City has a vision for seeking ‘above market rate’ units for the 24 Street development, but that was not part of the request for proposals (RFQ) that was published for the project. The Council has been told that the RFQ also provided clear guidance relative to the development timeline, but that is also incorrect as there is no timeline mentioned in the document. The Council was told the City sought an ownership model and that Henry Walker Homes provided that, while the other respondent did not. He noted the RFQ only asks respondents to state a preference, but the City’s preference was not stated in the RFQ, and the other respondent clearly stated they would provide a rental or ownership model if the City preferred one or the other. He stated a City Council member, on Facebook, repeated the falsehood about the ownership model being explicitly requested in the RFQ because they implicitly trusted what they were told by City staff. The Council should be able to trust what they are told. He added a third developer approached the Director a few years ago with a concept for townhomes on the subject property; this was an unsolicited proposal, but the developer was told the City was going to publish an RFQ and that they would be contacted once the RFQ was released. However, the developer was not contacted. The developer lives in Ogden and has taken their interests outside of Ogden as they are no longer interested in developing in Ogden. He stated that he has heard these types of stories over and over again and the scarcity of applications for these projects is manufactured. Laura Lewis referenced the Council’s action on the MAKE Ogden downtown zoning ordinances and Council member White’s comments about the State of Utah pushing cities to increase housing opportunities; she asked if the claim is that the State is forcing the City to allow dense housing on the Union Station campus and if that is the case, she would like to review the | ) document in which that requirement was communicated. She asked how the State of Utah can dictate what the City does on the Union Station property.

column3: stated he has approached many City Councils in the past and even had to meet with Council members in other cities to edu
column4: Mark Nelson stated he has approached many City Councils in the past and even had to meet with Council members in other cities to educate them on certain issues, but tonight he would like to commend the Council for the job they have done. The Council knows more about what is going on than the general public. The general public can become upset and there will always be naysayers; in fact, there will always be more negative feedback than positive feedback because those who are pleased with what is happening will sit back and let it happen. He stated the Council has done a great job and it is impossible to please everyone; Ogden looks better than it has in his entire lifetime, and he hears from many business owners and developers about their , desire to be in Ogden. He stated there are some old buildings that should be torn down and others that need to be preserved and he | is supportive of the Council and their ability to make those decisions. Steve Jones suggested that everyone think about Union Station in a different way and from the perspective of what a visitor coming to Ogden should experience. The Council should think about what a visitor will see and feel when they walk onto the campus and if their feelings will make them want to spend more time in Ogden and in other nearby historic areas. The most important thing is what people will experience when they come to downtown Ogden, and he is very disappointed by how the Council voted tonight. However, he does not feel all is lost and the Council still have oversight and approval authority for future development of the campus, and he hopes the staff and Council will only pursue things that will enhance what is already in existence. He concluded two things he would like to see happen are expedient planning and envisioning of the future of the campus and the creation of a Union Station Advisory Board that can be involved in that process. Thayne Fisher congratulated the Council for making a wise decision to proceed with implementation of the MAKE Ogden Plan. Success is not defined as everyone getting what they want, but for parties to compromise. He agreed there are many vital historical elements at the Union Station and he believes they will be properly protected according to standards dictated by the

column3: stated she is also worried about Union Station because she understands that local governments are not subject to adherin
column4: Sue Wilkerson stated she is also worried about Union Station because she understands that local governments are not subject to adhering to requirements of the Historic Register; she urged the Council to pay close attention to what happens at Union Station and the surrounding property. She then noted that a more immediate concern relates to the potential for flooding in Ogden City; temperatures are forecasted to be 80 degrees tomorrow, but she has noticed that sandbags have not been placed along areas of the Ogden River where the flood risk is high. She believes the weeks ahead will be very difficult and she does not believe the City is prepared. She has already had two of her rental property’s basements flooded with ground water and she believes conditions will worsen. ; Chair Choberka inquired as to the Landmarks Commission’s involvement with the historic preservation of the Union Station. Ms. Wilkerson stated that the Commission is involved in the preservation of the grand lobby on the building’s interior, but no other interior area of the building. She noted the Landmarks Commission is involved with preservation of the exterior of the building. However, the Landmarks Commission has not been heavily involved since the property and building were acquired by the City from the Union Station railroad. Angel Castillo congratulated Chief Young for being recognized for his service and support to the Ogden community. She also congratulated the Weber State University (WSU) Cheer Team for being named Grand National Champion for six years running. She then referenced comments about intentionality and historic preservation parameters for Union Station; while the City has communicated good intentions, if those intentions are not clearly communicated in writing, they will not always be enforced. \ She stated Union Station is the heart and soul of Ogden City and the City must be very careful in how they deal with it; she ! reiterated she is not opposed to density downtown or new commercial development to improve the City’s tax base, but the City , must be intentional and clear, and those intentions must be communicated in black and white, so they are understood. She asked the Council to take the next steps slowly and be clear about how Union Station will be protected and what types of businesses and development will be allowed around it.

column3: discussed the historical elements at the Union Station that have not been modified and should be protected; the claim th
column4: Teresa Holmes discussed the historical elements at the Union Station that have not been modified and should be protected; the claim that the wings of the Station have been modified to the point that they can no longer be protected as a historical feature is ‘crap’. She wished she had been given the opportunity to give the Council the tour of Union Station because she has worked at the Station for over 21 years and is familiar with the entire building. However, she has been pushed out of the Station to allow developers to take it over. She loves Ogden and Union Station and is disgusted with the actions that have been taken that will harm Union Station and the history of the surrounding property; it is not true that the only part of the Station that is original is the grand lobby. She declared that comment to be an outright lie. :

column4: Angel Castillo stated she is attending an education summit in San Diego, California and she appreciates the ability to participate in the Council’s meeting remotely. She thanked Chief Mathieu for his leadership; his debrief was stellar and the fact that he accepted responsibility for what occurred in recent flooding events is the true example of leadership. However, she has raised the issue of flooding with Chief Administrative Officer Johnson and there should have been planning underway for catastrophic flooding events; the snowpack is historic, and the City should have been aware of the risks that created for the : community. She stated the citizenry is fully devoted and connected to ensure response to flooding, but City Administration should have started working to prepare at least a month ago. She concluded that the response of Chief Mathieu and his Department reinforces her belief that public safety employees should be better compensated for their service.

column3: stated that during the last RDA meeting he spoke about a developer interested in the 550 24" Street project, who present
column4: Heath Satow stated that during the last RDA meeting he spoke about a developer interested in the 550 24" Street project, who presented ideas to the current Community and Economic Development Director prior to the formal request for qualifications (RFQ) publication. The developer was personally assured they would be contacted by the City when an RFQ was released, but that never occurred. There may be no legal requirement to obtain as many quality proposals as possible, but this rises to the level of nonfeasance and should be unacceptable to every member of the Council. No one has reached out to him about this issue, particularly the four Council members who voted in support of the development. Developers are being actively discouraged from trying to invest in Ogden; they have learned it is wiser to invest in other cities unless they have an inside track in Ogden. He does not know what it will take to bring about actual functional change to the process in Ogden. He is not opposed to growth and development in the City, but he would like the elected officials to start looking closer at these deals. He then stated he must address what occurred in the meeting room tonight before the meeting started; Community and Economic Development Director Cooper walked up behind him, slapped him on the shoulder, and said “I can’t wait to hear what you are here to lie about today.” He stated he did not respond, but he knows at least one elected official heard it. He understands the concerns he is drawing attention to may be unwelcome and it is fine if someone disagrees with him, but one thing he is not is a liar. Carolyn Lietuvininkas referenced Ms. Bramwell’s comments about eminent domain; it is interesting that the Utah Law is specific about how property can be taken for public good. The law states that private property shall not be taken or damaged for public use without just compensation. Additionally, no person shall be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law. The fact that Ms. Bramwell is still complaining about her property suggests that the policies the City have adopted are designed to fatigue her into abandoning or selling her property, or the City confiscating it under eminent domain. That is shameful if that is the case. ‘The City may not like her or the use ofher property, but she has the right to be protected. In the grand scheme of RDA projects, the City does not have the right to steal property from her. Several Council members have met with citizens to TO ___________________—_____________—_" on discuss the doctrine of a lesser magistrate and she appreciates that; those who have not met with the citizens are simply avoiding 5 those conversations and that is being noted. She studies law and it will be very bad for the City when she starts ‘dropping : “ petitions’ on the Council and they are forced to answer for things that have gone on. Agenda 2021, agenda 2030, and agenda 2050 é are buzz words for globalizing the world and complete aggregating the United States Constitution and the Council does not have i the right to steal from future generations and they should think long and hard about the actions they are taking. Nothing should be approved if it violates the Constitution or God’s law.

column4: Sebastian Benitez stated he is the service coordinator for the LDS Church in his neighborhood and his area of the City is ready to respond when needed in future flooding events. He thanked City staff for communicating with him and providing important updates on how he can help. He stated he loves Ogden and is proud to live here. Teresa Bramwell echoed what Chief Mathieu said earlier; it is important to know what has happened to cause the flooding events in order to prepare for it happening again. Everyone is watching Ogden City and she cited news articles dating back to 2007 from outlets such as the New York Times, Desert News, Associated Press, KSL, and ABC News; the articles discuss matters such as outdoor recreation offerings, development, an urban gondola, and the use of imminent domain as part of Redevelopment Agency (RDA) projects.

column3: asked the Mayor, City Council, and City staff to consider what will happen if the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center is not
column4: Amy Wicks asked the Mayor, City Council, and City staff to consider what will happen if the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center is not given a reasonable lease extension to give them time to find a new home. The Center treats around 4,000 animals each year and the next closest treatment facility is located 90 minutes away and operated from a home. There is no other place for birds and other wildlife in the area to be treated and if the Center is forced to stop taking new patients, there will be detrimental effects. She stated she feels Mayor Caldwell wants to have this issue finished before he leaves office and seems determined to leave destruction in his wake, but that is not acceptable. She has not seen a Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) project brief for demolition of the building that houses the Center, and if there is no publicly allocated funding for the project, there should be no hurry. There is no harm in allowing the Center to stay in the building for more than just six months; they need sufficient time to find or build a new facility. She stated that the Mayor has never been personally involved in discussions with the Center and has only directed his staff to handle it; she suggested he stand up for his decision or give the Center more time.

column3: stated that some rituals are positive and healthy, but she has a ritual with the City Council that occurs each year when
column4: Angel Castillo stated that some rituals are positive and healthy, but she has a ritual with the City Council that occurs each year when the annual budget is presented to the body, wherein she stands before them pleading for more money for first responders and increased staffing levels. Every year since 2018 she has stood before the Council to ask them to prioritize public safety and in tonight’s work session the first responders stood before the Council asking for the same thing. They have been asked to ‘hang on’ for years and now is the time to prioritize public safety. Everything else in the City is just a ‘decoration’, but public safety is a vital necessity. She would love to end this ritual and not come before the Council next year asking for the same thing.

column3: noted police quotas have been banned in Utah since 2018, but the Ogden Police Department (OPD) has found a way to write
column4: Malik Dayo noted police quotas have been banned in Utah since 2018, but the Ogden Police Department (OPD) has found a way to write more tickets; Fox 13 News interviewed seven current and former OPD Officers who were too afraid to identify themselves and appear on camera and they each shared stories of their supervisor pressuring them to write more tickets. Officers, lawmakers, and drivers feel the OPD is acting against the spirit of the State law, or even breaking the law. Officers have said they were made to feel their job is more about raising revenue than public safety.
