column4: Doug Stephens stated he graduated from WSU in 1972. He then referenced the agenda item to appoint a new Public Services Director. He stated that Justin Anderson will do a great job in that role, but he chose to attend tonight’s meeting to publicly thank and acknowledge former Director Jay Lowder for his service to the community. He has influenced so many special events and areas of the City and his dedication to Ogden City is evident. He stated he is a great individual and Ogden City is better , because of him. Consideration of the appointment of Justin Anderson as Public Services Director for Ogden City A letter from Mayor Caldwell requesting consideration of the appointment of Justin Anderson as the Ogden City Public Services Director for Ogden City came before the Council for consideration. Mayor Caldwell first thanked former Public Services Director Lowder for his leadership and commitment to the City; he then noted that he has recommended the appointment of Mr. Anderson to replace Mr. Lowder. Mr. Anderson is also very committed to the City and his Department and has been outstanding in his representation of Ogden City. He asked for the Council’s advice and consent regarding the proposed appointment. Council member Nadolski also thanked Mr. Lowder for his service to the Ogden community. He then stated that he is supportive of the appointment of Mr. Anderson, who has already done a great deal of ‘heavy lifting’ for the Ogden community. He thanked Mayor Caldwell for asking for his input before recommending the appointment of Mr. Anderson. COUNCIL MEMBER HYER MOVED TO APPROVE THE APPOINTMENT OF JUSTIN ANDERSON AS THE OGDEN CITY PUBLIC SERVICES DIRECTOR. MOTION WAS SECONDED BY COUNCIL MEMBER WHITE, ALL VOTING AYE. \ Mr. Anderson stated he is grateful for his opportunity; he is incredibly blessed with a supportive wife and children. They _.’ understand his commitment to serving Ogden City and they have been very supportive and understanding of his sacrifices. He thanked several Council members for their support of himself and the Public Services Department throughout many different projects they have completed in the City. He also thanked Mayor Caldwell for his support, friendship, and leadership; he has always put employees first during his tenure and he thanked him for his trust and kindness. He then noted that tonight, the Council nnn nnn nese Chambers is full of some of the finest individuals; they are Ogden City employees who love working in and for this community and he thanked them. He especially thanked Mr. Lowder. He has never worked with someone who has pushed him so hard to ro) make sure things are done correctly — even perfectly. He noted Mr. Lowder has put his heart into this community for 38 years and his love for the community is evident. He thanked Mr. Lowder for his honest feedback and support. Consideration of the appointment of Taylor Nielsen as City Engineer for Ogden City A letter from Mayor Caldwell requesting consideration of the appointment of Taylor Nielsen as the Ogden City Engineer came before the Council for consideration. Mayor Caldwell stated that Mr. Nielsen is an employee who he considers a ‘silent warrior’ for Ogden City; he is always able to reasonably assess a problem and find a solution. He has a great combination of skillsets that serve the community in a tremendous fashion, and he is honored to recommend him for appointment to the position of City Engineer. Council member Nadolski stated that Mr. Lowder put in place a great succession plan for his Department, which makes it easy to choose people for these types of positions in the Public Services Department. He commented on his relationship with Mr. Nielsen through their participation in youth sports in the community and noted he is confident Mr. Nielsen is the right person for this position. He again thanked Mayor Caldwell for asking for his input on this recommendation before presenting it to the Council. COUNCIL MEMBER HYER MOVED TO APPROVE THE APPOINTMENT OF TAYLOR NIELSEN AS THE OGDEN CITY ENGINEER. MOTION WAS SECONDED BY COUNCIL MEMBER LOPEZ, ALL VOTING AYE.

column3: noted he has signed an affidavit affirming that the court is in compliance with all statutory requirements and minimum s
column4: Judge Stucki noted he has signed an affidavit affirming that the court is in compliance with all statutory requirements and minimum standards established by the Judicial Council, and he asked for the Council’s adoption of the proposed resolution requesting recertification of the Justice Court. Council member Lopez stated that he has attended a few sessions at the Ogden City Justice Court and was proud of the way the Court staff and Judge Stucki treated those who had been required to attend court. Chair Choberka introduced in writing proposed Resolution 2023-23, entitled: “A resolution of the Ogden City Council requesting the recertification of the Ogden City Justice Court.” COUNCIL MEMBER LOPEZ MOVED THE RESOLUTION BE ADOPTED, AND THE CHAIR BE AUTHORIZED TO SIGN THE SAME. MOTION WAS SECONDED BY VICE CHAIR RICHEY, WITH THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE: VOTING AYE —- COUNCIL MEMBERS BLAIR, HYER, LOPEZ, NADOLSKI, RICHEY, WHITE, VICE CHAIR RICHEY, AND CHAIR CHOBERKA. VOTING NO — NONE.

column3: stated that the renewal of the College Town Initiative was wonderful because it brought everyone together. There are so
column4: Linda Sanchez stated that the renewal of the College Town Initiative was wonderful because it brought everyone together. There are so many offerings at the school, and she appreciates having access to them. She then noted that she listened to tonight’s work session and the discussion of snow removal policies; she is appreciative of the Council for conducing a survey regarding the matter and for taking additional time to analyze the matter before voting on any changes. She acknowledged that all residents need safety and security during the winter months, but the City should not adopt policies that will be detrimental to some. : Angel Castillo stated she also appreciates the Council’s consideration of community input relative to snow removal policies; the Council needs to make a concerted effort to meet people where they are in order to understand how a change will impact everyone and not just those who had the time and opportunity to respond to the survey. She then noted that this morning, the Weber County Housing Authority won an Agency of the Year award, and she is proud of the work they are doing in the community. She is also proud of the Council for having conversations about housing affordability and appropriate housing policies for the Ogden community.

column3: thanked the Mayor and Council for their support. He also thanked Mr. Anderson for his support and serving as an example
column4: Mr. Nielsen thanked the Mayor and Council for their support. He also thanked Mr. Anderson for his support and serving as an example to him. He added Mr. Lowder has also been a great mentor and exceptional leader and he has learned so much under the two of them and due to the way they structured the Department. He also thanked his wife and family for their endless support. He stated that Mayor Caldwell has also led the City so well; he has created an environment and culture that has caused great employees to desire to stay in Ogden. He stated that what makes his job so great is the wonderful people he gets to work with; he acknowledged the City employees present tonight to support himself and Mr. Andreson in their appointments and noted that he looks forward to working alongside them on many projects in the future. Proposed Resolution 2023-23 requesting the recertification of the Ogden City Justice Court bo A memo from the Management Services Department came before the Council to consider a resolution requesting the recertification of the Ogden City Justice Court. The memo stated Justice Courts must be certified by the State Justice Courts Standards Committee and the Judicial Council every four years. The Administrativé Office of the Courts must receive a request for certification no later than December 15, 2024. Justice Court Administrator Richardson summarized the memo and stated Administration is requesting the Council adopt a resolution asking the State Justice Courts Standards Committee and the Judicial Council recertify the Ogden City Justice Court and affirming the City’s willingness to continue to meet all requirements necessary to continue operations. The City wrote an Opinion Letter outlining the operational procedures of the Court and the feasibility of continuing operations as required by law.

column3: stated she graduated from WSU, and she is excited about the Coalition. She noted she owns a property : along the Bus Rap
column4: Teresa Bramwell stated she graduated from WSU, and she is excited about the Coalition. She noted she owns a property : along the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) route that WSU was instrumental in bringing it to the community; she rode it to tonight’s meeting, and it was full of people that did not look like college students. She would love to have a conversation with some people in attendance tonight to see what can be done to make the Ogden community better because she feels it has deteriorated over the past 20 years.

column3: stated he grew up next to the original Weber State University (WSU) campus and he is also grateful to the school for the
column4: Travis Pate stated he grew up next to the original Weber State University (WSU) campus and he is also grateful to the school for their contributions to the community. He added that Walt Masaka’s hundredth birthday is next week, and he isa WSU alum.

column3: expressed her gratitude to Mayor Caldwell and his Administration for his service; she acknowledged the growth and improv
column4: Angel Castillo expressed her gratitude to Mayor Caldwell and his Administration for his service; she acknowledged the growth and improvements that have occurred in the City during his tenure and thanked him for always being a champion for City ; employees. Her relentless pursuit for housing solutions, homelessness reduction, and responsible use of taxpayer resources and the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) was always driven by her deep love for Ogden, and she may have been the ‘teacher that was particularly hard on a student that she knows can be excellent’. It is important to hold a vision for the City to not be just amazing, but to be the best in class; the current Administration has laid a strong foundation for this vision, and she looks forward to a future steeped in shared values and community first thinking. She noted Mayor-elect Nadolski’s commitment to the community and legislative expertise promise a bright future for Ogden. His focus on putting kids and people first resonates deeply with her and she is excited to see how his leadership will guide Ogden to new heights. She sees a horizon filled with hope for Ogden; a hope that the current Administration nurtured and one that Mayor-elect Nadolski will foster. She asked all to unite in their efforts to make Ogden a city that lives up to its incredible potential. She stated that the dedication of Mayor Caldwell and Mayor-elect . Nadolski is a beacon of inspiration and it is her hope that the Council, incoming Administration, and the community will stand ) together committed to Ogden’s journey; respecting its past and embracing its future with the grace and determination of diplomats. :

column3: thanked Council members Lopez and Nadolski for their service to the community. He thanked them for being open and availa
column4: Heath Satow thanked Council members Lopez and Nadolski for their service to the community. He thanked them for being open and available and for spending hours of their time listening to his and others’ concerns. He also acknowledged their ability to receive constructive criticism in an honorable way without ever making excuses. It takes a principled person to carry oneself in the manner they have. He looks forward to what Council member Lopez will continue to do in the community and to Council member Nadolski’s leadership in the coming years as the City’s Mayor. He addressed Mayor Caldwell and stated that the criticisms he has made over the years were about strong differences of opinion and not about him as a person. He wished him the best of luck and success in whatever he chooses to do in the future.

column3: thanked Council members Lopez and Nadolski and noted she feels they have ‘gone above and beyond’ : to support the people
column4: Teresa Bramwell thanked Council members Lopez and Nadolski and noted she feels they have ‘gone above and beyond’ : to support the people of Ogden. When she heard they were both leaving the City Council at the end of the year, she felt anxiety based upon her feelings that they are the two Council members that support the people the most. She is excited that Council member Nadolski will be moving into the position of Mayor, and she is excited to see what he accomplishes. She is sure he will be a fantastic leader for Ogden, and she looks forward to positive changes. She also thanked Mayor Caldwell for his service.

column3: stated she was excited to hear from the visitors from Hof, Germany as her family is from Bavaria. She then echoed Ms. Sa
column4: Adrienne Zubiller stated she was excited to hear from the visitors from Hof, Germany as her family is from Bavaria. She then echoed Ms. Sanchez’s recommendation regarding public hearings; residents are disappointed when the Council does not listen to the input provided during a public hearing. They are insulted when the Council takes action on a matter immediately after a public hearing is closed and the action is contrary to the input provided by the public. She stated she worked for the federal government and would be happy to consult the Council on their policies surrounding public hearings.

column3: thanked the Council for hearing from Wynter Storm at the beginning of the meeting. She thanked Mayor Nadolski for attend
column4: Angel Castillo thanked the Council for hearing from Wynter Storm at the beginning of the meeting. She thanked Mayor Nadolski for attending the Martin Luther King, Jr. Day celebration events and noted that City Administration has not been represented in those events in the past. She offered a ‘shout out’ to the City’s Public Works Department due to their response to the recent winter storm events; they have cleared the City’s streets of snow in a quick and efficient manner, but she suggested the City look into purchasing equipment to be added to plow blades that will prevent snow from being stacked in driveways. She noted she would be interested in learning if there were any challenges in enforcing the recently adopted ordinance regarding on- street parking during winter months. She would also like an update on the status of the lawsuit dealing with Ogden Airport hangars and the extension of the contract with the Northern Utah Wildlife Rehabilitation Center. Council member Hyer addressed the comments regarding the Council’s public hearing procedures. He stated it is his hope that people do not wait until a public hearing to provide their thoughts; the Council accepts public comments at every meeting or via email at any time. A public hearing is a statutory requirement, but it is not the first opportunity for public input. He added, however, that he is not opposed to a policy change that would delay action on an item until a later date following a public hearing. Council Executive Director Eller-Smith noted that change has been made for Council actions required on the annual budget. Chair Choberka added that there have been instances where the Council has delayed action on an item due to the input provided during a public hearing.

column3: stated she was impressed by the information provided by the Harvard students during tonight’s work session. She then off
column4: Linda Sanchez stated she was impressed by the information provided by the Harvard students during tonight’s work session. She then offered a suggestion to the Council regarding their public hearing procedures; she suggested that an action not be taken on an item on the same night that the public hearing is held, but instead that multiple public hearings be held or that action be scheduled for a later date following a public hearing. She then reported the water coming from the water fountain outside of Council Chambers is white and milky.

column3: discussed his history at the Ogden Airport as a hangar owner; all improvements he has made have been done with approval
column4: David Carlson discussed his history at the Ogden Airport as a hangar owner; all improvements he has made have been done with approval of the Airport Manager, but in March of 2022, he learned that he would be shut down and his lease would be terminated in November of 2022. He has been trying to communicate with the City since that time with no success, but he has paid improper invoices for outstanding fees. He received a call today from someone from Breeze Airlines who asked for his help with maintenance and repair of the ground equipment at the Airport and he had to inform the individual that he has been shut down by the Ogden City Attorney and the Ogden Airport Manager.

column3: spoke to his desire for improved transparency and suggested the City’s website be updated and improved. He also expresse
column4: David Timmerman spoke to his desire for improved transparency and suggested the City’s website be updated and improved. He also expressed his concern about the ‘looming eviction’ of the Northern Utah Wildlife Rehabilitation Center (NUWRC); it is his understanding that the NUWRC is facing penalties if they are not completely out of the building by March 7, but he would like to know why the deadline is so important and what the penalties are. He also still does not understand why the NUWRC is being evicted and what project will be completed once the Center is closed. He concluded by offering comparisons between the eviction of the NUWRC and the development of the MAKE Ogden Plan; he suggested that the City spend as much time on other projects and services as they have on the NUWRC and the MAKE Ogden Plan.

column3: addressed new information regarding the Brown Ice Cream building, which is in a far worse state of blight than it was tw
column4: Heath Satow addressed new information regarding the Brown Ice Cream building, which is in a far worse state of blight than it was two years ago. He cited statements he made in the past regarding the manner in which the value of the building was determined and how it was marketed for sale; he also expressed concern about the actions of City staff in recommending the sale of the building to the developer selected by City Administration. He concluded the broker that created the lowered valuation of the building now owns the building under a newly created LLC name; he is hopeful that with a new Director of the Community and Economic Development the City will not be party to such ‘shady dealings’ and he asked the City Attorney to consider whether the new property owner will be held to the original contractual deadline of November 2024 for renovations to be completed. The argument provided by City Administration in the past regarding the lowered valuation of the building was to expedite the removal of blight, but it has been 27 months and blight is only becoming worse. He hopes the City Council and Mayor will work together to instill policy that will prevent something like this from happening in the future. Angel Castillo congratulated Chair Richey and Vice Chair White for their election to the leadership roles. She also commented on her appreciation for the discussion during tonight’s work session regarding the Mayor’s efforts to work with the State Legislature on many matters. She then addressed the Council’s discussion of the group dwelling ordinance during the January 23, 2024, work session; she is pleased that smaller lots will be allowed, but she is concerned about the minimum dwelling size of 2,500 square feet. This will result in the construction of $500,000 homes, which are not affordable by the ‘missing middle’. She suggested the minimum unit sizes be reduced to make them more affordable, especially on smaller building lots. She then stated she is also concerned about the NUWRC and the lack of plans for the reuse of the land on which the Center is currently located. Adrianne Zubler also asked questions about the NUWRC; she thought the matter had been resolved months ago and she does not understand what has changed. She inquired as to the differences between the Dinosaur Park and the NUWRC; improvements that will be completed on the NUWRC land; why the Dinsoaur Park is given preference over the NUWRC; and why dead animals are more important than live animals.

column3: discussed outstanding issues with standing water on 1200 West, the road west of Business Depot Ogden on the Marriott-Sla
column4: Kerry Wayne discussed outstanding issues with standing water on 1200 West, the road west of Business Depot Ogden on the Marriott-Slaterville border. He also encouraged the Mayor and City Council to reconsider the eviction of the NUWRC. He added that City Attorney Williams was the City Attorney under former Mayor, Mike Caldwell, and he suggested that Mayor Nadolski consider terminating his employment; many of the bad decisions that were made in the past that have caused harm to residents and business owners have had the support of the City Attorney’s office.

column3: thanked former Chair Choberka for always being responsive to the residents of Ogden. She welcomed newly elected Council
column4: Linda Sanchez thanked former Chair Choberka for always being responsive to the residents of Ogden. She welcomed newly elected Council members as well. She reminded the elected officials of the City of their role and to always consider if actions they are taking are constitutional. She then discussed recent actions taken by the Weber County Commission that deal with water preservation and development in unincorporated areas of the County and suggested the City Council consider similar measures. She thanked Council member Myers for the questions he asked during tonight’s work session meeting. She also addressed matters of equality in the 2023 Utah Legislative Session. Teresa Bramwell also thanked former Chair Choberka for her kindness and responsiveness to residents. She then discussed the definition of the real estate term “highest and best use” and asked everyone to consider who the term should apply to. She believes that it should apply to the owner of a property, who should be able to realize the highest and best use of their property and receive commensurate value. When the government uses the term, that means that politicians get to decide a property’s highest and best use.

column3: commented on the success of recent special events in the community and thanked the Mayor and City Council for participat
column4: Travis Pate commented on the success of recent special events in the community and thanked the Mayor and City Council for participating in those events; he is concerned about preserving the history of the community and he encouraged the Council and Mayor to enlist residents in those efforts, especially throughout 2024 when there will be many celebrations related to the Union Station.

column3: expressed her pleasure with the City’s acknowledgement and recognition of Pastor Petty.
column4: Adrienne Zubiller expressed her pleasure with the City’s acknowledgement and recognition of Pastor Petty.

column3: thanked Pastor Petty for the work he has done in the Ogden community, and she thanked the Executive Director and Board f
column4: Angel Castillo thanked Pastor Petty for the work he has done in the Ogden community, and she thanked the Executive Director and Board for honoring him. She then noted that during the last City Council meeting she had a question about minimum unit sizes in the group dwelling ordinance. She asked that the City carefully consider the minimum square footage for a dwelling space in a group dwelling development. She then noted that she was thrilled to hear Board member Hyer ask about deed restrictions in tonight’s work session because she has been suggesting the City use that mechanism for many years to impose restrictions on certain types of developments where an applicant is asking for some sort of concession from the City. Executive Director Comments Executive Director Nadolski also thanked Pastor Petty for his contributions to the community; he also thanked the Board for participating in recognizing him. He then stated that he is working to get answers regarding the Brown Ice Cream building; Administration has reached out to the current owner to try to learn of his plans for the building and to determine if the obligations agreed to by the previous owner will be passed on to the new owner. He added that he is also trying to get updated information regarding the Northen Utah Wildlife Rehabilitation Center and will be providing an update to the Board soon regarding the timing of the Center’s relocation as well as the Dinosaur Park’s expansion plans. He then asked Chief Administrative Officer Brown to address Mr. Satow’s question about the Q Factor projects in the community. Ms. Brown stated the building on 25th Street has been secured to ensure the safety of the surrounding area. Relative to the Ogden Business Exchange project, they are likely in default and Administration is working to evaluate the City’s next steps. Board member Comments Board member Blair thanked Pastor Petty as well as the Diversity Commission for the valuable work they are doing in Ogden City. One of his favorite parts of being an elected official is being able to associate with so many great people that are working to impact the community they live in. He then noted he attended the groundbreaking ceremony for The Wonder Block project last Friday and it was very exciting, and he looks forward to the future of that project. Vice Chair White thanked Ms. Bramwell for elevating the matter of homeownership by women in the Ogden community. This is something that is very important to her, along with elevating women to leadership positions, and she is happy to be part of a government that values those issues. She noted that the City completed a study three years ago to evaluate whether women were being paid equally to their male counterparts and the results of that study were positive; however, it may be time to conduct a similar study again in the near future. There being no further business to come before the Agency, BOARD MEMBER MYERS MOVED THE MEETING

column3: thanked Board member Blair for raising the question regarding the Brown Ice Cream Building in tonight’s work session, bu
column4: Heath Satow thanked Board member Blair for raising the question regarding the Brown Ice Cream Building in tonight’s work session, but it appears that there will not be an answer provided tonight. He also referenced a question he asked a few weeks ago regarding the projects underway in the City being managed by Q Factor and he asked Administration to provide an answer to that question as well.

column3: addressed Vice Chair White, noting that she voted for her in her last campaign for office in Ogden City; she voted for h
column4: Teresa Bramwell addressed Vice Chair White, noting that she voted for her in her last campaign for office in Ogden City; she voted for her because she was not originally from Ogden, she is a woman, and she seems very educated and informed on the issues facing Ogden City. She felt Vice Chair White could make changes that would benefit women in Ogden City. She feels as though Ogden City has been in a ‘strangle hold’ for decades and some people are able to make money while others are not. Women are in the ‘not category’. She asked Vice Chair White to think about those things when she is voting on issues that come before her. This morning there was a story on Good Morning America regarding home ownership; in 2023, 19 percent of all homes were purchased by single women and only 10 percent were purchased by single men. Prior to 1974 a woman could not obtain a mortgage, but the current generation of women can own homes. Women are buying homes because they want stability in their lives, and they are willing to make financial sacrifices that allow them to afford a home. In East Central Ogden, the homeownership rate is just 40 percent, while the rate in Utah and Weber County is 70 percent.

column3: thanked the Council for their careful consideration of the Synchrony Bank line of credit during tonight’s work session m
column4: Angel Castillo thanked the Council for their careful consideration of the Synchrony Bank line of credit during tonight’s work session meeting; she indicated she is especially grateful for Council member Choberka’s questions about the City creating its own revolving loan fund for the purposes for which the line of credit is currently being used. She discussed training she has engaged in in recent months to learn more about these issues and suggested that City Administration look into those options further in order to begin to work to solve the housing problems in the Ogden community in advance of very important events that will be held in the State of Utah in the next 10 years. Travis Pate referenced recent land use training provided to the City Council and Planning Commission but noted that there is not enough focus on historic preservation and the training was not provided to City staff that is working on development processes in the community. He stated that the City needs to more carefully consider historic preservation, especially when considering the types of projects that have been acted upon during tonight’s City Council meeting. Overlay zoning that requires historic preservation of certain elements of a property should be required for projects like the zone change on Chester Street.

column3: asked if the City has answers to questions he has asked in recent meetings regarding the projects that are under the con
column4: Heath Satow asked if the City has answers to questions he has asked in recent meetings regarding the projects that are under the control of Q Factor in the Ogden community. He would also like follow-up information on the status of the Brown Ice Cream building.

column3: stated that as she was listening to tonight’s meeting, she noticed concerns being expressed by women; she indicated a wo
column4: Teresa Bramwell stated that as she was listening to tonight’s meeting, she noticed concerns being expressed by women; she indicated a woman referenced the petitioner for the Chester Street rezone also being a member of the Planning Commission. Another resident noted the fact that the previous owner of that property, who was a woman, was not allowed to build anything bigger than the current home. She indicated women expressed the concern about the amount of parking being made available to residents of the multi-family projects in the community. She then noted that it seems that a lot of men speak in Council meetings, and they are able to get things accomplished, but women are not given the same consideration. Linda Sanchez referenced the discussion during tonight’s work session regarding short term rentals; she has a family member who has used a short-term rental in the past in a time of need and she would have hated for her family member to have encountered problems with on-street parking due to concerns of residents. She hopes the Council does not enact laws based upon worst case scenarios and she encouraged them to consider laws that are family friendly. She then noted she drove by the property at 218 Chester Street, and she did not believe that it would accommodate 32 units or could be easily accessed by a fire truck. Chair Richey stated that public safety of the development on Chester Street will be carefully studied as the project moves through the subdivision application process.

column3: addressed the Council’s discussion during their work session regarding short-term rentals; she appreciates that the Coun
column4: Angel Castillo addressed the Council’s discussion during their work session regarding short-term rentals; she appreciates that the Council will discuss the matter in greater detail as she feels it is important for the Council to strike a balance between allowing short term rentals and long-term rentals. Permitted parking should be required for short-term rentals and she is happy to send the Council information about how other communities are regulating parking issues. Heath Satow cited the City’s use of Zoom for allowing electronic participation in open meetings and suggested that the City use the full-text transcription service offered by Zoom to make Council meetings searchable. This will increase overall transparency. He would also like to see a vote summary provided for each agenda item. He then asked for an update on the projects for which Q-Factor is involved with the City’s Redevelopment Agency (RDA). In a previous meeting he asked about the current value of the Browns Ice Cream building and if the current owner is bound by the terms agreed to by the previous owner. The City Attorney indicated that the current owner has expressed their commitment to abide by those terms, but that is not a legal requirement and asked if they can be held to the timelines of the project given the need to eliminate blight at the property.

column3: stated she was at her home on 25th Street and Monroe Boulevard recently and her neighbor directly behind her stopped by
column4: Teresa Bramwell stated she was at her home on 25th Street and Monroe Boulevard recently and her neighbor directly behind her stopped by and told her he is selling his home and moving, as are the neighboring property owners. This is because they learned of a nearby project that includes 160 low-income apartments; they are very concerned about crime in the neighborhood. She is concerned about this because these people own their homes and work in Ogden, and they expected an appreciation of their real estate holdings. She wondered if the Council’s intent behind approving the low-income apartments was to drive homeowners out of the area. She concluded she is very disturbed by the matter. Linda Sanchez referenced the recently spoken of goals to increase walkability in the community and to utilize rain barrels to reduce water consumption; she spoke of a city in the eastern United States who gave goats to all residents to take care of their yards. Not only do goats mow lawns, but they produce organic fertilizer.

column3: stated she is excited to hear about the progress of the Marshall N. White Center. She then referenced tonight’s work ses
column4: Angel Castillo stated she is excited to hear about the progress of the Marshall N. White Center. She then referenced tonight’s work session discussion of the proposed creation of a Flex Industrial Zone and noted the key point missing in the proposed ordinance is reference to clear span construction. This is important as the community is moving into an uncertain time relative to office space development. Flex space needs to be truly flexible to provide reuse opportunities to ensure it is not cheaper to demolish a building than to convert it to a different use. She is grateful the Council asked for more discussion of the matter and asked them to research market trends relative to office space development.

column3: stated that he does support the creation of the Flex Industrial Zone but found it ironic that the text explicitly prohib
column4: Heath Satow stated that he does support the creation of the Flex Industrial Zone but found it ironic that the text explicitly prohibits any smells detectable outside of the building while there is still a business present in Ogden City that regularly ‘stinks up’ the entire City. He then referenced the recent sale of the Brown Ice Cream Building to a realtor who misrepresented the size of the building by half; the realtor is a business partner of the person who purchased the building at an undervalued price. Six weeks ago, he started asking the Council about the legal responsibilities of the new owner and he has not received an answer. He read the statement he made during the last meeting regarding this matter and asked for an answer this evening. He reiterated the area is blighted and the whole reason for accelerating the sale of the building was to remove blight as quickly as possible. The reason this matters is because if the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) is making contracts with developers, he wants to ensure those contracts cannot be entirely overridden by selling a property to another party. Teresa Bramwell added to the comments made by Mr. Satow; she has reached out to the owner of the Brown Ice Cream Building who told her that he is not doing anything with the property until interest rates come down. He asked her if she has a suggestion for the reuse of the property, to which she answered no. The individual told her that he could not come up with any ideas of what to do with the building and if this is the case, she wonders why he owns it. She suspects he will sit on the property and sell it for a profit when possible. She then echoed Ms. Castillo’s comments about the value of a Flex Industrial zone; she would like a zone assigned to her property that would allow for different uses depending on market conditions. Her property is zoned neighborhood commercial, but the uses allowed in that zone are very limited and those who have been interested in opening a business in her building have been refused a business license by the City.

column3: addressed a few topics discussed during tonight’s work session meeting; she is supportive of historic preservation throu
column4: Angel Castillo addressed a few topics discussed during tonight’s work session meeting; she is supportive of historic preservation throughout the community and asked that the Council support initiatives that will help to facilitate preservation. She also addressed the topic of painting brick and suggested that the City look into allowing specific masonry paint that does not damage the brick and does last for decades. She noted that if the Council chooses to proceed with adoption of an ordinance prohibiting brick painting, it will be necessary to communicate with the realtors association in the area in order for them to communicate the law to potential home buyers in the Ogden community. She also encouraged the Council to provide tools to the City’s Code Enforcement Division, such as a geolocation application, to help them do their job in a more efficient and effective manner. Heath Satow also referenced items from tonight’s work session; one Council member had asked about the use of earned interest on the Marshall White Center (MWC) bond and the answer provided by Administration was that it would be added to the construction budget for the project. He asked if that means that the City is increasing the amount to be paid to the contractor or if it will allow for a broader project scope. Chief Administrative Officer Brown indicated she will look into Mr. Satow’s question to ensure she provides an accurate answer.

column3: stated she is also disturbed by the Council’s adoption of the flag ordinance; she supports Council member Choberka and V
column4: Angel Castillo stated she is also disturbed by the Council’s adoption of the flag ordinance; she supports Council member Choberka and Vice Chair White in their opposition to the ordinance and she wished the Council had not adopted it. She referenced a discussion during tonight’s work session regarding the design of property at 144 25th Street; she noted Council member Graf expressed concerns regarding building height and massing and she shares those concerns. Also, generally speaking, when a permit expires, the permittee must reapply and if codes have changed since the original approval of the permit, the new code should be imposed on the applicant. She suggested adjusting the massing on the upper level to address concerns about the massing on the street level. She then referenced increase in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and noted that the City does not have an AI policy; she suggested the City consider a policy to help improve efficiency throughout the City. Chair Richey asked City Administration to respond to Mr. Satow’s question about documenting the voting record of Council members. City Recorder Hansen stated that the official minutes of all open meetings do include a record of Council votes; the results document published by Council staff following a meeting does not contain that same information and, rather, simply indicates the Council’s action on all agenda items. However, that document is not considered the official minutes of the meeting. Chair Richey asked if official minutes are posted on the City’s website once they are approved, to which Ms. Hansen answered yes.

column3: addressed the adoption of the ordinance regulating the flags that can be flown on City flag poles; he indicated this ado
column4: Heath Satow addressed the adoption of the ordinance regulating the flags that can be flown on City flag poles; he indicated this adoption was proposed to prevent anyone from flying the gay pride flag on a City flagpole and he is upset that the Council adopted it. He then noted in the past he raised a question about why the City does not publish the voting record of Council members on the action taken summary for each Council meeting, but no one responded to his question. He referenced the Open and Public Meetings Act, which indicates that written minutes of an open meeting shall include a record of each vote taken by the public body. He stated that he interprets that to mean that the City is not following Utah Code and that should be corrected. If he is wrong, he still believes it would make people feel better if they could easily look up a Council member’s voting record.

column3: stated she will continue to attend City Council meetings because she is very frustrated with the City; the City is her e
column4: Teresa Bramwell stated she will continue to attend City Council meetings because she is very frustrated with the City; the City is her enemy at this time and is not on her side and does not want her to succeed. Her most recent frustration relates to an interaction she had with the Building Services Division for an inquiry to locate a lifetime shed on her property. She was told she cannot do that until she spends $500 to plead her case to the Planning Commission to tell them why she needs to put a temporary shed on her property for storage purposes. For some reason, the zoning of her property prohibits anything other than a church or beauty salon. Her property has always been used for residential purposes and it is not appropriate to ban accessory storage units. She is unsure of the point of the zoning other than to upset residents and property owners. She wished everything were easier in Ogden, but that has not been the case in her experience.

column3: commented on Mayor Nadolski’s presentation regarding his first 100 days in office and his goals for the future. He asked
column4: Al Jones commented on Mayor Nadolski’s presentation regarding his first 100 days in office and his goals for the future. He asked that the City focus on sustainable and planned growth rather than growth for the sake of growth. He then noted he walks around Ogden on a regular basis, and he has noticed several sections of sidewalk that are in deplorable condition; he asked that the City work to allocate sufficient funding in the budget to fix these problems. Mr. Jones also has noticed that the amount of garbage on City streets and sidewalks has increased dramatically; at one time, there were garbage cans conveniently located across the City and he was able to pick up trash and discard it in those cans, but those cans have been removed so he no longer collects trash. Now he only picks up aluminum cans and on a 10-block walk today, he collected 40 cans. The highest number of cans he has collected in a similar distance is 74 and that is absolutely deplorable.

column3: stated she listened to tonight’s work session meeting and was grateful to learn that there is a group working on the R2-
column4: Angel Castillo stated she listened to tonight’s work session meeting and was grateful to learn that there is a group working on the R2-S zone of the City. She stated that she has not recommended conditional overlay zoning be used as a form of deed restrictions on these projects; rather, she has suggested the City engage in a quid pro quo with a developer and grant spot zoning in exchange for deed restrictions. The City should not be giving away land that could otherwise be used for affordable residential growth. Ms. Castillo stated she is certified in the field of community land trusts and has access to a network of experts in other communities that could advise her on what things have worked to create a lasting impact relative to housing opportunities. She offered her expertise to the City Council and encouraged them to pursue the community land trust model.

column3: reiterated sentiments he has expressed in the past regarding the needed reform of Redevelopment Agency policies. He stat
column4: Heath Satow reiterated sentiments he has expressed in the past regarding the needed reform of Redevelopment Agency policies. He stated that last week he was told that Council voting records are publicly available, but when looking for those records on the City’s website he encountered difficulty. He asked that simplified voting records be posted in an easily accessible location.

column3: addressed the concept of a police citation quota and encouraged Mayor Nadolski to take this issue into consideration as
column4: Malik Dayo addressed the concept of a police citation quota and encouraged Mayor Nadolski to take this issue into consideration as he continues to work to improve the Ogden community. He noted he understands there is legislation being considered at the state level that would make ticket quotas illegal and he asked the Mayor if he is going to wait to learn the outcome of that legislation or if he will do the right thing and eliminate the quota being imposed by the Ogden Police Department on its officers.

column3: stated that he was recently very disappointed in the City’s legislative branch due to the quickness and lack of thought
column4: Nathan Sutherland stated that he was recently very disappointed in the City’s legislative branch due to the quickness and lack of thought given to the public facing discussion for vital issues in the community, including the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center, the Union Station, and the Wonder Block project. He paid attention to those issues and did not see the same level of thought go into those matters that went into several of the items included on tonight’s agenda. This improvement makes him very excited. The Mayor has committed to elevating the role and importance of communications and community engagement and it appears that Mr. Johnson shares that goal. Mr. Sutherland truly hopes that change will come to fruition, especially when the City is considering spending tens of millions of dollars in the community. He asked that the Mayor and Council think about the ‘little man’ during their deliberations in the future.

column3: expressed his support for Mayor Nadolski and the City Council and stated he is excited about the future of the City unde
column4: Sebastian Benitez expressed his support for Mayor Nadolski and the City Council and stated he is excited about the future of the City under the current leadership. He also asked that City Administration look into the matter of a closed street near Weber State University that is impacting traffic circulation in that area. Bonnie Sass and Karyn Webster approached and provided the Mayor and Council with a letter regarding a request from Aspen Ridge Homeowners Association (HOA) pertaining to the City’s “Flip Your Strip” program; they would like the City to include HOA’s with townhomes in the program. Residents in multi-family projects are also interested in water conservation and would like access to the same financial incentives available to single-family homeowners for assistance in converting turf to xeriscape.

column3: stated a lot of great work has been done tonight, but he advised the Council to consider opening the General Plan and to
column4: Travis Pate stated a lot of great work has been done tonight, but he advised the Council to consider opening the General Plan and to study the existing General Plan and Community Plans to understand whether any project that is being proposed in the community conforms with those plans. Mr. Pate indicated the previous Administration employed deplorable actions and they were rubber-stamped by the City Council. The City has turned its back on its history rather than striving to learn from it.

column3: stated that she supports Mr. Pate’s suggestion for the Council to consider contradictory actions, specifically when it r
column4: Angel Castillo stated that she supports Mr. Pate’s suggestion for the Council to consider contradictory actions, specifically when it relates to historic preservation efforts in the community. She then commended the Mayor and Council for proceeding with bonding actions to fix water line issues in the community. She also referenced the discussion during tonight’s work session regarding short term rental regulations; she suspects there are options for tightening regulations that would make it easier for enforcement staff to address any nuisances related to parking or other matters.

column3: thanked Mayor Nadolski for his attendance at City Council meetings and for listening to residents in an effort to assist
column4: Teresa Bramwell thanked Mayor Nadolski for his attendance at City Council meetings and for listening to residents in an effort to assist them with their concerns. She also thanked the Council for their attention to the public. She apologized for her emotion in recent meetings after having a frustrating experience pertaining to a land use application for her property. She tried to obtain a permit for a shed on her property and she met Chris Tremea, Code Services Manager; he spoke to her about his knowledge of her property, and this caused her to research the zoning of her property. She found there are just 18 properties in the entire City that are zoned NC-1 in a City of 90,000. Five of those properties are vacant and just one is a home and that is hers. She is concerned that Mr. Tremea has her zoning ‘memorized’.

column3: stated that he recently visited with the City Council in a work session about his desires for historic preservation of a
column4: Travis Pate stated that he recently visited with the City Council in a work session about his desires for historic preservation of an area of the community; he also received a letter, but does not understand the current status of his application. He would like to visit with the Council or Council staff in a more meaningful way and to get clarification on the City’s current position. He indicated that many decisions made by the City Council are contradictory in nature and this should be carefully considered.

column3: stated she wished to voice concern about the Weber County inland port project; she noted it is not within Ogden City but
column4: Amy Wicks stated she wished to voice concern about the Weber County inland port project; she noted it is not within Ogden City but believes it can bring some negative consequences to the City if the current plan is pushed through. The project has grown from around 900 acres to over 9,000 acres with very little transparency and public input. She cited census data relating to the amount of farmland left in Weber County and noted that the proposed project will consume nearly 10 percent of that land. The development also involves a significant public subsidy and creates an uneven playing field by interfering with the free market by competing with warehouse and industrial spaces within Ogden City. The public perception of the project is concerning, and it is prudent to put the project on hold until serious questions and concerns can be addressed. She spoke about the impact that the project will have on sensitive wetland areas surrounding the project area and implored responsible parties to complete pertinent studies before proceeding with the project. She asked that the Council submit a request to the Weber County Commission to rescind approval of the project until these questions can be answered and until a robust publicly transparent process has taken place.

column3: asked that the Council continue to work on challenges created by short term rentals following the adoption of the ordina
column4: Angel Castillo asked that the Council continue to work on challenges created by short term rentals following the adoption of the ordinance intended to address nuisances at rental properties. She added that the FlashVote survey results should be considered when working to address the root issues with the short-term rental use.

column3: thanked the Council for the thoughtful manner in which they have conducted business over the past several months. She is
column4: Linda Sanchez thanked the Council for the thoughtful manner in which they have conducted business over the past several months. She is also proud of many of the initiatives included in Mayor Nadolski’s proposed budget. She thanked emergency response services in the community for aid they rendered to one of her coworkers recently. She noted she loves the recent efforts to bring the community together and she thanked everyone who is involved in those efforts.

column3: expressed her opinion that the practice of ‘gatekeeping’ is occurring in Ogden on a regular basis. She noted gatekeeping
column4: Teresa Bramwell expressed her opinion that the practice of ‘gatekeeping’ is occurring in Ogden on a regular basis. She noted gatekeeping is the ‘activity of controlling and usually limiting access to something’. She feels it has happened to her a lot in the City of Ogden, though it has not happened to her in any other place. She is a woman of the world and has lived in many places throughout the world; but she was born and raised in Ogden, and she does not have access to information that others do. In order for gatekeeping to occur, there must be a gatekeeper and she has been trying to find out who that is in Ogden government; she believes there are a few, but she knows who one of them definitely is. She had an interaction with this gatekeeper when she was calling Ogden Police Department about crime that was occurring at her property. Most Police Officers in Ogden are great, but one is not, and this is the one that has responded to her property; he brought a new recruit with him to her property, and she found it odd that he was new because he appeared to be fairly old. She had another interaction with this gatekeeper when her home was on fire; this person had moved from the Police Department to the Fire Department. Linda Sanchez referenced the currently underway annual budget development process in the City and cited discussion during tonight’s work session meeting about potential tax or fee increases that could impact residents. She encouraged the elected officials of the City to keep in mind the elderly population who usually do not even receive a one-percent increase in their income. A cost-of-living increase could put them at risk of deciding whether to buy food or medicine over paying their taxes. She added that she has not received a pay increase recently and she does not receive an increase every year. She is also concerned about the lack of an emergency fund in the City; the City must prepare for inevitable situations. Chair Richey stated that a one percent property tax increase is proposed; the information presented to the Board by Administration indicates that there has been a four-percent increase in wages in the area and a three percent inflation rate; the difference between those two is one percent and that is the basis for recommending a one percent tax increase. He added that the City does have a ‘rainy day fund’ and State law regulates the amount of money that can be held in that account each year. Chief

column3: stated he is disturbed to hear that the current Administration is not treating the residents of Marriott- Slaterville an
column4: Heath Satow stated he is disturbed to hear that the current Administration is not treating the residents of Marriott- Slaterville any better than the previous Administration did; the City is making a great deal of money from BDO and some of that should be used to make those residents whole. He then addressed the City’s budgetary process, citing a general fund increase of eight percent when compared to last year. He noted that this does not include any increase related to the large waterline project in Ogden Canyon. He has seen similar increases that outpace population growth, but he is not seeing significant efforts to reduce costs or redundancies. The Administration is making sure that all City employees are receiving pay increases to offset the impact of inflation, but residents are not receiving the same consideration. He urged the City to enlist an outside consultant to review the budget and determine if any budget reductions could be made.

column3: stated he lives on 1200 West in Marriott-Slaterville, which is often referred to as Ogden’s Waterfront, Boyer Beach, and
column4: Kerry Wayne stated he lives on 1200 West in Marriott-Slaterville, which is often referred to as Ogden’s Waterfront, Boyer Beach, and Mosquito Coast; he and his neighbors have been asking for over two years for the City to do something to address the water problems on 1200 West and today is the first day in eight months that there has not been standing water in the location. There was an article in the Standard-Examiner over a year ago in which former Chief Administrative Officer Johnson was quoted as saying that the problem was being fixed, but still nothing has been done. He has spoken with Mayor Nadolski about the issue, but Mayor Nadolski is not happy with him and has asked him to no longer contact his staff and to take all of his complaints to Marriott-Slaterville City. However, he has found that Ogden City is no longer communicating with Marriott- Slaterville and that is problematic. Marriott-Slaterville is planning to improve 1200 West with expansion to occur on the Business Depot Ogden (BDO) side of the road, so Ogden City needs to be involved. He is only asking that the City be understanding of what the residents on 1200 West have lived through. The Boyer Company created the problem, and the water will no longer drain in the area because incorrect materials were used; he will continue to call each time there is standing water and he implored all parties to work together.

column3: stated that she came to finish the story she started last week about ‘the gatekeeper’. She does not have a great deal of
column4: Teresa Bramwell stated that she came to finish the story she started last week about ‘the gatekeeper’. She does not have a great deal of experience with government, but she feels the way she has been treated by Ogden City is a violation of her constitutional rights. She cited the Fourth Amendment of the United States Constitution and noted that she feels a ‘gatekeeper’ in Ogden is keeping people from accomplishing anything with their property in order for others to come in and purchase the property and profit from it. The first experience she had with the gatekeeper was when he was employed by the Police Department; the second time, he came to her home as a representative of the Fire Department following a fire at her home. He entered her home and took her electric meter with him, and she has never been informed of how to retrieve it or what became of it. She then received a notice from the Code Services Division about the lack of a notice of vacancy on her home following the fire. She came to the City and found the gatekeeper was now the ‘boss’ of the Code Services Division.

column3: stated that she would love for the City Council to help her and other property owners in the vicinity of 25th Street and
column4: Teresa Bramwell stated that she would love for the City Council to help her and other property owners in the vicinity of 25th Street and Monroe Boulevard. She wants to make back some of the money she has lost due to her ownership of her property.

column3: stated that he has circulated a petition and gathered 61 signatures in his neighborhood; he read the long title of the p
column4: Wayne Richey stated that he has circulated a petition and gathered 61 signatures in his neighborhood; he read the long title of the petition, which related to requested road closure of Taylor Avenue via a gate on the south side of the Weber State University (WSU) campus. This is due to increased traffic in the area that has impacted the safety and quality of life on the street. He also noted that he sent a letter regarding the same subject matter to the Mayor’s Office a year ago and he read from that letter as well. He cited another street on the north side of the WSU campus that has already been closed using a gate and this has set a reasonable precedent for other residential streets surrounding the campus.

column3: stated that over the past several months there has been construction on Country Hills Drive, and it has created a signif
column4: Jake Oakey stated that over the past several months there has been construction on Country Hills Drive, and it has created a significant inconvenience for his neighborhood. He and many others have had to find other routes to get in and out of the area and he has noticed police vehicles parked at the old Jakes Over The Top restaurant in an effort to catch people that are driving past the ‘road closed’ sign and cite them. He stated he appreciates their efforts to enforce the law, but he suggested that they park in another area to remind people not to go through the construction area or even to help guide traffic. There is plenty of space for two lanes of traffic. Acting Chair White referenced Mr. Satow’s comments and stated it is her understanding that there will be a large-scale study similar to what was performed in the Prosecutor’s Office. She also referenced Ms. Bramwell’s comments and noted that the City has attempted to determine whether women are treated fairly and equitably in terms of compensation as a City employee.

column3: stated she lives on the portion of Taylor Avenue that connects Weber State University (WSU) to the Dee Events Center and
column4: Tara Oakey stated she lives on the portion of Taylor Avenue that connects Weber State University (WSU) to the Dee Events Center and her neighborhood has proposed a date for shutting down that section of the road to prevent traffic using that section of the road to get to WSU. They love and support WSU, but the traffic is causing safety concerns for the people who live there. She cited things that have been done on the street in an attempt to slow or reduce traffic, but none have worked. The neighborhood suggests installing a gate at the end of the street that can be opened when needed; something similar has been done on Birch Avenue and the same options should be made available to her neighborhood.

column3: wished everyone a happy Independece Day, which is about taxation with out representation. She acknowledged that Ogden Ci
column4: Teresa Bramwell wished everyone a happy Independece Day, which is about taxation with out representation. She acknowledged that Ogden City elected officials are representing her and she is grateful for their willingness to do so. She listened to tonight’s work session as well and she heard of a large increase in pay for public safety employees and most general employees that work for Ogden City. This causes her to believe there is a very big disconnect in Ogden City in terms of the services that are being provided and the people that are receiving those services. These are the taxpayers. The same people who were criminals ten years ago are still criminals today. The same people who were taxpayers ten years ago are still taxpayers today. Those groups of people have not changed. The Police Department and Prosecutor’s Office are charged with dealing with criminals, but there is talk of making these areas of the City self-sufficient. However, it is important to understand that the taxpayers will pay the taxes that will fund those areas of the City. The City is not learning from its past and functioning any better. Women are still victims in Ogden City and the ‘needle needs to move’.

column3: stated he has expressed concerns regarding the paid parking system, a matter that was discussed during tonight’s work se
column4: Heath Satow stated he has expressed concerns regarding the paid parking system, a matter that was discussed during tonight’s work session. He noted that staff has compared the City’s proposal with programs that have been employed in other cities, but he does not view those examples as ‘success stories’, nor convincing as justification for proceeding with the program in Ogden. He cited differences between Ogden and the other cities that were relied upon, including population disparities, access to free shuttles, and times of day that free parking is available in the downtown areas of those other cities.

column3: stated that there are often presentations given during the Council work session meetings and she asked that those presen
column4: Laura Lewis stated that there are often presentations given during the Council work session meetings and she asked that those presentations be made publicly available prior to the meeting so that the public can review them and be prepared with questions. She also cited the paid parking program and noted staff mentioned that businesses are supportive of the program and do not want people loitering in their business. She stated that she owned a small business for years and she wanted people to stay in her store because that meant they would spend more money. She also asked if each business as well as the general public were polled to determine the level of support for a paid parking program; it is likely that many residents will simply drive to other communities to shop in order to save the costs of paid parking. She echoed Ms. Sanchez’s comments about residents living on a fixed income; these individuals will receive a 2.6 percent cost of living adjustment (COLA) in their social security benefit, which is nearly nothing. That increase will be consumed by the City’s property tax increase and the paid parking program, and this will reduce the public’s standard of living. Steve Jones also expressed concerns about the paid parking program; he believes the program will drive people and businesses away from Ogden because there are other viable alternatives very close by that do not charge for parking. He encouraged the Council to carefully consider the impacts of their decisions; Ogden is not like the many other cities that were cited by staff, and he cautioned the Council against ruining what the City has. Chair Richey stated that no decisions have been made regarding the final details of the paid parking system, but actions have been taken in the past that have solidified the decision to implement some type of paid parking program in downtown Ogden. Many of the topics discussed during tonight’s work session are yet to be determined, such as a 15-minute free parking timeframe, scaling the program based upon demand for parking in downtown Ogden. Chief Administrative Officer Brown added that there will also be a free trolley service in downtown Ogden. The City is still receiving public feedback and will collaborate with Weber County to determine that the program benefits the entire community. Chair Richey then referenced Ms. Lewis’s question about the presentations that are made during work sessions; the meeting packet is posted the Thursday before the meeting, but the Council does not receive the presentation documents until the day of the meeting. Council staff briefly illustrated the steps to access meeting packets for each Council meeting. Ms. Lewis reiterated her suggestion that the presentations be made available before the meeting. Council staff emphasized that the Council does not even receive the presentations until the night of the meeting. Council member Graf added that action is not taken during work session meeting and there is time for the Council to continue to receive public comment on any matter that is discussed during a work session prior to action being taken.

column3: stated she recently had a great interaction with Anna Davidson; she is compassionate, non-judgmental, and is likely not
column4: Linda Sanchez stated she recently had a great interaction with Anna Davidson; she is compassionate, non-judgmental, and is likely not compensated enough for what she does for Ogden City, She then also referenced the Council’s discussion of the paid parking program during the work session. She stated that taxpayers have paid for the government buildings located in Ogden’s downtown and should not be required to pay to park near them. It is offensive to charge people to park and many people on fixed incomes will not be able to afford this additional expense. She stated that the City needs to make access to federal government buildings free. Taxes continue to increase in order to pay City employees more money, but the general public is not receiving a pay increase. She stated she is frugal with her money, and she advised the City to do the same.

column3: stated that she has had two issues at her home this week involving homeless individuals; these individuals have been cam
column4: Teresa Bramwell stated that she has had two issues at her home this week involving homeless individuals; these individuals have been camping on her property and she was able to speak to one of them and find out why he arrived on her front porch. This is not something that she can fix, but perhaps the City can fix it. She called 9-1-1 to report the homeless encampment on her front porch, but no one ever came to her property. While she was waiting for emergency responders, the individual who had been camping on her porch arrived and told her that he had been evicted from his residence; he told her that he had previously lived in the home where the Family Dollar is now located and he planned to call her to ask if he could place his belongings on her porch, but he could not find her phone number. She stated that she has ‘no trespassing’ signs along the front of her property, and she asked him if that deterred him from entering her property and placing items on her porch and he told her no and that he planned to call her. She told him that he did not have permission to have his belongings on her porch and that he needed to leave her property, so he proceeded to move to the Family Dollar property. She stated these are the kinds of things she is dealing with as a property owner, and she thought the City should be aware of it.

column3: stated that given the Council’s action to increase taxes and adopt a budget for Fiscal Year (FY) 2024- 2025, she does be
column4: Linda Sanchez stated that given the Council’s action to increase taxes and adopt a budget for Fiscal Year (FY) 2024- 2025, she does believe that the men and women of the Fire Department do need some help. In the Police Department, she would recommend improved de-escalation training for employees to make residents more comfortable calling for emergency support from a police officer. She recited the following quote: ‘Hard times create strong men. Strong men create good times. Good times create weak men. Weak men create hard times.’ She reminded everyone to learn from their own history to avoid being in hard times on a regular basis. She then stated she identifies as an over-taxed, under-represented, non-woke, pissed off American, but she has been impressed by the efforts of the City Council to help to represent all residents of the community. She stated the American flag is her flag and she will not apologize for that; it does not stand for skin color, religion, or sexual orientation, but it does stand for freedom. She referenced the Council’s conversation in tonight’s work session regarding diversity and indicated she hopes they will be careful not to divide people in the community. She then noted that the City’s approval of high-density housing projects in recent years were intended to reduce the tax burden of the community, but she has not seen that come to fruition. Pieder Beeli referenced the Council’s prioritization of Ogden City employees in the annual budget. He challenged that priority and indicated government does not generate wealth, but it extracts wealth from its citizens and the citizens and their pocketbooks should be the top priority for the City Council. It may be possible to parcel out some services performed by City employees to the private sector and see if prices can be reduced. He stated if City employees are unsatisfied, they can go to the private sector; he does not understand why the City performs so many functions and services that could be provided by a private company. Government is parasitic by nature, and he is displeased to hear about the Council’s prioritization of taking care of the parasitic personnel. Wealth generation is performed by service to others and self-sacrifice and government does not do either of those things.

column3: thanked the Mayor and Council for the hard work they have dedicated to developing a budget; he plans to be in attendance
column4: Steve Jones thanked the Mayor and Council for the hard work they have dedicated to developing a budget; he plans to be in attendance at future meetings on a regular basis to resume his dialogue with the Administration and Council regarding the Union Station. He referenced the “Save the Union Station” Facebook page, which includes a great deal of information regarding the Station and opportunities for improving the campus. He stated that Mayor Nadolski has spent a great deal of time examining the recommendations of those interested in the project and he feels it is time to proceed with action. Emily Beeli relayed a story about a family that purchased a home made of ‘hodge-podged’ materials; they sought to renovate the exterior of the home and learned that their options are extensively restricted based upon zoning of the home. All options available were very expensive and they were concerned about going into debt in order to proceed. She asked that the Council reconsider these zoning codes to increase options available to homeowners interested in improving the appearance and increasing the value of their home.

column3: stated that he approached the Council in June regarding a petition to close Taylor Avenue on the south side of Weber Sta
column4: Blaine Richey stated that he approached the Council in June regarding a petition to close Taylor Avenue on the south side of Weber State University (WSU). Since then, the City installed speed radar signs on both sides of the road, but it is his hope this is a short-term solution to calm traffic until a closure gate can be installed. He believes the signs will help in the short term but will become ineffective over time. Every road on the north side of the campus has been closed to through traffic and the same consideration should be given for roads on the south side. The Campus Master Plan references road closures on the south side of the campus, but the closure of Taylor Avenue has not been considered even though it has the capacity to benefit many more residents than other roads. Residents realize that WSU is a huge community partner, but the concerns of Ogden residents should not be dismissed as a result. He believes the University wants to keep the road open to provide connectivity to the Dee Events Center, but there are other options for connectivity. A traffic study should be conducted to determine the appropriate solutions for the area.

column3: stated she was pleased by Mr. Brierley’s presentation regarding the proposed amendments to the Ogden Bend Mixed Use Zone
column4: Emily Beeli stated she was pleased by Mr. Brierley’s presentation regarding the proposed amendments to the Ogden Bend Mixed Use Zone area; she is pleased by reduced restrictions for property owners in the community because residents should be free to do what they want with their homes and properties. She stated she has faced restrictions on her home and property, and it has been very costly and time consuming to try to deal with those restrictions. Acting Chair White invited Administration to respond to the comments about the requested closure of Taylor Avenue. Mayor Nadolski first addressed Mr. Jensen’s comments and advised him to meet with representatives of the Community and Economic Development Department to have his questions answered. He then addressed the comments regarding Taylor Avenue, noting the petition to close the street has not been acted upon and that the radar signs are temporary in nature. Efforts are underway to get the signs located in their permanent condition, but the City wanted to have something in place before school resumes. He stated he is not sure that the road closure will be the final action, but more work will be done in an effort to respond to the concerns of the residents. He then noted he agreed with Ms. Sanchez’s comments regarding the impact the American Flag had on the community over the course of the Pioneer Days celebration. He added he will need more specific information about Ms. Beeli’s concerns regarding restrictions on landowners in the community. Acting Chair White also addressed Ms. Sanchez’s comments and noted that each year, Council member Hyer does a good job of recognizing Constitution Day. She addressed Ms. Beeli’s comments as well and indicated that in addition to City Codes, the City is required to adhere to State and National Building Codes, and that could be contributing to some of the regulations that are concerning to residents.

column3: stated she was grateful for the large American flag flying over Washington Boulevard during Pioneer Days that brought pe
column4: Linda Sanchez stated she was grateful for the large American flag flying over Washington Boulevard during Pioneer Days that brought people together and encouraged hope and peace. She stated sometimes when she listens to Council meetings, she gets the feeling the founding fathers and the U.S. Constitution has been forgotten and the younger generation does not know about the history of the nation. She asked for a ceremonial item to be included on future agendas to provide some education about the Constitution.

column3: stated he was confused by the discussion of the proposed Ogden Bend Mixed-Use Zone text amendments; he owns property on
column4: Scott Jensen stated he was confused by the discussion of the proposed Ogden Bend Mixed-Use Zone text amendments; he owns property on 18th Street, and he is unsure how this will impact him. He is currently being harassed by Code Enforcement and feels they are overstepping their authority; instead of working with landowners, they are eager to cite and fine them.
